title: 奧賽羅
author: William Shakespeare 威廉·莎士比亞
description: 《Othello, the Moor of Venice》(約1603)。威尼斯摩爾族將軍奧賽羅同戴絲德夢娜私下成婚,旗官伊阿古因嫉妒同怨恨,設下陰謀令奧賽羅誤信妻子不貞,終釀成殺妻自盡嘅悲劇。全劇五幕十五場,每段對白標示說話者,英文原文對照廣東話/普通話翻譯。

chapters.title: Act I, Scene I — Venice. A Street 第一幕第一場:威尼斯街道

passages.original: Enter Roderigo and Iago.
passages.vernacular: [羅德利哥同伊阿古上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅德利哥和伊阿古上。]

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Tush, never tell me, I take it much unkindly That thou, Iago, who hast had my purse, As if the strings were thine, shouldst know of this.
passages.vernacular: 呸,唔好同我講,我覺得好唔友善,你,伊阿古,一直當我個錢包係你嘅咁用,竟然事先知道呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 呸,不要對我說,我覺得很不友善,你,伊阿古,一直當我的錢包是你的那樣用,竟然事先知道這件事。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: ’Sblood, but you will not hear me.
passages.vernacular: 天啊,你就係唔肯聽我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天啊,你就是不肯聽我說。

passages.original: If ever I did dream of such a matter, Abhor me.
passages.vernacular: 如果我曾夢想過咁嘅事,就憎我吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我曾夢想過這樣的事,就恨我吧。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Thou told’st me, thou didst hold him in thy hate.
passages.vernacular: 你話過你憎恨佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說過你恨他。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Despise me if I do not.
passages.vernacular: 如果我唔憎,就鄙視我吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我不恨,就鄙視我吧。

passages.original: Three great ones of the city, In personal suit to make me his lieutenant, Off-capp’d to him;
passages.vernacular: 城中三位顯要,親自請求為我爭取副官一職,向佢脫帽致敬;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 城中三位顯要,親自請求為我爭取副官一職,向他脫帽致敬;

passages.original: and by the faith of man, I know my price, I am worth no worse a place.
passages.vernacular: 憑人嘅信義,我知道自己嘅價值,我值得唔差過呢個職位。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑人的信義,我知道自己的價值,我值得不差過這個職位。

passages.original: But he, as loving his own pride and purposes, Evades them, with a bombast circumstance, Horribly stuff’d with epithets of war:
passages.vernacular: 但佢,只愛自己嘅驕傲同目的,用一番浮誇嘅託詞迴避,裡面塞滿可怕嘅戰爭字眼:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他,只愛自己的驕傲和目的,用一番浮誇的託詞迴避,裡面塞滿可怕的戰爭字眼:

passages.original: And in conclusion, Nonsuits my mediators: for “Certes,” says he, “I have already chose my officer.”
passages.vernacular: 最後駁回我嘅講客:因為「當然」,佢話,「我已選定我嘅軍官。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後駁回我的說客:因為「當然」,他說,「我已選定我的軍官。」

passages.original: And what was he?
passages.vernacular: 咁佢選咗誰?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那他選了誰?

passages.original: Forsooth, a great arithmetician, One Michael Cassio, a Florentine, A fellow almost damn’d in a fair wife, That never set a squadron in the field, Nor the division of a battle knows More than a spinster, unless the bookish theoric, Wherein the toged consuls can propose As masterly as he:
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,一位偉大嘅算術家,一個叫邁克爾·凱西奧嘅佛羅倫斯人,一個幾乎因為有個美麗妻子而被詛咒嘅傢伙,從未在戰場擺過一個中隊,對戰陣嘅布置所知唔比紡織女工多,除咗書本上嘅理論,嗰啲穿長袍嘅執政官一樣可以講得同佢一般高明:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,一位偉大的算術家,一個叫邁克爾·凱西奧的佛羅倫斯人,一個幾乎因為有個美麗妻子而被詛咒的傢伙,從未在戰場擺過一個中隊,對戰陣的布置所知不比紡織女工多,除了書本上的理論,那些穿長袍的執政官一樣可以說得和他一般高明:

passages.original: mere prattle without practice Is all his soldiership.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅軍事才能,不過係冇實踐嘅空談。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的軍事才能,不過是沒實踐的空談。

passages.original: But he, sir, had the election, And I, of whom his eyes had seen the proof At Rhodes, at Cyprus, and on other grounds, Christian and heathen, must be belee’d and calm’d By debitor and creditor, this counter-caster, He, in good time, must his lieutenant be, And I, God bless the mark, his Moorship’s ancient.
passages.vernacular: 但佢,先生,得到咗選任,而我,佢親眼見過我喺羅德島、塞浦路斯同其他基督教同異教地方嘅表現,卻要被呢個算帳先生擋住風,令我停滯不前,佢居然成為副官,而我,上帝保佑呢個標記,只係佢摩爾老爺嘅旗官。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他,先生,得到了選任,而我,他親眼見過我在羅德島、塞浦路斯和其他基督教和異教地方的表現,卻要被這個算帳先生擋住風,使我停滯不前,他居然成為副官,而我,上帝保佑這個標記,只是他摩爾老爺的旗官。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: By heaven, I rather would have been his hangman.
passages.vernacular: 憑天發誓,我寧願做佢嘅劊子手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑天發誓,我寧願做他的劊子手。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Why, there’s no remedy.
passages.vernacular: 咦,冇辦法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,沒辦法。

passages.original: ’Tis the curse of service, Preferment goes by letter and affection, And not by old gradation, where each second Stood heir to the first.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係服役嘅詛咒,晉升靠推薦信同私情,而唔係按舊有嘅等級,即每個次位繼承前一位。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是服役的詛咒,晉升靠推薦信和私情,而不是按舊有的等級,即每個次位繼承前一位。

passages.original: Now sir, be judge yourself Whether I in any just term am affin’d To love the Moor.
passages.vernacular: 而家,先生,你自己評判,我有任何正當理由,要愛呢個摩爾人嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,先生,你自己評判,我有任何正當理由,要愛這個摩爾人嗎?

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: I would not follow him, then.
passages.vernacular: 咁我就唔跟隨佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那我就不跟隨他。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: O, sir, content you.
passages.vernacular: 啊,先生,請放心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,先生,請放心。

passages.original: I follow him to serve my turn upon him: We cannot all be masters, nor all masters Cannot be truly follow’d.
passages.vernacular: 我跟隨佢,係為咗利用佢達到我嘅目的:我哋唔能全部做主人,所有主人亦唔能全被真誠跟隨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我跟隨他,是為了利用他達到我的目的:我們不能全部做主人,所有主人也不能全被真誠跟隨。

passages.original: You shall mark Many a duteous and knee-crooking knave That, doting on his own obsequious bondage, Wears out his time, much like his master’s ass, For nought but provender, and when he’s old, cashier’d.
passages.vernacular: 你會見到許多盡責、屈膝嘅奴才,迷戀自己奉承嘅束縛,一生磨損,像主人嘅驢,只為草料,老咗就被遣散。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會見到許多盡責、屈膝的奴才,迷戀自己奉承的束縛,一生磨損,像主人的驢,只為草料,老了就被遣散。

passages.original: Whip me such honest knaves.
passages.vernacular: 把呢種老實奴才鞭打畀我睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把這種老實奴才鞭打給我看。

passages.original: Others there are Who, trimm’d in forms, and visages of duty, Keep yet their hearts attending on themselves, And throwing but shows of service on their lords, Do well thrive by them, and when they have lin’d their coats, Do themselves homage.
passages.vernacular: 另有一些人,裝飾著盡忠嘅形式同面貌,心卻一直為自己服務,只對主人做表面功夫,靠佢哋好好發達,等到口袋裝滿,就向自己致敬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另有一些人,裝飾著盡忠的形式和面貌,心卻一直為自己服務,只對主人做表面功夫,靠他們好好發達,等到口袋裝滿,就向自己致敬。

passages.original: These fellows have some soul, And such a one do I profess myself.
passages.vernacular: 呢類人有啲靈魂,我自認就係咁樣嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這類人有點靈魂,我自認就是這樣的人。

passages.original: For, sir, It is as sure as you are Roderigo, Were I the Moor, I would not be Iago:
passages.vernacular: 因為,先生,就像你係羅德利哥一樣確定,如果我係摩爾人,我就唔會做伊阿古:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為,先生,就像你是羅德利哥一樣確定,如果我是摩爾人,我就不會做伊阿古:

passages.original: In following him, I follow but myself.
passages.vernacular: 跟隨佢,我其實只係在跟隨我自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跟隨他,我其實只是在跟隨我自己。

passages.original: Heaven is my judge, not I for love and duty, But seeming so for my peculiar end.
passages.vernacular: 上天為證,我並非出於愛同責任,而只係為咗我自己嘅特殊目的而裝作如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上天為證,我並非出於愛和責任,而只是為了我自己的特殊目的而裝作如此。

passages.original: For when my outward action doth demonstrate The native act and figure of my heart In complement extern, ’tis not long after But I will wear my heart upon my sleeve For daws to peck at: I am not what I am.
passages.vernacular: 因為當我外在嘅行動,以表面客套顯示我內心天生嘅行為同形象時,不久之後,我就會把心掛在袖子上,讓寒鴉啄食:我並唔係我所表現嘅嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為當我外在的行動,以表面客套顯示我內心天生的行為和形象時,不久之後,我就會把心掛在袖子上,讓寒鴉啄食:我並不是我所表現的那樣。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: What a full fortune does the thick-lips owe, If he can carry’t thus!
passages.vernacular: 呢個厚嘴唇如果能咁得逞,佢欠下幾咁豐厚嘅運氣!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個厚嘴唇如果能這樣得逞,他欠下多麼豐厚的運氣!

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Call up her father, Rouse him, make after him, poison his delight, Proclaim him in the streets;
passages.vernacular: 叫醒佢父親,驚動佢,追著佢,毒害佢嘅歡樂,在街上公開佢;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叫醒她父親,驚動他,追著他,毒害他的歡樂,在街上公開他;

passages.original: incense her kinsmen, And though he in a fertile climate dwell, Plague him with flies:
passages.vernacular: 激怒佢嘅親戚,縱使佢住喺肥沃之地,也用蒼蠅折磨佢:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 激怒她的親戚,縱使他住在肥沃之地,也用蒼蠅折磨他:

passages.original: though that his joy be joy, Yet throw such changes of vexation on’t, As it may lose some color.
passages.vernacular: 即使佢嘅歡樂真係歡樂,也要往上面拋煩惱嘅變化,令佢失去一些光彩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使他的歡樂真是歡樂,也要往上面拋煩惱的變化,使它失去一些光彩。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Here is her father’s house, I’ll call aloud.
passages.vernacular: 呢度就係佢父親嘅房子,我大聲叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡就是她父親的房子,我大聲叫。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Do, with like timorous accent and dire yell As when, by night and negligence, the fire Is spied in populous cities.
passages.vernacular: 叫吧,用嗰種驚恐嘅語調同可怕嘅尖叫,如同喺夜裡因疏忽,在人煙稠密嘅城市發現火災時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叫吧,用那種驚恐的語調和可怕的尖叫,如同在夜裡因疏忽,在人煙稠密的城市發現火災時。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: What ho, Brabantio!
passages.vernacular: 喂,勃拉班修!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喂,勃拉班修!

passages.original: Signior Brabantio, ho!
passages.vernacular: 勃拉班修大人,喂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勃拉班修大人,喂!

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Awake!
passages.vernacular: 醒來!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醒來!

passages.original: what ho, Brabantio!
passages.vernacular: 喂,勃拉班修!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喂,勃拉班修!

passages.original: Thieves, thieves!
passages.vernacular: 有賊,有賊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有賊,有賊!

passages.original: Look to your house, your daughter, and your bags!
passages.vernacular: 睇好你嘅屋、你嘅女兒同你嘅錢袋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看好你的屋、你的女兒和你的錢袋!

passages.original: Thieves, thieves!
passages.vernacular: 有賊,有賊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有賊,有賊!

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Brabantio appears above at a window.
passages.vernacular: 勃拉班修在上方窗口出現。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勃拉班修在上方窗口出現。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: What is the reason of this terrible summons?
passages.vernacular: 呢個可怕嘅召喚係為咗咩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這可怕的召喚是為了什麼?

passages.original: What is the matter there?
passages.vernacular: 嗰邊出咗咩事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那邊出了什麼事?

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Signior, is all your family within?
passages.vernacular: 大人,你全家都在裡面嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,你全家都在裡面嗎?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Are your doors locked?
passages.vernacular: 你嘅門鎖好了嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的門鎖好了嗎?

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: Why, wherefore ask you this?
passages.vernacular: 咦,你為何問呢個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,你為何問這個?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Zounds, sir, you’re robb’d, for shame put on your gown, Your heart is burst, you have lost half your soul;
passages.vernacular: 天啊,先生,你被偷喇,羞恥地穿上你嘅長袍,你嘅心已碎,你已失去一半靈魂;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天啊,先生,你被偷了,羞恥地穿上你的長袍,你的心已碎,你已失去一半靈魂;

passages.original: Even now, now, very now, an old black ram Is tupping your white ewe.
passages.vernacular: 就在此刻,此刻,正在此刻,一隻老黑公羊正在跟你嘅白母羊交配。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在此刻,此刻,正在此刻,一隻老黑公羊正在跟你的白母羊交配。

passages.original: Arise, arise, Awake the snorting citizens with the bell, Or else the devil will make a grandsire of you: Arise, I say.
passages.vernacular: 起來,起來,用鐘聲叫醒打鼾嘅市民,否則魔鬼會令你成為祖父:起來,我話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起來,起來,用鐘聲叫醒打鼾的市民,否則魔鬼會使你成為祖父:起來,我說。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: What, have you lost your wits?
passages.vernacular: 咩,你瘋咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,你瘋了嗎?

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Most reverend signior, do you know my voice?
passages.vernacular: 最可敬嘅大人,你認得我嘅聲音嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最可敬的大人,你認得我的聲音嗎?

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: Not I.
passages.vernacular: 唔認得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不認得。

passages.original: What are you?
passages.vernacular: 你係邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是誰?

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: My name is Roderigo.
passages.vernacular: 我叫羅德利哥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我叫羅德利哥。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: The worser welcome.
passages.vernacular: 更加唔受歡迎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 更加不受歡迎。

passages.original: I have charg’d thee not to haunt about my doors;
passages.vernacular: 我曾吩咐你唔好喺我門前出冇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我曾吩咐你不要在我門前出沒;

passages.original: In honest plainness thou hast heard me say My daughter is not for thee;
passages.vernacular: 你已聽過我坦白直講,我女兒唔係畀你嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你已聽過我坦白直說,我女兒不是給你的;

passages.original: and now in madness, Being full of supper and distempering draughts, Upon malicious bravery, dost thou come To start my quiet.
passages.vernacular: 而家你竟然喺瘋狂中,食飽晚餐、飲落擾亂神智嘅酒,出於惡意嘅逞強,嚟驚擾我嘅安寧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在你竟然在瘋狂中,吃飽晚餐、喝下擾亂神智的酒,出於惡意的逞強,來驚擾我的安寧。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Sir, sir, sir,—
passages.vernacular: 先生,先生,先生——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,先生,先生——

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: But thou must needs be sure My spirit and my place have in them power To make this bitter to thee.
passages.vernacular: 但你必須確信,我嘅精神同地位足以令你為此食苦頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你必須確信,我的精神和地位足以使你為此吃苦頭。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Patience, good sir.
passages.vernacular: 耐心,好先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 耐心,好先生。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: What tell’st thou me of robbing?
passages.vernacular: 你同我講咩盜竊?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你對我說什麼盜竊?

passages.original: This is Venice.
passages.vernacular: 呢度係威尼斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡是威尼斯。

passages.original: My house is not a grange.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅房子唔係農莊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的房子不是農莊。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Most grave Brabantio, In simple and pure soul I come to you.
passages.vernacular: 最莊重嘅勃拉班修,我以單純純潔嘅心嚟搵你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最莊重的勃拉班修,我以單純純潔的心來找你。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Zounds, sir, you are one of those that will not serve God if the devil bid you.
passages.vernacular: 天啊,先生,你係嗰種就算魔鬼吩咐你,你也唔肯事奉上帝嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天啊,先生,你是那種就算魔鬼吩咐你,你也不肯事奉上帝的人。

passages.original: Because we come to do you service, and you think we are ruffians, you’ll have your daughter cover’d with a Barbary horse;
passages.vernacular: 因為我哋嚟係為你效勞,而你以為我哋係無賴,你就寧願讓你女兒畀柏柏爾駿馬騎;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我們來是為你效勞,而你以為我們是無賴,你就寧願讓你女兒被柏柏爾駿馬騎;

passages.original: you’ll have your nephews neigh to you; you’ll have coursers for cousins and gennets for germans.
passages.vernacular: 你寧願你外甥哋向你嘶鳴;你寧願讓戰馬做表親,讓西班牙小馬做兄弟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你寧願你外甥們向你嘶鳴;你寧願讓戰馬做表親,讓西班牙小馬做兄弟。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: What profane wretch art thou?
passages.vernacular: 你係咩褻瀆嘅東西?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是什麼褻瀆的東西?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: I am one, sir, that comes to tell you your daughter and the Moor are now making the beast with two backs.
passages.vernacular: 我係嚟告訴你,先生,你女兒同摩爾人而家正在做嗰頭有兩個背嘅野獸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是來告訴你,先生,你女兒和摩爾人現在正在做那頭有兩個背的野獸。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: Thou art a villain.
passages.vernacular: 你係個惡棍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是個惡棍。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: You are a senator.
passages.vernacular: 你係個議員。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是個議員。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: This thou shalt answer.
passages.vernacular: 呢件事你要交代。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這件事你要交代。

passages.original: I know thee, Roderigo.
passages.vernacular: 我認得你,羅德利哥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我認得你,羅德利哥。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Sir, I will answer anything.
passages.vernacular: 先生,我咩都願意回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,我什麼都願意回答。

passages.original: But I beseech you, If ’t be your pleasure, and most wise consent, (As partly I find it is) that your fair daughter, At this odd-even and dull watch o’ the night, Transported with no worse nor better guard, But with a knave of common hire, a gondolier, To the gross clasps of a lascivious Moor:
passages.vernacular: 但我懇求你,如果呢個係你嘅意願,也係你最明智嘅同意(我部分睇來確係如此),你美麗嘅女兒,在呢個奇怪而沉悶嘅夜晚,冇更好或更差嘅護衛,只有一個普通雇傭嘅奴才,一個船夫,被送到一個淫蕩摩爾人粗野嘅擁抱中:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我懇求你,如果這是你的意願,也是你最明智的同意(我部分看來確是如此),你美麗的女兒,在這奇怪而沉悶的夜晚,沒有更好或更差的護衛,只有一個普通雇傭的奴才,一個船夫,被送到一個淫蕩摩爾人粗野的擁抱中:

passages.original: If this be known to you, and your allowance, We then have done you bold and saucy wrongs.
passages.vernacular: 如果你知道此事,並且許可,咁我哋對你做咗大膽放肆嘅冒犯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你知道此事,並且許可,那麼我們對你做了大膽放肆的冒犯。

passages.original: But if you know not this, my manners tell me, We have your wrong rebuke.
passages.vernacular: 但如果你唔知道,我嘅禮貌告訴我,你責備我哋係唔對嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但如果你不知道,我的禮貌告訴我,你責備我們是不對的。

passages.original: Do not believe That from the sense of all civility, I thus would play and trifle with your reverence.
passages.vernacular: 唔好相信我會失去一切禮貌,咁樣戲弄、輕慢你嘅尊嚴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要相信我會失去一切禮貌,這樣戲弄、輕慢你的尊嚴。

passages.original: Your daughter (if you have not given her leave) I say again, hath made a gross revolt, Tying her duty, beauty, wit, and fortunes In an extravagant and wheeling stranger Of here and everywhere.
passages.vernacular: 你女兒(如果你冇准許)我再講一次,已犯下嚴重嘅叛逆,把佢嘅責任、美貌、智慧同財富,繫在一個四處漂泊、到處流浪嘅外來人身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你女兒(如果你沒准許)我再說一次,已犯下嚴重的叛逆,把她的責任、美貌、智慧和財富,繫在一個四處漂泊、到處流浪的外來人身上。

passages.original: Straight satisfy yourself: If she be in her chamber or your house, Let loose on me the justice of the state For thus deluding you.
passages.vernacular: 即刻親自確認:如果佢喺房間或你嘅屋裡,就讓國家嘅法律向我問罪,因我咁樣欺騙你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬上親自確認:如果她在房間或你的屋裡,就讓國家的法律向我問罪,因我這樣欺騙你。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: Strike on the tinder, ho!
passages.vernacular: 快打火,喂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 快打火,喂!

passages.original: Give me a taper!
passages.vernacular: 畀我一支蠟燭!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我一支蠟燭!

passages.original: Call up all my people!
passages.vernacular: 叫醒所有我嘅人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叫醒所有我的人!

passages.original: This accident is not unlike my dream, Belief of it oppresses me already.
passages.vernacular: 呢件事同我嘅夢境不無相似,我已經被呢個信念壓得喘不過氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這件事與我的夢境不無相似,我已經被這個信念壓得喘不過氣。

passages.original: Light, I say, light!
passages.vernacular: 光,我話,光!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 光,我說,光!

passages.original: [Exit from above.]
passages.vernacular: [從上方退下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [從上方退下。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Farewell; for I must leave you: It seems not meet nor wholesome to my place To be produc’d, as if I stay I shall, Against the Moor.
passages.vernacular: 再見;因為我必須離開你:如果我留低——睇嚟我一定會——被帶去對質摩爾人,呢個對我嘅身份既不合適,也不健康。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見;因為我必須離開你:如果我留下——看來我一定會——被帶去對質摩爾人,這對我的身份既不合適,也不健康。

passages.original: For I do know the state, However this may gall him with some check, Cannot with safety cast him, for he’s embark’d With such loud reason to the Cyprus wars, Which even now stand in act, that, for their souls, Another of his fathom they have none To lead their business.
passages.vernacular: 因為我知道,國家雖然可能對佢有所挫折,卻唔能安全地廢黜佢,因為佢已投身塞浦路斯戰爭,而戰事正在進行,佢哋就算拼命也搵唔到另一個同佢身材相當嘅人嚟領導呢項事業。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我知道,國家雖然可能對他有所挫折,卻不能安全地廢黜他,因為他已投身塞浦路斯戰爭,而戰事正在進行,他們就算拼命也找不到另一個和他身材相當的人來領導這項事業。

passages.original: In which regard, Though I do hate him as I do hell pains, Yet, for necessity of present life, I must show out a flag and sign of love, Which is indeed but sign.
passages.vernacular: 為此,雖然我恨佢如地獄嘅痛苦,但為咗眼前嘅生計,我必須打出愛嘅旗幟與標記,呢個確實只係標記而已。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為此,雖然我恨他如地獄的痛苦,但為了眼前的生計,我必須打出愛的旗幟與標記,這確實只是標記而已。

passages.original: That you shall surely find him, Lead to the Sagittary the raised search, And there will I be with him.
passages.vernacular: 你一定能搵到佢,把被喚起嘅搜索隊領到射手座旅館,我會喺嗰度與佢在一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你一定能找到他,把被喚起的搜索隊領到射手座旅館,我會在那裡與他在一起。

passages.original: So, farewell.
passages.vernacular: 咁,再見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼,再見。

passages.original: [Exit.]
Enter Brabantio with Servants and torches.
passages.vernacular: [勃拉班修帶僕人同火把上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [勃拉班修帶僕人和火把上。]

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: It is too true an evil.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係個太真實嘅災禍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是個太真實的災禍。

passages.original: Gone she is, And what’s to come of my despised time, Is naught but bitterness.
passages.vernacular: 佢走咗,我往後被輕視嘅日子,只有苦澀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她走了,我往後被輕視的日子,只有苦澀。

passages.original: Now Roderigo, Where didst thou see her?
passages.vernacular: 而家,羅德利哥,你喺邊度見到佢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,羅德利哥,你在哪裡看見她?

passages.original: (O unhappy girl!)
passages.vernacular: (啊不幸嘅女孩!)
passages.vernacularMandarin: (啊不幸的女孩!)

passages.original: With the Moor, say’st thou?
passages.vernacular: 同摩爾人在一起,你話?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 和摩爾人在一起,你說?

passages.original: (Who would be a father!)
passages.vernacular: (誰願做父親!)
passages.vernacularMandarin: (誰願做父親!)

passages.original: How didst thou know ’twas she?
passages.vernacular: 你點知道係佢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你怎麼知道是她?

passages.original: (O, she deceives me Past thought.)
passages.vernacular: (啊,佢欺騙我,超乎想像。)
passages.vernacularMandarin: (啊,她欺騙我,超乎想像。)

passages.original: What said she to you?
passages.vernacular: 佢對你講咗啲咩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她對你說了什麼?

passages.original: Get more tapers, Raise all my kindred.
passages.vernacular: 多拎啲蠟燭,叫醒我所有親戚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多拿些蠟燭,叫醒我所有親戚。

passages.original: Are they married, think you?
passages.vernacular: 你認為佢哋結咗婚嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你認為他們結婚了嗎?

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Truly I think they are.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,我諗係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,我想是。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: O heaven!
passages.vernacular: 啊天啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊天啊!

passages.original: How got she out?
passages.vernacular: 佢點出去嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她怎麼出去的?

passages.original: O treason of the blood!
passages.vernacular: 啊,血緣嘅背叛!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,血緣的背叛!

passages.original: Fathers, from hence trust not your daughters’ minds By what you see them act.
passages.vernacular: 為人父者,從此唔好憑所見嘅行為嚟信任女兒嘅心思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為人父者,從此不要憑所見的行為來信任女兒的心思。

passages.original: Is there not charms By which the property of youth and maidhood May be abused?
passages.vernacular: 難道冇咒術可以濫用青春同少女嘅天性嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 難道沒咒術可以濫用青春與少女的天性嗎?

passages.original: Have you not read, Roderigo, Of some such thing?
passages.vernacular: 羅德利哥,你冇讀過類似嘅事嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅德利哥,你沒讀過類似的事嗎?

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Yes, sir, I have indeed.
passages.vernacular: 有,先生,確實讀過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有,先生,確實讀過。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: Call up my brother.
passages.vernacular: 叫我兄弟嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叫我兄弟來。

passages.original: O, would you had had her!
passages.vernacular: 啊,要係你娶咗佢就好喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,要是你娶了她就好了!

passages.original: Some one way, some another.
passages.vernacular: 有嘅往呢邊,有嘅往嗰邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有的往這邊,有的往那邊。

passages.original: Do you know Where we may apprehend her and the Moor?
passages.vernacular: 你知道喺邊度可以捉到佢同摩爾人嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道在哪裡可以捉到她和摩爾人嗎?

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: I think I can discover him, if you please To get good guard, and go along with me.
passages.vernacular: 我諗我可以搵到佢,如果你願意帶備足夠護衛,跟我一齊去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我可以找到他,如果你願意帶備足夠護衛,跟我一起去。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: Pray you lead on.
passages.vernacular: 請你帶路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你帶路。

passages.original: At every house I’ll call, I may command at most.
passages.vernacular: 我會逐家逐戶去叫,大多數我都可以指揮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會逐家逐戶去叫,大多數我都可以指揮。

passages.original: Get weapons, ho!
passages.vernacular: 拎武器,喂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿武器,喂!

passages.original: And raise some special officers of night.
passages.vernacular: 仲要召集一些夜間特別軍官。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還要召集一些夜間特別軍官。

passages.original: On, good Roderigo.
passages.vernacular: 前進,好羅德利哥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 前進,好羅德利哥。

passages.original: I will deserve your pains.
passages.vernacular: 我會報答你嘅辛勞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會報答你的辛勞。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act I, Scene II — Venice. Another Street 第一幕第二場:威尼斯另一條街

passages.original: Enter Othello, Iago and Attendants with torches.
passages.vernacular: [奧賽羅、伊阿古同持火把嘅侍從上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧賽羅、伊阿古和持火把的侍從上。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Though in the trade of war I have slain men, Yet do I hold it very stuff o’ the conscience To do no contriv’d murder;
passages.vernacular: 雖然在戰爭呢行我殺過人,但我認為唔做預謀嘅謀殺,先係良心嘅真正本質;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然在戰爭這行我殺過人,但我認為不做預謀的謀殺,才是良心的真正本質;

passages.original: I lack iniquity Sometimes to do me service: nine or ten times I had thought to have yerk’d him here under the ribs.
passages.vernacular: 我有時缺乏邪惡去為我所用:有九次十次我本想喺呢度肋骨下刺佢一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有時缺乏邪惡去為我所用:有九次十次我本想在這裡肋骨下刺他一下。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: ’Tis better as it is.
passages.vernacular: 而家咁樣更好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在這樣更好。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Nay, but he prated, And spoke such scurvy and provoking terms Against your honour, That with the little godliness I have, I did full hard forbear him.
passages.vernacular: 唔,但佢胡講八道,對你嘅名譽講咗咁卑劣挑釁嘅講話,憑我僅有嘅一點虔誠,我先好不容易忍住唔動佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,但他胡說八道,對你的名譽說了那麼卑劣挑釁的話,憑我僅有的一點虔誠,我才好不容易忍住不動他。

passages.original: But I pray you, sir, Are you fast married?
passages.vernacular: 但請問,將軍,你真係結咗婚?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但請問,將軍,你真的結婚了嗎?

passages.original: Be assur’d of this, That the magnifico is much belov’d And hath in his effect a voice potential As double as the duke’s;
passages.vernacular: 你要肯定,嗰位大人物深受愛戴,實際上佢嘅聲音有力,影響力係公爵嘅兩倍;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要肯定,那位大人物深受愛戴,實際上他的聲音有力,影響力是公爵的兩倍;

passages.original: he will divorce you, Or put upon you what restraint and grievance The law (with all his might to enforce it on) Will give him cable.
passages.vernacular: 佢會令你離婚,或者喺法律允許(佢會用盡全力執行)嘅範圍內,向你施加任何限制同不滿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他會使你離婚,或者在法律允許(他會用盡全力執行)的範圍內,向你施加任何限制和不滿。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Let him do his spite; My services, which I have done the signiory, Shall out-tongue his complaints.
passages.vernacular: 讓佢逞恨吧;我為共和國所做嘅功勞,會比佢嘅控訴更響亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓他逞恨吧;我為共和國所做的功勞,會比他的控訴更響亮。

passages.original: ’Tis yet to know,— Which, when I know that boasting is an honour, I shall promulgate,—I fetch my life and being From men of royal siege.
passages.vernacular: 仲未有人知道——等我知道自誇係榮譽時,我會公布——我嘅生命同出身來自王族。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還沒人知道——等我知道自誇是榮譽時,我會公布——我的生命與出身來自王族。

passages.original: And my demerits May speak unbonneted to as proud a fortune As this that I have reach’d.
passages.vernacular: 而我嘅功過,可以脫帽面對與我所達到嘅同樣高傲嘅命運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而我的功過,可以脫帽面對與我所達到的同樣高傲的命運。

passages.original: For know, Iago, But that I love the gentle Desdemona, I would not my unhoused free condition Put into circumscription and confine For the sea’s worth.
passages.vernacular: 要知道,伊阿古,若唔係我愛溫柔嘅戴絲德夢娜,我唔會為咗海洋嘅全部財富,把我無拘無束嘅自由身置於限制同禁錮之中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要知道,伊阿古,若不是我愛溫柔的戴絲德夢娜,我不會為了海洋的全部財富,把我無拘無束的自由身置於限制與禁錮之中。

passages.original: But look, what lights come yond?
passages.vernacular: 但睇,嗰邊來咗咩火光?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但看,那邊來了什麼火光?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Those are the raised father and his friends: You were best go in.
passages.vernacular: 嗰啲係被喚醒嘅父親同佢嘅朋友哋:你最好入去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是被喚醒的父親和他的朋友們:你最好進去。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Not I; I must be found.
passages.vernacular: 我唔;我必須被搵到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不;我必須被找到。

passages.original: My parts, my title, and my perfect soul Shall manifest me rightly. Is it they?
passages.vernacular: 我嘅才幹、我嘅頭銜同我完美嘅靈魂會正確地顯明我。係佢哋嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的才幹、我的頭銜和我完美的靈魂會正確地顯明我。是他們嗎?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: By Janus, I think no.
passages.vernacular: 憑雅努斯,我諗唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑雅努斯,我想不是。

passages.original: Enter Cassio and Officers with torches.
passages.vernacular: [凱西奧同持火把嘅軍官哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [凱西奧和持火把的軍官們上。]

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: The servants of the duke and my lieutenant.
passages.vernacular: 係公爵嘅僕人同我嘅副官。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是公爵的僕人和我的副官。

passages.original: The goodness of the night upon you, friends!
passages.vernacular: 願夜晚嘅美好降於你哋,朋友哋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願夜晚的美好降於你們,朋友們!

passages.original: What is the news?
passages.vernacular: 有咩消息?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有什麼消息?

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: The duke does greet you, general, And he requires your haste-post-haste appearance Even on the instant.
passages.vernacular: 公爵向你問候,將軍,並要求你火速趕到,就在此刻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 公爵向你問候,將軍,並要求你火速趕到,就在此刻。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: What is the matter, think you?
passages.vernacular: 你認為係咩事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你認為是什麼事?

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Something from Cyprus, as I may divine.
passages.vernacular: 據我推測,與塞浦路斯有關。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 據我推測,與塞浦路斯有關。

passages.original: It is a business of some heat.
passages.vernacular: 係件緊急嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是件緊急的事。

passages.original: The galleys Have sent a dozen sequent messengers This very night at one another’s heels;
passages.vernacular: 戰船今晚已接連派來十二個信使,一個接一個;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戰船今晚已接連派來十二個信使,一個接一個;

passages.original: And many of the consuls, rais’d and met, Are at the duke’s already.
passages.vernacular: 許多執政官被喚起集合,已經在公爵嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 許多執政官被喚起集合,已經在公爵那裡。

passages.original: You have been hotly call’d for, When, being not at your lodging to be found, The senate hath sent about three several quests To search you out.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋急切地搵你,因為喺你住處搵唔到,元老院已派出三批人去搜尋你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們急切地找你,因為在你住處找不到,元老院已派出三批人去搜尋你。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: ’Tis well I am found by you.
passages.vernacular: 幸好被你搵到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幸好被你找到。

passages.original: I will but spend a word here in the house, And go with you.
passages.vernacular: 我只喺呢間屋裡講句話,就同你哋去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只在這屋裡說句話,就和你們去。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Ancient, what makes he here?
passages.vernacular: 旗官,佢嚟呢度做咩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 旗官,他來這裡做什麼?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Faith, he tonight hath boarded a land carrack:
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,佢今晚登上咗一艘陸地大帆船:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,他今晚登上了一艘陸地大帆船:

passages.original: If it prove lawful prize, he’s made forever.
passages.vernacular: 如果證明係合法戰利品,佢就一輩子發達。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果證明是合法戰利品,他就一輩子發達。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: I do not understand.
passages.vernacular: 我唔明白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不明白。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: He’s married.
passages.vernacular: 佢結咗婚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他結婚了。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: To who?
passages.vernacular: 同邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跟誰?

passages.original: Enter Othello.
passages.vernacular: [奧賽羅上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧賽羅上。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Marry to—Come, captain, will you go?
passages.vernacular: 娶咗——來,將軍,你去嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 娶了——來,將軍,你去嗎?

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Have with you.
passages.vernacular: 我跟你哋去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我跟你們去。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Here comes another troop to seek for you.
passages.vernacular: 又來咗一隊人搵你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又來了一隊人找你。

passages.original: Enter Brabantio, Roderigo and Officers with torches and weapons.
passages.vernacular: [勃拉班修、羅德利哥同持火把武器嘅軍官哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [勃拉班修、羅德利哥和持火把武器的軍官們上。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: It is Brabantio.
passages.vernacular: 係勃拉班修。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是勃拉班修。

passages.original: General, be advis’d, He comes to bad intent.
passages.vernacular: 將軍,小心,佢來意不善。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 將軍,小心,他來意不善。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Holla, stand there!
passages.vernacular: 喂,企住!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喂,站住!

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Signior, it is the Moor.
passages.vernacular: 大人,嗰個係摩爾人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,那是摩爾人。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: Down with him, thief!
passages.vernacular: 打倒佢,賊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 打倒他,賊!

passages.original: [They draw on both sides.]
passages.vernacular: [雙方拔劍。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [雙方拔劍。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: You, Roderigo!
passages.vernacular: 你,羅德利哥!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你,羅德利哥!

passages.original: Come, sir, I am for you.
passages.vernacular: 來,先生,我來對付你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,先生,我來對付你。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Keep up your bright swords, for the dew will rust them.
passages.vernacular: 收起你哋明亮嘅劍,露水會令佢哋生鏽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 收起你們明亮的劍,露水會使它們生鏽。

passages.original: Good signior, you shall more command with years Than with your weapons.
passages.vernacular: 好大人,你憑年齡比憑武器更能發號施令。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好大人,你憑年齡比憑武器更能發號施令。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: O thou foul thief, where hast thou stow’d my daughter?
passages.vernacular: 啊你呢個卑鄙嘅賊,你把我女兒藏喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊你這個卑鄙的賊,你把我女兒藏在哪裡?

passages.original: Damn’d as thou art, thou hast enchanted her, For I’ll refer me to all things of sense, (If she in chains of magic were not bound) Whether a maid so tender, fair, and happy, So opposite to marriage, that she shunn’d The wealthy curled darlings of our nation, Would ever have, to incur a general mock, Run from her guardage to the sooty bosom Of such a thing as thou—to fear, not to delight.
passages.vernacular: 你呢個該死嘅,你對佢施咗魔法,因為我可以訴諸一切理智嘅人,(如果佢冇被魔法嘅鎖鏈綁住)一個咁溫柔、美麗、幸福、咁反對婚姻嘅少女,連我哋國家嗰啲富有、鬈髮嘅寵兒都避開,會唔會為咗招致眾人嘲笑,逃離監護,投入你呢種東西烏黑嘅懷抱——令人恐懼,而唔係歡喜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這個該死的,你對她施了魔法,因為我可以訴諸一切理智的人,(如果她沒被魔法的鎖鏈綁住)一個如此溫柔、美麗、幸福、如此反對婚姻的少女,連我們國家那些富有、鬈髮的寵兒都避開,會不會為了招致眾人嘲笑,逃離監護,投入你這種東西烏黑的懷抱——使人恐懼,而不是歡喜。

passages.original: Judge me the world, if ’tis not gross in sense, That thou hast practis’d on her with foul charms, Abus’d her delicate youth with drugs or minerals That weakens motion.
passages.vernacular: 讓全世界評判,如果你唔係用卑鄙嘅魔咒對佢下手,用藥物或礦物濫用佢嬌嫩嘅青春,削弱佢嘅意志,呢個難道唔係明顯嘅嗎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓全世界評判,如果你不是用卑鄙的魔咒對她下手,用藥物或礦物濫用她嬌嫩的青春,削弱她的意志,這難道不是明顯的嗎。

passages.original: I’ll have’t disputed on; ’Tis probable, and palpable to thinking.
passages.vernacular: 我要把呢件事拎去辯論;呢個係可能嘅,而且在思考上顯而易見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要把這件事拿去辯論;這是可能的,而且在思考上顯而易見。

passages.original: I therefore apprehend and do attach thee For an abuser of the world, a practiser Of arts inhibited and out of warrant.— Lay hold upon him, if he do resist, Subdue him at his peril.
passages.vernacular: 所以我逮捕你,並拘押你,因為你係個毒害世界嘅人,一個施行被禁止、冇授權嘅法術嘅人。——抓住佢,如果佢反抗,後果自負,制服佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我逮捕你,並拘押你,因為你是個毒害世界的人,一個施行被禁止、沒授權的法術的人。——抓住他,如果他反抗,後果自負,制服他。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Hold your hands, Both you of my inclining and the rest:
passages.vernacular: 停手,無論係我呢邊嘅人,還係其餘嘅:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 停手,無論是我這一邊的人,還是其餘的:

passages.original: Were it my cue to fight, I should have known it Without a prompter.
passages.vernacular: 如果輪到我動手,我自己會知道,唔需要提詞員。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果輪到我動手,我自己會知道,不需要提詞員。

passages.original: Where will you that I go To answer this your charge?
passages.vernacular: 你要我去邊度回應你呢項指控?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要我去哪裡回應你這項指控?

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: To prison, till fit time Of law and course of direct session Call thee to answer.
passages.vernacular: 去監獄,直到適當嘅法律時間同直接開庭,叫你答辯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去監獄,直到適當的法律時間和直接開庭,叫你答辯。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: What if I do obey?
passages.vernacular: 如果我服從呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我服從呢?

passages.original: How may the duke be therewith satisfied, Whose messengers are here about my side, Upon some present business of the state, To bring me to him?
passages.vernacular: 公爵嘅使者就在我身旁,因國家嘅緊急事務要帶我去見公爵,咁公爵點會滿意?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 公爵的使者就在我身旁,因國家的緊急事務要帶我去見公爵,這樣公爵怎麼會滿意?

passages.title: Officer 軍官
passages.original: ’Tis true, most worthy signior, The duke’s in council, and your noble self, I am sure is sent for.
passages.vernacular: 確實如此,最尊貴嘅大人,公爵在開會,我相信您高貴嘅本人也被召去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實如此,最尊貴的大人,公爵在開會,我相信您高貴的本人也被召去了。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: How?
passages.vernacular: 點?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼?

passages.original: The duke in council?
passages.vernacular: 公爵在開會?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 公爵在開會?

passages.original: In this time of the night?
passages.vernacular: 喺呢個夜晚時分?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這夜晚時分?

passages.original: Bring him away; Mine’s not an idle cause.
passages.vernacular: 帶佢走;我嘅案子唔係閒事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 帶他走;我的案子不是閒事。

passages.original: The duke himself, Or any of my brothers of the state, Cannot but feel this wrong as ’twere their own.
passages.vernacular: 公爵本人,或我嘅任何國家同僚,都不得不覺得呢個冤屈如同自己嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 公爵本人,或我的任何國家同僚,都不得不覺得這冤屈如同自己的。

passages.original: For if such actions may have passage free, Bond-slaves and pagans shall our statesmen be.
passages.vernacular: 因為如果呢種行為可以通行無阻,我哋嘅政治家就會係奴隸同異教徒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為如果這種行為可以通行無阻,我們的政治家就會是奴隸和異教徒。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act I, Scene III — Venice. A Council Chamber 第一幕第三場:威尼斯議事廳

passages.original: The Duke and Senators sitting at a table; Officers attending.
passages.vernacular: [公爵同議員哋坐喺桌旁;軍官侍立。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [公爵和議員們坐在桌旁;軍官侍立。]

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: There is no composition in these news That gives them credit.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲消息毫無一致之處,令人難以置信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些消息毫無一致之處,令人難以置信。

passages.title: First Senator 第一議員
passages.original: Indeed, they are disproportion’d; My letters say a hundred and seven galleys.
passages.vernacular: 確實前後不合;我嘅信話有一百零七艘戰船。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實前後不合;我的信說有一百零七艘戰船。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: And mine a hundred and forty.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅話一百四十。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的說一百四十。

passages.title: Second Senator 第二議員
passages.original: And mine two hundred: But though they jump not on a just account, (As in these cases, where the aim reports, ’Tis oft with difference,) yet do they all confirm A Turkish fleet, and bearing up to Cyprus.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅話二百:但雖然數字不一致(呢種情況,憑目測報告,常有差異),佢哋都確認有一支土耳其艦隊,正駛向塞浦路斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的說二百:但雖然數字不一致(這種情況,憑目測報告,常有差異),他們都確認有一支土耳其艦隊,正駛向塞浦路斯。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Nay, it is possible enough to judgement: I do not so secure me in the error, But the main article I do approve In fearful sense.
passages.vernacular: 唔,呢個在判斷上好有可能:我並唔對呢種誤差安心,但我認可主要內容,並深感恐懼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,這在判斷上很有可能:我並不對這種誤差安心,但我認可主要內容,並深感恐懼。

passages.title: Sailor 水手
passages.original: [Within.] What, ho! what, ho! what, ho!
passages.vernacular: [內。]喂!喂!喂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: [內。]喂!喂!喂!

passages.title: Officer 軍官
passages.original: A messenger from the galleys.
passages.vernacular: 戰船來嘅信使。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戰船來的信使。

passages.original: Enter Sailor.
passages.vernacular: [水手上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [水手上。]

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Now,—what’s the business?
passages.vernacular: 點樣——咩事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎樣——什麼事?

passages.title: Sailor 水手
passages.original: The Turkish preparation makes for Rhodes, So was I bid report here to the state By Signior Angelo.
passages.vernacular: 土耳其人嘅備戰駛向羅德島,我奉安哲羅大人之命向元老院咁報告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 土耳其人的備戰駛向羅德島,我奉安哲羅大人之命向元老院如此報告。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: How say you by this change?
passages.vernacular: 你哋點睇呢個變化?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們怎麼看這個變化?

passages.title: First Senator 第一議員
passages.original: This cannot be By no assay of reason.
passages.vernacular: 無論點樣用理智推敲,呢個都不可能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論怎樣用理智推敲,這都不可能。

passages.original: ’Tis a pageant To keep us in false gaze.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係一場假象,要令我哋誤望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是一場假象,要使我們誤望。

passages.original: When we consider The importancy of Cyprus to the Turk;
passages.vernacular: 當我哋考慮到塞浦路斯對土耳其人嘅重要性時;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我們考慮到塞浦路斯對土耳其人的重要性時;

passages.original: And let ourselves again but understand That, as it more concerns the Turk than Rhodes, So may he with more facile question bear it, For that it stands not in such warlike brace, But altogether lacks the abilities That Rhodes is dress’d in.
passages.vernacular: 再讓我哋明白:既然塞浦路斯對土耳其人比羅德島更重要,佢就更容易奪取,因為佢冇咁嚴密嘅戰備,完全缺乏羅德島所具備嘅能力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再讓我們明白:既然塞浦路斯對土耳其人比羅德島更重要,他就更容易奪取,因為它沒有那麼嚴密的戰備,完全缺乏羅德島所具備的能力。

passages.original: If we make thought of this, We must not think the Turk is so unskilful To leave that latest which concerns him first, Neglecting an attempt of ease and gain, To wake and wage a danger profitless.
passages.vernacular: 如果我哋咁諗,就唔應認為土耳其人會愚蠢到,把與佢最切身相關嘅留到最後,捨棄輕易且有利嘅攻擊,去喚醒並進行無利可圖嘅危險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我們這樣想,就不應認為土耳其人會愚蠢到,把與他最切身相關的留到最後,捨棄輕易且有利的攻擊,去喚醒並進行無利可圖的危險。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Nay, in all confidence, he’s not for Rhodes.
passages.vernacular: 唔,我完全有信心,佢唔係衝著羅德島。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,我完全有信心,他不是衝著羅德島。

passages.title: Officer 軍官
passages.original: Here is more news.
passages.vernacular: 又有消息喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又有消息了。

passages.original: Enter a Messenger.
passages.vernacular: [一位信使上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [一位信使上。]

passages.title: Messenger 信使
passages.original: The Ottomites, reverend and gracious, Steering with due course toward the isle of Rhodes, Have there injointed them with an after fleet.
passages.vernacular: 尊敬而仁慈嘅大人,奧斯曼人沿正確航線駛向羅德島,已喺嗰度與後續艦隊會合。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尊敬而仁慈的大人,奧斯曼人沿正確航線駛向羅德島,已在那裡與後續艦隊會合。

passages.title: First Senator 第一議員
passages.original: Ay, so I thought.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,我就諗到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,我就想到。

passages.original: How many, as you guess?
passages.vernacular: 你猜有幾多?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你猜有多少?

passages.title: Messenger 信使
passages.original: Of thirty sail, and now they do re-stem Their backward course, bearing with frank appearance Their purposes toward Cyprus.
passages.vernacular: 三十艘帆船,而家佢哋折回航線,公開朝塞浦路斯進發。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三十艘帆船,現在他們折回航線,公開朝塞浦路斯進發。

passages.original: Signior Montano, Your trusty and most valiant servitor, With his free duty recommends you thus, And prays you to believe him.
passages.vernacular: 您忠誠勇敢嘅僕人蒙塔諾大人,以佢自由嘅忠誠咁向您致意,並請您相信佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您忠誠勇敢的僕人蒙塔諾大人,以他自由的忠誠這樣向您致意,並請您相信他。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: ’Tis certain, then, for Cyprus.
passages.vernacular: 咁可以肯定係去塞浦路斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那可以肯定是去塞浦路斯。

passages.original: Marcus Luccicos, is not he in town?
passages.vernacular: 馬可·盧奇科斯,佢唔喺城裡嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬可·盧奇科斯,他不在城裡嗎?

passages.title: First Senator 第一議員
passages.original: He’s now in Florence.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家喺佛羅倫斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他現在在佛羅倫斯。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Write from us to him; post-post-haste dispatch.
passages.vernacular: 代我哋寫信畀佢;火速發送。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 代我們寫信給他;火速發送。

passages.title: First Senator 第一議員
passages.original: Here comes Brabantio and the valiant Moor.
passages.vernacular: 勃拉班修同勇敢嘅摩爾人來喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勃拉班修和勇敢的摩爾人來了。

passages.original: Enter Brabantio, Othello, Iago, Roderigo and Officers.
passages.vernacular: [勃拉班修、奧賽羅、伊阿古、羅德利哥同軍官哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [勃拉班修、奧賽羅、伊阿古、羅德利哥和軍官們上。]

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Valiant Othello, we must straight employ you Against the general enemy Ottoman.
passages.vernacular: 勇敢嘅奧賽羅,我哋必須立即派你對付共同嘅敵人奧斯曼人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勇敢的奧賽羅,我們必須立即派你對付共同的敵人奧斯曼人。

passages.original: [To Brabantio.]
passages.vernacular: [對勃拉班修。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對勃拉班修。]

passages.original: I did not see you; welcome, gentle signior, We lack’d your counsel and your help tonight.
passages.vernacular: 我剛才冇睇到你;歡迎,高貴嘅大人,今晚我哋缺少你嘅建議同幫助。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我剛才沒看到你;歡迎,高貴的大人,今晚我們缺少你的建議和幫助。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: So did I yours.
passages.vernacular: 我也缺少你哋嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也缺少你們的。

passages.original: Good your grace, pardon me.
passages.vernacular: 好公爵殿下,請原諒我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好公爵殿下,請原諒我。

passages.original: Neither my place, nor aught I heard of business Hath rais’d me from my bed, nor doth the general care Take hold on me;
passages.vernacular: 唔係我嘅職位,也唔係我聽到嘅任何事務令我起床,公眾嘅關切也冇抓住我;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是我的職位,也不是我聽到的任何事務使我起床,公眾的關切也沒有抓住我;

passages.original: for my particular grief Is of so flood-gate and o’erbearing nature That it engluts and swallows other sorrows, And it is still itself.
passages.vernacular: 因為我個人嘅悲痛具有洪水決堤般壓倒一切嘅性質,佢吞冇咗其他悲傷,而自己依然如故。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我個人的悲痛具有洪水決堤般壓倒一切的性質,它吞沒了其他悲傷,而自己依然如故。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Why, what’s the matter?
passages.vernacular: 咦,咩事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,什麼事?

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: My daughter!
passages.vernacular: 我嘅女兒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的女兒!

passages.original: O, my daughter!
passages.vernacular: 啊,我嘅女兒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,我的女兒!

passages.title: Duke And Senators 公爵同議員們
passages.original: Dead?
passages.vernacular: 死咗?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 死了?

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: Ay, to me.
passages.vernacular: 係,對我嚟講死咗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,對我來說死了。

passages.original: She is abused, stol’n from me, and corrupted By spells and medicines bought of mountebanks;
passages.vernacular: 佢被糟蹋,被從我身邊偷走,被江湖郎中賣嘅咒術同藥物腐蝕;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她被糟蹋,被從我身邊偷走,被江湖郎中賣的咒術和藥物腐蝕;

passages.original: For nature so preposterously to err, Being not deficient, blind, or lame of sense, Sans witchcraft could not.
passages.vernacular: 因為天性若非有缺陷、盲目或感官殘廢,冇巫術係不可能咁荒謬地出錯嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為天性若非有缺陷、盲目或感官殘廢,沒巫術是不可能這樣荒謬地出錯的。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Whoe’er he be, that in this foul proceeding, Hath thus beguil’d your daughter of herself, And you of her, the bloody book of law You shall yourself read in the bitter letter, After your own sense, yea, though our proper son Stood in your action.
passages.vernacular: 無論佢係誰,在呢種卑劣嘅行為中,咁樣騙去你女兒嘅自己,也騙去你嘅女兒,你可以親自按自己嘅理解閱讀法律嗰血腥冷酷嘅字句,即使係我哋嘅親兒子牽涉喺你嘅訴訟中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論他是誰,在這種卑劣的行為中,這樣騙去你女兒的自己,也騙去你的女兒,你可以親自按自己的理解閱讀法律那血腥冷酷的字句,即使是我們的親兒子牽涉在你的訴訟中。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: Humbly I thank your grace.
passages.vernacular: 我謙卑地感謝殿下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我謙卑地感謝殿下。

passages.original: Here is the man, this Moor, whom now it seems Your special mandate for the state affairs Hath hither brought.
passages.vernacular: 呢個人喺呢度,呢個摩爾人,而家睇來係您為國家事務下嘅特別命令把佢帶來喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個人在這裡,這個摩爾人,現在看來是您為國家事務下的特別命令把他帶來了。

passages.title: All 眾人
passages.original: We are very sorry for ’t.
passages.vernacular: 我哋對此深感抱歉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們對此深感抱歉。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: [To Othello.]
passages.vernacular: [對奧賽羅。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對奧賽羅。]

passages.original: What, in your own part, can you say to this?
passages.vernacular: 就你自己而言,你有咩可講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就你自己而言,你有什麼可說?

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: Nothing, but this is so.
passages.vernacular: 冇,只能話呢個係事實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有,只能說這是事實。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Most potent, grave, and reverend signiors, My very noble and approv’d good masters:
passages.vernacular: 最有權勢、莊重而可敬嘅各位大人,我最高貴而經受考驗嘅好主人哋:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最有權勢、莊重而可敬的各位大人,我最高貴而經受考驗的好主人們:

passages.original: That I have ta’en away this old man’s daughter, It is most true;
passages.vernacular: 我帶走了呢位老人嘅女兒,呢個係千真萬確嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我帶走了這位老人的女兒,這是千真萬確的;

passages.original: true, I have married her.
passages.vernacular: 確實,我娶咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實,我娶了她。

passages.original: The very head and front of my offending Hath this extent, no more.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅罪過嘅全部範圍就係咁多,再冇喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的罪過的全部範圍就是這麼多,再沒有了。

passages.original: Rude am I in my speech, And little bless’d with the soft phrase of peace;
passages.vernacular: 我講話粗魯,缺乏和平時期嘅柔和措辭;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說話粗魯,缺乏和平時期的柔和措辭;

passages.original: For since these arms of mine had seven years’ pith, Till now some nine moons wasted, they have us’d Their dearest action in the tented field, And little of this great world can I speak, More than pertains to feats of broil and battle, And therefore little shall I grace my cause In speaking for myself.
passages.vernacular: 因為自從我呢雙臂有咗七歲嘅力氣,直到九個月前,佢哋一直在帳篷營地裡最忙碌地行動,我對呢個偉大嘅世界,除咗與爭鬥同戰事有關嘅,能講嘅好少,所以我替自己辯護時,也好難為自己嘅理由增色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為自從我這雙臂有了七歲的力氣,直到九個月前,它們一直在帳篷營地裡最忙碌地行動,我對這偉大的世界,除了與爭鬥和戰事有關的,能說的很少,所以我替自己辯護時,也很難為自己的理由增色。

passages.original: Yet, by your gracious patience, I will a round unvarnish’d tale deliver Of my whole course of love:
passages.vernacular: 然而,承蒙你哋寬容耐心,我會講一個不加修飾嘅質樸故事,講述我整個戀愛嘅過程:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,承蒙你們寬容耐心,我會講一個不加修飾的質樸故事,講述我整個戀愛的過程:

passages.original: what drugs, what charms, What conjuration, and what mighty magic, (For such proceeding I am charged withal) I won his daughter.
passages.vernacular: 我用咗咩藥物、咩符咒、咩召魂術、咩強大嘅魔法(因為我被指控用呢種手段),贏得佢嘅女兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我用了什麼藥物、什麼符咒、什麼召魂術、什麼強大的魔法(因為我被指控用這種手段),贏得他的女兒。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: A maiden never bold: Of spirit so still and quiet that her motion Blush’d at herself;
passages.vernacular: 一個從不大膽嘅少女:性情如此安靜,連佢自己嘅情動都會令佢臉紅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個從不大膽的少女:性情如此安靜,連她自己的情動都會使她臉紅;

passages.original: and she, in spite of nature, Of years, of country, credit, everything, To fall in love with what she fear’d to look on!
passages.vernacular: 而佢竟然不顧天性、年齡、國家、名譽,一切,愛上佢怕睇嘅東西!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而她竟然不顧天性、年齡、國家、名譽,一切,愛上她怕看的東西!

passages.original: It is judgement maim’d and most imperfect That will confess perfection so could err Against all rules of nature, and must be driven To find out practices of cunning hell, Why this should be.
passages.vernacular: 只有殘缺而不完整嘅判斷,先會承認完美竟能違背一切自然規律出錯,並被迫去尋找地獄嘅奸計來解釋呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有殘缺而不完整的判斷,才會承認完美竟能違背一切自然規律出錯,並被迫去尋找地獄的奸計來解釋這件事。

passages.original: I therefore vouch again, That with some mixtures powerful o’er the blood, Or with some dram conjur’d to this effect, He wrought upon her.
passages.vernacular: 因此我再次斷言,佢係用咗某種對血液有強大作用嘅混合物,或某種為此目的調製嘅藥劑,對佢下咗手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此我再次斷言,他是用了某種對血液有強大作用的混合物,或某種為此目的調製的藥劑,對她下了手。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: To vouch this is no proof; Without more wider and more overt test Than these thin habits and poor likelihoods Of modern seeming do prefer against him.
passages.vernacular: 斷言並唔係證據;除非有更廣泛、更公開嘅檢驗,而唔係你哋而家用呢啲單薄嘅推測同貧乏嘅可能性來指控佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斷言並不是證據;除非有更廣泛、更公開的檢驗,而不是你們現在用這些單薄的推測和貧乏的可能性來指控他。

passages.title: First Senator 第一議員
passages.original: But, Othello, speak: Did you by indirect and forced courses Subdue and poison this young maid’s affections?
passages.vernacular: 但奧賽羅,講吧:你是否用間接同強迫嘅手段,征服並毒害咗呢位少女嘅感情?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但奧賽羅,說吧:你是否用間接和強迫的手段,征服並毒害了這位少女的感情?

passages.original: Or came it by request, and such fair question As soul to soul affordeth?
passages.vernacular: 還係通過請求,以及靈魂對靈魂所提供嘅嗰種公平交談而來?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還是通過請求,以及靈魂對靈魂所提供的那種公平交談而來?

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: I do beseech you, Send for the lady to the Sagittary, And let her speak of me before her father.
passages.vernacular: 我懇求你哋,派人到射手座旅館請嗰位小姐,讓佢喺父親面前講我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我懇求你們,派人到射手座旅館請那位小姐,讓她在父親面前說我。

passages.original: If you do find me foul in her report, The trust, the office I do hold of you, Not only take away, but let your sentence Even fall upon my life.
passages.vernacular: 如果你哋從佢嘅陳述中發現我卑劣,唔單止要收回你哋畀我嘅信任同職位,仲要讓你哋嘅判決落喺我嘅性命上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你們從她的陳述中發現我卑劣,不但要收回你們給我的信任與職位,還要讓你們的判決落在我的性命上。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Fetch Desdemona hither.
passages.vernacular: 去帶戴絲德夢娜嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去帶戴絲德夢娜來。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Ancient, conduct them, you best know the place.
passages.vernacular: 旗官,帶佢哋去,你最熟悉嗰個地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 旗官,帶他們去,你最熟悉那地方。

passages.original: [Exeunt Iago and Attendants.]
passages.vernacular: [伊阿古同侍從哋下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [伊阿古和侍從們下。]

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: And till she come, as truly as to heaven I do confess the vices of my blood, So justly to your grave ears I’ll present How I did thrive in this fair lady’s love, And she in mine.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢嚟之前,我會如對上天嗰樣真誠地坦白我血氣嘅罪過,同樣公正地向你哋莊重嘅耳朵講述,我如何贏得呢位美麗小姐嘅愛,而佢也贏得我嘅愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在她來之前,我會如對上天那樣真誠地坦白我血氣的罪過,同樣公正地向你們莊重的耳朵講述,我如何贏得這位美麗小姐的愛,而她也贏得我的愛。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Say it, Othello.
passages.vernacular: 講吧,奧賽羅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說吧,奧賽羅。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Her father lov’d me, oft invited me, Still question’d me the story of my life, From year to year—the battles, sieges, fortunes, That I have pass’d.
passages.vernacular: 佢父親愛我,常邀請我,一直問我人生嘅故事,一年又一年——我經歷過嘅戰役、圍城、命運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她父親愛我,常邀請我,一直問我人生的故事,一年又一年——我經歷過的戰役、圍城、命運。

passages.original: I ran it through, even from my boyish days To the very moment that he bade me tell it, Wherein I spake of most disastrous chances, Of moving accidents by flood and field;
passages.vernacular: 我從少年時代講起,一直到佢叫我講述嗰一刻,講到最悲慘嘅遭遇,講到水上同陸上令人動容嘅意外;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從少年時代講起,一直到他叫我講述的那一刻,講到最悲慘的遭遇,講到水上和陸上令人動容的意外;

passages.original: Of hair-breadth scapes i’ th’ imminent deadly breach;
passages.vernacular: 講到喺迫近嘅致命缺口中千鈞一髮嘅逃脫;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 講到在迫近的致命缺口中千鈞一髮的逃脫;

passages.original: Of being taken by the insolent foe, And sold to slavery, of my redemption thence, And portance in my traveler’s history, Wherein of antres vast and deserts idle, Rough quarries, rocks, and hills whose heads touch heaven, It was my hint to speak,—such was the process;
passages.vernacular: 講到被傲慢嘅敵人俘虜,被賣為奴,我如何贖身,以及在旅行者歷史中嘅種種,其中提到廣闊嘅洞穴、荒涼嘅沙漠、崎嶇嘅採石場、岩石同頂天嘅山峰——呢個係我嘅提示——就係咁嘅過程;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 講到被傲慢的敵人俘虜,被賣為奴,我如何贖身,以及在旅行者歷史中的種種,其中提到廣闊的洞穴、荒涼的沙漠、崎嶇的採石場、岩石與頂天的山峰——這是我的提示——就是這樣的過程;

passages.original: And of the Cannibals that each other eat, The Anthropophagi, and men whose heads Do grow beneath their shoulders.
passages.vernacular: 還有互相吞食嘅食人族、安索波法吉人,以及頭長喺肩膀下面嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有互相吞食的食人族、安索波法吉人,以及頭長在肩膀下面的人。

passages.original: This to hear Would Desdemona seriously incline.
passages.vernacular: 聽呢啲,戴絲德夢娜認真地傾心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽這些,戴絲德夢娜認真地傾心。

passages.original: But still the house affairs would draw her thence, Which ever as she could with haste dispatch, She’d come again, and with a greedy ear Devour up my discourse;
passages.vernacular: 但家務事總係把佢叫走,佢每次盡快處理完,就會返嚟,用貪婪嘅耳朵吞下我嘅話;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但家務事總是把她叫走,她每次盡快處理完,就會回來,用貪婪的耳朵吞下我的話;

passages.original: which I observing, Took once a pliant hour, and found good means To draw from her a prayer of earnest heart That I would all my pilgrimage dilate, Whereof by parcels she had something heard, But not intentively.
passages.vernacular: 我注意到呢點,有一次趁著合適嘅時機,搵到辦法令佢誠懇地請求我,把我整個朝聖之旅詳細講述,佢以前零零碎碎聽過一些,卻唔係專心聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我注意到這點,有一次趁著合適的時機,找到辦法讓她誠懇地請求我,把我整個朝聖之旅詳細講述,她以前零零碎碎聽過一些,卻不是專心聽。

passages.original: I did consent, And often did beguile her of her tears, When I did speak of some distressful stroke That my youth suffer’d.
passages.vernacular: 我答應喇,每當我講到年輕時遭受嘅某個悲慘打擊,常引得佢落淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我答應了,每當我講到年輕時遭受的某個悲慘打擊,常引得她落淚。

passages.original: My story being done, She gave me for my pains a world of sighs.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅故事講完後,佢畀咗我一世界嘅歎息作為辛勞嘅回報。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的故事講完後,她給了我一世界的歎息作為辛勞的回報。

passages.original: She swore, in faith, ’twas strange, ’twas passing strange;
passages.vernacular: 佢發誓,真嘅,呢個奇怪,奇怪極喇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她發誓,真的,這奇怪,奇怪極了;

passages.original: ’Twas pitiful, ’twas wondrous pitiful.
passages.vernacular: 呢個可憐,可憐得不可思議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這可憐,可憐得不可思議。

passages.original: She wish’d she had not heard it, yet she wish’d That heaven had made her such a man:
passages.vernacular: 佢希望冇聽過,卻又希望上天把佢造成咁嘅一個人:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她希望沒聽過,卻又希望上天把她造成這樣的一個人:

passages.original: she thank’d me, And bade me, if I had a friend that lov’d her, I should but teach him how to tell my story, And that would woo her.
passages.vernacular: 佢感謝我,並吩咐我,如果我有個朋友愛佢,只需教佢點樣講我嘅故事,咁就能追求佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她感謝我,並吩咐我,如果我有個朋友愛她,只需教他如何講我的故事,那就能追求她。

passages.original: Upon this hint I spake: She lov’d me for the dangers I had pass’d, And I lov’d her that she did pity them.
passages.vernacular: 我就憑呢個暗示開口:佢愛我,係因為我經歷嘅危險;我愛佢,係因為佢憐憫呢啲危險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就憑這個暗示開口:她愛我,是因為我經歷的危險;我愛她,是因為她憐憫這些危險。

passages.original: This only is the witchcraft I have us’d.
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係我用過嘅唯一巫術。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是我用過的唯一巫術。

passages.original: Here comes the lady.
passages.vernacular: 小姐來喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小姐來了。

passages.original: Let her witness it.
passages.vernacular: 讓佢作證。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓她作證。

passages.original: Enter Desdemona, Iago and Attendants.
passages.vernacular: [戴絲德夢娜、伊阿古同侍從哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [戴絲德夢娜、伊阿古和侍從們上。]

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: I think this tale would win my daughter too.
passages.vernacular: 我諗呢個故事也會贏得我女兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想這個故事也會贏得我女兒。

passages.original: Good Brabantio, Take up this mangled matter at the best.
passages.vernacular: 好勃拉班修,把呢件殘破嘅事盡量往好處諗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好勃拉班修,把這件殘破的事盡量往好處想。

passages.original: Men do their broken weapons rather use Than their bare hands.
passages.vernacular: 人寧願用壞咗嘅武器,也唔用赤手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人寧願用壞了的武器,也不用赤手。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: I pray you hear her speak.
passages.vernacular: 請你聽佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你聽她說。

passages.original: If she confess that she was half the wooer, Destruction on my head, if my bad blame Light on the man!—Come hither, gentle mistress:
passages.vernacular: 如果佢承認自己有一半係追求者,願我頭上降毀滅,如果我歸咎於嗰個人!——過嚟,高貴嘅小姐:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她承認自己有一半是追求者,願我頭上降毀滅,如果我歸咎於那個人!——過來,高貴的小姐:

passages.original: Do you perceive in all this noble company Where most you owe obedience?
passages.vernacular: 你在呢個高貴嘅場合中,是否睇出你最應該服從誰?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在這個高貴的場合中,是否看出你最應該服從誰?

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: My noble father, I do perceive here a divided duty:
passages.vernacular: 我高貴嘅父親,我喺呢度睇到一個分裂嘅責任:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我高貴的父親,我在這裡看到一個分裂的責任:

passages.original: To you I am bound for life and education.
passages.vernacular: 我因生命同教養而對你負有責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我因生命與教養而對你負有責任。

passages.original: My life and education both do learn me How to respect you.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅生命同教養都教我點樣尊敬你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的生命與教養都教我如何尊敬你。

passages.original: You are the lord of duty, I am hitherto your daughter: but here’s my husband.
passages.vernacular: 你係責任嘅主人,到此為止我係你嘅女兒:但呢度係我嘅丈夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是責任的主人,到此為止我是你的女兒:但這裡是我的丈夫。

passages.original: And so much duty as my mother show’d To you, preferring you before her father, So much I challenge that I may profess Due to the Moor my lord.
passages.vernacular: 正如我母親向你顯示嘅責任,佢把你置於佢父親之前,我也要求同樣多嘅責任,我可以聲明呢個係應對摩爾人我嘅主人嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正如我母親向你顯示的責任,她把你置於她父親之前,我也要求同樣多的責任,我可以聲明這是應對摩爾人我的主人的。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: God be with you!
passages.vernacular: 願上帝與你同在!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願上帝與你同在!

passages.original: I have done.
passages.vernacular: 我講完喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說完了。

passages.original: Please it your grace, on to the state affairs.
passages.vernacular: 請殿下繼續處理國家事務。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請殿下繼續處理國家事務。

passages.original: I had rather to adopt a child than get it.— Come hither, Moor:
passages.vernacular: 我寧願收養孩子,也唔生孩子。——過嚟,摩爾人:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧願收養孩子,也不生孩子。——過來,摩爾人:

passages.original: I here do give thee that with all my heart Which, but thou hast already, with all my heart I would keep from thee.—For your sake, jewel, I am glad at soul I have no other child, For thy escape would teach me tyranny, To hang clogs on them.—I have done, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 我在此全心全意把呢個畀你——如果你仲冇,我全心全意唔會畀你——為咗你,寶貝,我心裡高興我冇別嘅孩子,因為你嘅逃離會教我變成暴君,畀佢哋戴上枷鎖。——我講完喇,殿下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在此全心全意把這個給你——如果你還沒有,我全心全意不會給你——為了你,寶貝,我心裡高興我沒別的孩子,因為你的逃離會教我變成暴君,給他們戴上枷鎖。——我說完了,殿下。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Let me speak like yourself, and lay a sentence, Which as a grise or step may help these lovers Into your favour.
passages.vernacular: 讓我像你一樣講嘢,並講一句格言,作為台階,幫助呢對戀人得到你嘅恩寵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我像你一樣說話,並說一句格言,作為台階,幫助這對戀人得到你的恩寵。

passages.original: When remedies are past, the griefs are ended By seeing the worst, which late on hopes depended.
passages.vernacular: 當補救已過,睇到最壞嘅情況,悲傷就結束喇,呢個最壞嘅剛才還繫於希望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當補救已過,看到最壞的情況,悲傷就結束了,這最壞的剛才還繫於希望。

passages.original: To mourn a mischief that is past and gone Is the next way to draw new mischief on.
passages.vernacular: 哀悼已過去嘅災禍,係招來新災禍嘅捷徑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哀悼已過去的災禍,是招來新災禍的捷徑。

passages.original: What cannot be preserved when fortune takes, Patience her injury a mockery makes.
passages.vernacular: 命運奪走而無法保全嘅,耐心就把佢嘅傷害變成嘲笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 命運奪走而無法保全的,耐心就把她的傷害變成嘲笑。

passages.original: The robb’d that smiles steals something from the thief;
passages.vernacular: 被劫而微笑嘅人,從賊嗰度偷到一點東西;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被劫而微笑的人,從賊那裡偷到一點東西;

passages.original: He robs himself that spends a bootless grief.
passages.vernacular: 沉溺無益悲傷嘅人,係在搶劫自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沉溺無益悲傷的人,是在搶劫自己。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: So let the Turk of Cyprus us beguile, We lose it not so long as we can smile;
passages.vernacular: 即使土耳其人騙走塞浦路斯,只要我哋能微笑,我哋就冇失去;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使土耳其人騙走塞浦路斯,只要我們能微笑,我們就沒有失去;

passages.original: He bears the sentence well, that nothing bears But the free comfort which from thence he hears;
passages.vernacular: 嗰只承受自由安慰嘅人,把判決承受得好;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那只承受自由安慰的人,把判決承受得好;

passages.original: But he bears both the sentence and the sorrow That, to pay grief, must of poor patience borrow.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰為咗償還悲傷而必須向可憐嘅耐心借貸嘅人,既承受判決,又承受悲傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那為了償還悲傷而必須向可憐的耐心借貸的人,既承受判決,又承受悲傷。

passages.original: These sentences to sugar or to gall, Being strong on both sides, are equivocal:
passages.vernacular: 呢啲格言,無論化作糖或膽汁,兩邊都強,意思含糊:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些格言,無論化作糖或膽汁,兩邊都強,意思含糊:

passages.original: But words are words; I never yet did hear That the bruis’d heart was pierced through the ear.
passages.vernacular: 但話只係話;我從未聽過被擊傷嘅心係從耳朵被刺穿嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但話只是話;我從未聽過被擊傷的心是從耳朵被刺穿的。

passages.original: I humbly beseech you, proceed to the affairs of state.
passages.vernacular: 我謙卑地懇求你,繼續國家事務。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我謙卑地懇求你,繼續國家事務。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: The Turk with a most mighty preparation makes for Cyprus.
passages.vernacular: 土耳其人以最強大嘅準備駛向塞浦路斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 土耳其人以最強大的準備駛向塞浦路斯。

passages.original: Othello, the fortitude of the place is best known to you.
passages.vernacular: 奧賽羅,呢個地方嘅防禦力你最清楚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奧賽羅,這個地方的防禦力你最清楚。

passages.original: And though we have there a substitute of most allowed sufficiency, yet opinion, a sovereign mistress of effects, throws a more safer voice on you:
passages.vernacular: 雖然我哋喺嗰度有一位公認非常勝任嘅代理,但輿論作為效果嘅至高女主人,更信任你:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然我們在那裡有一位公認非常勝任的代理,但輿論作為效果的至高女主人,更信任你:

passages.original: you must therefore be content to slubber the gloss of your new fortunes with this more stubborn and boisterous expedition.
passages.vernacular: 所以你必須甘心用呢次更艱難、更喧鬧嘅遠征,來玷污你新婚好運嘅光澤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以你必須甘心用這次更艱難、更喧鬧的遠征,來玷污你新婚好運的光澤。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: The tyrant custom, most grave senators, Hath made the flinty and steel couch of war My thrice-driven bed of down:
passages.vernacular: 暴君「習慣」,最莊重嘅議員哋,已令堅硬如燧石同鋼鐵嘅戰場之床,成為我三度壓實嘅鵝絨床:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 暴君「習慣」,最莊重的議員們,已使堅硬如燧石和鋼鐵的戰場之床,成為我三度壓實的鵝絨床:

passages.original: I do agnize A natural and prompt alacrity I find in hardness, and do undertake This present wars against the Ottomites.
passages.vernacular: 我承認,我喺艱苦中發現一種天然而敏捷嘅活力,並承擔呢場對抗奧斯曼人嘅戰爭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我承認,我在艱苦中發現一種天然而敏捷的活力,並承擔這場對抗奧斯曼人的戰爭。

passages.original: Most humbly, therefore, bending to your state, I crave fit disposition for my wife, Due reference of place and exhibition, With such accommodation and besort As levels with her breeding.
passages.vernacular: 因此,我最謙卑地向你哋嘅權威鞠躬,請求為我妻子安排適當處置,適當嘅居所、津貼,以及符合佢出身嘅待遇同隨從。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此,我最謙卑地向你們的權威鞠躬,請求為我妻子安排適當處置,適當的居所、津貼,以及符合她出身的待遇與隨從。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: If you please, Be’t at her father’s.
passages.vernacular: 如果你哋願意,就安排喺佢父親家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你們願意,就安排在她父親家。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: I’ll not have it so.
passages.vernacular: 我唔同意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不同意。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Nor I.
passages.vernacular: 我也唔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也不。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Nor I.
passages.vernacular: 我也唔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也不。

passages.original: I would not there reside, To put my father in impatient thoughts, By being in his eye.
passages.vernacular: 我唔願住喺嗰度,因喺佢眼前而令父親焦躁不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不願住在那裡,因在他眼前而使父親焦躁不安。

passages.original: Most gracious duke, To my unfolding lend your prosperous ear, And let me find a charter in your voice T’ assist my simpleness.
passages.vernacular: 最仁慈嘅公爵,請賜予我陳述以順利嘅耳朵,讓我喺你嘅聲音中搵到特許,幫助我嘅單純。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最仁慈的公爵,請賜予我陳述以順利的耳朵,讓我在你的聲音中找到特許,幫助我的單純。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: What would you, Desdemona?
passages.vernacular: 你想要咩,戴絲德夢娜?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你想要什麼,戴絲德夢娜?

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: That I did love the Moor to live with him, My downright violence and storm of fortunes May trumpet to the world:
passages.vernacular: 我愛摩爾人並願與佢同住,我嘅直接暴烈同命運嘅風暴可以向全世界宣告:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我愛摩爾人並願與他同住,我的直接暴烈與命運的風暴可以向全世界宣告:

passages.original: my heart’s subdued Even to the very quality of my lord.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅心甚至被征服到與我丈夫嘅本性相同。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的心甚至被征服到與我丈夫的本性相同。

passages.original: I saw Othello’s visage in his mind, And to his honours and his valiant parts Did I my soul and fortunes consecrate.
passages.vernacular: 我喺奧賽羅嘅心靈中睇到佢嘅容貌,並將我嘅靈魂同命運奉獻畀佢嘅榮譽同英勇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在奧賽羅的心靈中看到他的容貌,並將我的靈魂與命運奉獻給他的榮譽與英勇。

passages.original: So that, dear lords, if I be left behind, A moth of peace, and he go to the war, The rites for which I love him are bereft me, And I a heavy interim shall support By his dear absence.
passages.vernacular: 所以,親愛嘅大人哋,如果我被留下,作為和平嘅飛蛾,而佢上戰場,我愛佢嘅嗰啲儀式就被剝奪喇,我將喺佢珍貴嘅缺席中忍受沉重嘅空白期。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,親愛的大人們,如果我被留下,作為和平的飛蛾,而他上戰場,我愛他的那些儀式就被剝奪了,我將在他珍貴的缺席中忍受沉重的空白期。

passages.original: Let me go with him.
passages.vernacular: 讓我跟佢去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我跟他去。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Let her have your voice.
passages.vernacular: 請讓佢得到你嘅聲音(同意)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請讓她得到你的聲音(同意)。

passages.original: Vouch with me, heaven, I therefore beg it not To please the palate of my appetite, Nor to comply with heat, the young affects In me defunct, and proper satisfaction, But to be free and bounteous to her mind.
passages.vernacular: 天啊,與我同證:我請求呢點,唔係為咗討好我嘅食慾,也唔係為咗迎合熱情——我身上年輕嘅情慾已經消亡——同相應嘅滿足,而只係為咗自由大度地順從佢嘅意願。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天啊,與我同證:我請求這點,不是為了討好我的食慾,也不是為了迎合熱情——我身上年輕的情慾已經消亡——和相應的滿足,而只是為了自由大度地順從她的意願。

passages.original: And heaven defend your good souls that you think I will your serious and great business scant For she is with me.
passages.vernacular: 願上天保佑你哋善良嘅靈魂,唔好以為我因為佢與我同行,就會忽略你哋嚴肅重大嘅事務。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願上天保佑你們善良的靈魂,不要以為我因為她與我同行,就會忽略你們嚴肅重大的事務。

passages.original: No, when light-wing’d toys Of feather’d Cupid seel with wanton dullness My speculative and offic’d instruments, That my disports corrupt and taint my business, Let housewives make a skillet of my helm, And all indign and base adversities Make head against my estimation.
passages.vernacular: 唔會,如果長羽翼嘅丘比特嗰啲輕翼玩意以放蕩嘅遲鈍蒙住我嘅觀察同職務器官,令我嘅消遣腐蝕污染我嘅事務,就讓主婦把我嘅頭盔做成煎鍋,讓一切卑劣嘅逆境對我嘅名聲聚眾進攻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不會,如果長羽翼的丘比特那些輕翼玩意以放蕩的遲鈍蒙住我的觀察與職務器官,讓我的消遣腐蝕污染我的事務,就讓主婦把我的頭盔做成煎鍋,讓一切卑劣的逆境對我的名聲聚眾進攻。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Be it as you shall privately determine, Either for her stay or going.
passages.vernacular: 你哋私下決定,無論佢留下還係同行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們私下決定,無論她留下還是同行。

passages.original: The affair cries haste, And speed must answer it.
passages.vernacular: 事情要求迅速,必須迅速應對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事情要求迅速,必須迅速應對。

passages.title: First Senator 第一議員
passages.original: You must away tonight.
passages.vernacular: 你今晚必須出發。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你今晚必須出發。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: With all my heart.
passages.vernacular: 全心樂意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 全心樂意。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: At nine i’ the morning here we’ll meet again.
passages.vernacular: 明朝九點,我哋喺呢度再見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明早九點,我們在這裡再見。

passages.original: Othello, leave some officer behind, And he shall our commission bring to you, With such things else of quality and respect As doth import you.
passages.vernacular: 奧賽羅,留下一位軍官,佢會把我哋嘅委任狀帶畀你,連同其他對你重要且有關嘅物品。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奧賽羅,留下一位軍官,他會把我們的委任狀帶給你,連同其他對你重要且有關的物品。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: So please your grace, my ancient, A man he is of honesty and trust, To his conveyance I assign my wife, With what else needful your good grace shall think To be sent after me.
passages.vernacular: 如果殿下同意,我嘅旗官係個誠實可靠嘅人,我把妻子交畀佢護送,還有殿下認為需要隨後送來嘅其他東西。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果殿下同意,我的旗官是個誠實可靠的人,我把妻子交給他護送,還有殿下認為需要隨後送來的其他東西。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Let it be so.
passages.vernacular: 就咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣。

passages.original: Good night to everyone.
passages.vernacular: 大家晚安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大家晚安。

passages.original: [To Brabantio.]
passages.vernacular: [對勃拉班修。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對勃拉班修。]

passages.original: And, noble signior, If virtue no delighted beauty lack, Your son-in-law is far more fair than black.
passages.vernacular: 高貴嘅大人,如果美德唔缺悅人嘅美,你嘅女婿遠比佢嘅黑更美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 高貴的大人,如果美德不缺悅人的美,你的女婿遠比他的黑更美。

passages.title: First Senator 第一議員
passages.original: Adieu, brave Moor, use Desdemona well.
passages.vernacular: 再見,勇敢嘅摩爾人,好好待戴絲德夢娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見,勇敢的摩爾人,好好待戴絲德夢娜。

passages.title: Brabantio 勃拉班修
passages.original: Look to her, Moor, if thou hast eyes to see: She has deceiv’d her father, and may thee.
passages.vernacular: 摩爾人,如果你有眼睛,就留意佢:佢騙咗父親,也可能騙你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 摩爾人,如果你有眼睛,就留意她:她騙了父親,也可能騙你。

passages.original: [Exeunt Duke, Senators, Officers, &c.]
passages.vernacular: [公爵、議員、軍官等下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [公爵、議員、軍官等下。]

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: My life upon her faith!
passages.vernacular: 我拎生命擔保佢嘅忠貞!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我拿生命擔保她的忠貞!

passages.original: Honest Iago, My Desdemona must I leave to thee.
passages.vernacular: 誠實嘅伊阿古,我必須把我嘅戴絲德夢娜交畀你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誠實的伊阿古,我必須把我的戴絲德夢娜交給你。

passages.original: I prithee, let thy wife attend on her, And bring them after in the best advantage.— Come, Desdemona, I have but an hour Of love, of worldly matters, and direction, To spend with thee.
passages.vernacular: 請你讓你妻子服侍佢,並喺最好嘅時機把佢哋帶來。——來,戴絲德夢娜,我只有一小時嘅時間用於愛情、世俗事務同指示,與你共度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你讓你妻子服侍她,並在最好的時機把她們帶來。——來,戴絲德夢娜,我只有一小時的時間用於愛情、世俗事務和指示,與你共度。

passages.original: We must obey the time.
passages.vernacular: 我哋必須服從時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們必須服從時間。

passages.original: [Exeunt Othello and Desdemona.]
passages.vernacular: [奧賽羅同戴絲德夢娜下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧賽羅和戴絲德夢娜下。]

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Iago—
passages.vernacular: 伊阿古——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 伊阿古——

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: What sayst thou, noble heart?
passages.vernacular: 你講咩,高貴嘅心?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說什麼,高貴的心?

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: What will I do, thinkest thou?
passages.vernacular: 你認為我該點算?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你認為我該怎麼辦?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Why, go to bed and sleep.
passages.vernacular: 咦,上床瞓覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,上床睡覺。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: I will incontinently drown myself.
passages.vernacular: 我要立刻淹死自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要立刻淹死自己。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: If thou dost, I shall never love thee after.
passages.vernacular: 如果你咁做,我以後再也唔會愛你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你這樣做,我以後再也不會愛你。

passages.original: Why, thou silly gentleman!
passages.vernacular: 咦,你呢個傻瓜紳士!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,你這個傻瓜紳士!

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: It is silliness to live, when to live is torment;
passages.vernacular: 活著係折磨嘅時候,活著就係愚蠢;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 活著是折磨的時候,活著就是愚蠢;

passages.original: and then have we a prescription to die when death is our physician.
passages.vernacular: 然後當死亡係我哋嘅醫生時,我哋就有死嘅處方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後當死亡是我們的醫生時,我們就有死的處方。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: O villainous!
passages.vernacular: 啊,卑鄙!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,卑鄙!

passages.original: I have looked upon the world for four times seven years, and since I could distinguish betwixt a benefit and an injury, I never found man that knew how to love himself.
passages.vernacular: 我睇呢個世界已有四乘七年(二十八年),自從我能分辨好處同傷害,我從未見過一個識得愛自己嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看這個世界已有四乘七年(二十八年),自從我能分辨好處與傷害,我從未見過一個懂得愛自己的人。

passages.original: Ere I would say I would drown myself for the love of a guinea-hen, I would change my humanity with a baboon.
passages.vernacular: 在我講我要為一隻珍珠雞(比喻女人)嘅愛而淹死自己之前,我寧願把我嘅人性換畀狒狒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我說我要為一隻珍珠雞(比喻女人)的愛而淹死自己之前,我寧願把我的人性換給狒狒。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: What should I do?
passages.vernacular: 我該點算?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我該怎麼辦?

passages.original: I confess it is my shame to be so fond, but it is not in my virtue to amend it.
passages.vernacular: 我承認咁癡情係我嘅羞恥,但我嘅美德無力改正。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我承認這麼癡情是我的羞恥,但我的美德無力改正。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Virtue! a fig!
passages.vernacular: 美德!算個屁!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美德!算個屁!

passages.original: ’Tis in ourselves that we are thus or thus.
passages.vernacular: 我哋係咁樣或嗰樣,全在我哋自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們是這樣或那樣,全在我們自己。

passages.original: Our bodies are gardens, to the which our wills are gardeners.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅身體係花園,我哋嘅意志係園丁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的身體是花園,我們的意志是園丁。

passages.original: So that if we will plant nettles or sow lettuce, set hyssop and weed up thyme, supply it with one gender of herbs or distract it with many, either to have it sterile with idleness or manured with industry, why, the power and corrigible authority of this lies in our wills.
passages.vernacular: 所以,不論我哋要種蕁麻還係播萵苣,栽種牛膝草還係拔除百里香,只供應一種草藥還係分散種多種,讓佢因懶惰而荒蕪還係因勤勞而施肥,呢個嘅力量同可糾正嘅權威,全在於我哋嘅意志。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,不論我們要種蕁麻還是播萵苣,栽種牛膝草還是拔除百里香,只供應一種草藥還是分散種多種,讓它因懶惰而荒蕪還是因勤勞而施肥,這個的力量與可糾正的權威,全在於我們的意志。

passages.original: If the balance of our lives had not one scale of reason to poise another of sensuality, the blood and baseness of our natures would conduct us to most preposterous conclusions.
passages.vernacular: 如果我哋生命嘅天平冇一邊係理性來平衡另一邊嘅感性,我哋天性嘅血氣同卑劣就會引我哋得出最荒謬嘅結論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我們生命的天平沒有一邊是理性來平衡另一邊的感性,我們天性的血氣與卑劣就會引我們得出最荒謬的結論。

passages.original: But we have reason to cool our raging motions, our carnal stings, our unbitted lusts;
passages.vernacular: 但我哋有理性去冷卻我哋狂暴嘅衝動、肉慾嘅刺痛、不受控制嘅情慾;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我們有理性去冷卻我們狂暴的衝動、肉慾的刺痛、不受控制的情慾;

passages.original: whereof I take this, that you call love, to be a sect, or scion.
passages.vernacular: 由此我認為,你所謂嘅愛,不過係一個分支或嫁接枝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 由此我認為,你所謂的愛,不過是一個分支或嫁接枝。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: It cannot be.
passages.vernacular: 不可能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不可能。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: It is merely a lust of the blood and a permission of the will.
passages.vernacular: 佢只係血氣嘅慾望同意志嘅許可。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它只是血氣的慾望和意志的許可。

passages.original: Come, be a man.
passages.vernacular: 來,做個男子漢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,做個男子漢。

passages.original: Drown thyself?
passages.vernacular: 淹死自己?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 淹死自己?

passages.original: Drown cats and blind puppies.
passages.vernacular: 去淹死貓同瞎眼小狗吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去淹死貓和瞎眼小狗吧。

passages.original: I have professed me thy friend, and I confess me knit to thy deserving with cables of perdurable toughness;
passages.vernacular: 我已自稱係你嘅朋友,我承認我用永恆堅韌嘅纜繩繫在你嘅價值上;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已自稱是你的朋友,我承認我用永恆堅韌的纜繩繫在你的價值上;

passages.original: I could never better stead thee than now.
passages.vernacular: 我從未比而家更能幫你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從未比現在更能幫你。

passages.original: Put money in thy purse; follow thou the wars;
passages.vernacular: 把錢放進你錢包;去跟隨戰爭;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把錢放進你錢包;去跟隨戰爭;

passages.original: defeat thy favour with an usurped beard; I say, put money in thy purse.
passages.vernacular: 用借來嘅鬍子改變你嘅容貌;我話,把錢放進錢包。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 用借來的鬍子改變你的容貌;我說,把錢放進錢包。

passages.original: It cannot be that Desdemona should long continue her love to the Moor,—put money in thy purse,—nor he his to her.
passages.vernacular: 戴絲德夢娜不可能長久愛摩爾人——把錢放進錢包——佢也不可能長久愛佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戴絲德夢娜不可能長久愛摩爾人——把錢放進錢包——他也不可能長久愛她。

passages.original: It was a violent commencement, and thou shalt see an answerable sequestration—put but money in thy purse.
passages.vernacular: 開始得猛烈,你會睇到相應嘅分離——只要把錢放進錢包。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 開始得猛烈,你會看到相應的分離——只要把錢放進錢包。

passages.original: These Moors are changeable in their wills.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲摩爾人意志多變。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些摩爾人意志多變。

passages.original: Fill thy purse with money.
passages.vernacular: 用錢裝滿你嘅錢包。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 用錢裝滿你的錢包。

passages.original: The food that to him now is as luscious as locusts shall be to him shortly as acerb as the coloquintida.
passages.vernacular: 而家對佢好似蝗蟲(甜果)嗰樣美味嘅食物,好快對佢就好似苦瓜(藥瓜)嗰樣苦澀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在對他像蝗蟲(甜果)那樣美味的食物,很快對他就像苦瓜(藥瓜)那樣苦澀。

passages.original: She must change for youth.
passages.vernacular: 佢必須換成年輕嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她必須換成年輕的。

passages.original: When she is sated with his body, she will find the error of her choice.
passages.vernacular: 當佢對佢嘅身體厭倦,就會發現自己選擇嘅錯誤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當她對他的身體厭倦,就會發現自己選擇的錯誤。

passages.original: She must have change, she must.
passages.vernacular: 佢必須有變化,必須。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她必須有變化,必須。

passages.original: Therefore put money in thy purse.
passages.vernacular: 所以把錢放進錢包。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以把錢放進錢包。

passages.original: If thou wilt needs damn thyself, do it a more delicate way than drowning.
passages.vernacular: 如果你一定要詛咒自己,就用比淹死更精緻嘅方式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你一定要詛咒自己,就用比淹死更精緻的方式。

passages.original: Make all the money thou canst.
passages.vernacular: 盡你所能賺錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 盡你所能賺錢。

passages.original: If sanctimony and a frail vow betwixt an erring barbarian and a supersubtle Venetian be not too hard for my wits and all the tribe of hell, thou shalt enjoy her; therefore make money.
passages.vernacular: 如果一個迷途野蠻人同一個極其狡猾嘅威尼斯女子之間嘅虛偽神聖同脆弱誓言,冇難倒我嘅智慧同整個地獄部落,你就會得到佢;所以去賺錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果一個迷途野蠻人和一個極其狡猾的威尼斯女子之間的虛偽神聖和脆弱誓言,沒難倒我的智慧和整個地獄部落,你就會得到她;所以去賺錢。

passages.original: A pox of drowning thyself!
passages.vernacular: 去你嘅淹死自己!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去你的淹死自己!
