passages.original: It is clean out of the way: seek thou rather to be hanged in compassing thy joy than to be drowned and go without her.
passages.vernacular: 呢個完全唔對路:你寧願為得到你嘅快樂而被絞死,也唔好淹死而得唔到佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這完全不對路:你寧願為得到你的快樂而被絞死,也不要淹死而得不到她。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Wilt thou be fast to my hopes if I depend on the issue?
passages.vernacular: 如果我依賴結果,你會堅守我嘅希望嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我依賴結果,你會堅守我的希望嗎?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Thou art sure of me.
passages.vernacular: 你可以確定我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可以確定我。

passages.original: Go, make money.
passages.vernacular: 去,賺錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,賺錢。

passages.original: I have told thee often, and I retell thee again and again, I hate the Moor.
passages.vernacular: 我常對你講,並且一次次重述,我憎摩爾人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我常對你說,並且一次次重述,我恨摩爾人。

passages.original: My cause is hearted; thine hath no less reason.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅理由根深蒂固;你嘅理由不遜於我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的理由根深蒂固;你的理由不遜於我。

passages.original: Let us be conjunctive in our revenge against him:
passages.vernacular: 讓我哋聯手向佢復仇:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我們聯手向他復仇:

passages.original: if thou canst cuckold him, thou dost thyself a pleasure, me a sport.
passages.vernacular: 如果你能畀佢戴綠帽,你自己得到快樂,我得到消遣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你能給他戴綠帽,你自己得到快樂,我得到消遣。

passages.original: There are many events in the womb of time which will be delivered.
passages.vernacular: 時間嘅子宮中有許多事件將要誕生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 時間的子宮中有許多事件將要誕生。

passages.original: Traverse, go, provide thy money.
passages.vernacular: 前進,去,準備你嘅錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 前進,去,準備你的錢。

passages.original: We will have more of this tomorrow. Adieu.
passages.vernacular: 明日我哋再多傾。再見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明天我們再多談。再見。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Where shall we meet i’ the morning?
passages.vernacular: 明朝喺邊度見面?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明早在哪裡見面?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: At my lodging.
passages.vernacular: 喺我嘅住處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我的住處。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: I’ll be with thee betimes.
passages.vernacular: 我會早早來搵你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會早早來找你。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Go to, farewell.
passages.vernacular: 好,再見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,再見。

passages.original: Do you hear, Roderigo?
passages.vernacular: 你聽到嗎,羅德利哥?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你聽到嗎,羅德利哥?

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: What say you?
passages.vernacular: 你講咩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說什麼?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: No more of drowning, do you hear?
passages.vernacular: 唔好再提淹死喇,你聽到嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要再提淹死了,你聽到嗎?

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: I am changed.
passages.vernacular: 我改變喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我改變了。

passages.original: I’ll sell all my land.
passages.vernacular: 我要賣掉我所有嘅地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要賣掉我所有的地。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Thus do I ever make my fool my purse.
passages.vernacular: 我就係咁樣總係把我嘅傻瓜當成我嘅錢包。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就是這樣總是把我的傻瓜當成我的錢包。

passages.original: For I mine own gain’d knowledge should profane If I would time expend with such a snipe But for my sport and profit.
passages.vernacular: 因為如果唔係為咗消遣同利益,我若把時間花喺呢種呆子身上,就係褻瀆我自己得來嘅知識。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為如果不是為了消遣和利益,我若把時間花在這種呆子身上,就是褻瀆我自己得來的知識。

passages.original: I hate the Moor, And it is thought abroad that ’twixt my sheets He has done my office.
passages.vernacular: 我憎摩爾人,外面傳講佢喺我床上做咗我嘅差事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我恨摩爾人,外面傳說他在我床上做了我的差事。

passages.original: I know not if ’t be true, But I, for mere suspicion in that kind, Will do as if for surety.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知係咪屬實,但我僅憑呢種懷疑,就會當作確實嗰樣行事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知是否屬實,但我僅憑這種懷疑,就會當作確實那樣行事。

passages.original: He holds me well, The better shall my purpose work on him.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇重我,我嘅計謀就更容易喺佢身上奏效。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看重我,我的計謀就更容易在他身上奏效。

passages.original: Cassio’s a proper man.
passages.vernacular: 凱西奧係個英俊嘅男人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凱西奧是個英俊的男人。

passages.original: Let me see now, To get his place, and to plume up my will In double knavery. How, how? Let’s see.
passages.vernacular: 讓我諗諗,奪取佢嘅位置,並用雙重奸計滿足我嘅意願。點做?讓我睇睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我想想,奪取他的位置,並用雙重奸計滿足我的意願。怎麼做?讓我看看。

passages.original: After some time, to abuse Othello’s ear That he is too familiar with his wife.
passages.vernacular: 過啲時候,欺騙奧賽羅嘅耳朵,話佢同佢妻子太親密。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過些時候,欺騙奧賽羅的耳朵,說他與他妻子太親密。

passages.original: He hath a person and a smooth dispose, To be suspected, fram’d to make women false.
passages.vernacular: 佢有外表同圓滑嘅風度,容易被懷疑,生來就係令女人不忠嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有外表和圓滑的風度,容易被懷疑,生來就是使女人不忠的。

passages.original: The Moor is of a free and open nature That thinks men honest that but seem to be so, And will as tenderly be led by the nose As asses are. I have’t.
passages.vernacular: 摩爾人性格坦率開放,認為只要睇起來誠實嘅人就係誠實,並且會像驢一樣溫順地被牽著鼻子走。我有喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 摩爾人性格坦率開放,認為只要看起來誠實的人就是誠實,並且會像驢一樣溫順地被牽著鼻子走。我有了。

passages.original: It is engender’d.
passages.vernacular: 已經孕育成喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 已經孕育成了。

passages.original: Hell and night Must bring this monstrous birth to the world’s light.
passages.vernacular: 地獄同黑夜必須把呢個怪胎帶到世界嘅光明中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 地獄與黑夜必須把這個怪胎帶到世界的光明中。

passages.original: [Exit.]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene I — A Seaport in Cyprus 第二幕第一場:塞浦路斯海港

passages.original: Enter Montano and two Gentlemen.
passages.vernacular: [蒙塔諾同兩位紳士上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [蒙塔諾和兩位紳士上。]

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: What from the cape can you discern at sea?
passages.vernacular: 從海角你能喺海上睇到咩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從海角你能在海上看到什麼?

passages.title: First Gentleman 第一紳士
passages.original: Nothing at all, it is a high-wrought flood.
passages.vernacular: 完全睇唔到,海浪洶湧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 完全看不到,海浪洶湧。

passages.original: I cannot ’twixt the heaven and the main Descry a sail.
passages.vernacular: 我喺天同海之間睇唔到一張帆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在天和海之間看不到一張帆。

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: Methinks the wind hath spoke aloud at land.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得風喺陸地上已大聲講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得風在陸地上已大聲說話。

passages.original: A fuller blast ne’er shook our battlements.
passages.vernacular: 從未有更猛烈嘅風吹動我哋嘅城垛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從未有更猛烈的風吹動我們的城垛。

passages.original: If it hath ruffian’d so upon the sea, What ribs of oak, when mountains melt on them, Can hold the mortise?
passages.vernacular: 如果佢喺海上也咁肆虐,咩橡木船肋,喺山一般嘅巨浪傾倒其上時,能保持榫卯不裂?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果它在海上也這樣肆虐,什麼橡木船肋,在山一般的巨浪傾倒其上時,能保持榫卯不裂?

passages.original: What shall we hear of this?
passages.vernacular: 我哋會聽到咩消息?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們會聽到什麼消息?

passages.title: Second Gentleman 第二紳士
passages.original: A segregation of the Turkish fleet.
passages.vernacular: 土耳其艦隊被衝散。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 土耳其艦隊被衝散。

passages.original: For do but stand upon the foaming shore, The chidden billow seems to pelt the clouds, The wind-shak’d surge, with high and monstrous main, Seems to cast water on the burning Bear, And quench the guards of the ever-fixed pole;
passages.vernacular: 只要企喺泡沫翻滾嘅岸邊,被責罵嘅浪濤彷彿喺擊打雲層,被風搖撼嘅巨浪,高聳而可怕嘅海面,彷彿向燃燒嘅大熊星座潑水,熄滅永不移動嘅北極星嘅護衛星;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要站在泡沫翻滾的岸邊,被責罵的浪濤彷彿在擊打雲層,被風搖撼的巨浪,高聳而可怕的海面,彷彿向燃燒的大熊星座潑水,熄滅永不移動的北極星的護衛星;

passages.original: I never did like molestation view On the enchafed flood.
passages.vernacular: 我從未見過激怒嘅海面上有咁樣嘅騷動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從未見過激怒的海面上有這樣的騷動。

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: If that the Turkish fleet Be not enshelter’d, and embay’d, they are drown’d.
passages.vernacular: 如果土耳其艦隊冇搵到庇護、駛入海灣,佢哋都已淹死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果土耳其艦隊沒找到庇護、駛入海灣,他們都已淹死。

passages.original: It is impossible to bear it out.
passages.vernacular: 不可能承受得住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不可能承受得住。

passages.original: Enter a third Gentleman.
passages.vernacular: [第三位紳士上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [第三位紳士上。]

passages.title: Third Gentleman 第三紳士
passages.original: News, lads!
passages.vernacular: 有消息喇,小夥子哋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有消息了,小夥子們!

passages.original: Our wars are done.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅戰事結束喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的戰事結束了。

passages.original: The desperate tempest hath so bang’d the Turks That their designment halts.
passages.vernacular: 呢場絕望嘅風暴把土耳其人打得咁慘,佢哋嘅計劃停頓喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這場絕望的風暴把土耳其人打得這麼慘,他們的計劃停頓了。

passages.original: A noble ship of Venice Hath seen a grievous wreck and sufferance On most part of their fleet.
passages.vernacular: 一艘威尼斯嘅高貴船隻,親眼見到佢哋大部分艦隊遭受慘重嘅沉船同災難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一艘威尼斯的高貴船隻,親眼見到他們大部分艦隊遭受慘重的沉船與災難。

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: How?
passages.vernacular: 點?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼?

passages.original: Is this true?
passages.vernacular: 呢個係真嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是真的嗎?

passages.title: Third Gentleman 第三紳士
passages.original: The ship is here put in, A Veronessa; Michael Cassio, Lieutenant to the warlike Moor Othello, Is come on shore;
passages.vernacular: 船已駛入港口,係一艘威羅納船;邁克爾·凱西奧,好戰嘅摩爾人奧賽羅嘅副官,已上岸;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 船已駛入港口,是一艘威羅納船;邁克爾·凱西奧,好戰的摩爾人奧賽羅的副官,已上岸;

passages.original: the Moor himself at sea, And is in full commission here for Cyprus.
passages.vernacular: 摩爾人本人仲喺海上,佢全權受命來管理塞浦路斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 摩爾人本人還在海上,他全權受命來管理塞浦路斯。

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: I am glad on’t.
passages.vernacular: 我為此高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為此高興。

passages.original: ’Tis a worthy governor.
passages.vernacular: 佢係位出色嘅總督。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是位出色的總督。

passages.title: Third Gentleman 第三紳士
passages.original: But this same Cassio, though he speak of comfort Touching the Turkish loss, yet he looks sadly, And prays the Moor be safe;
passages.vernacular: 不過呢個凱西奧,雖然講到土耳其人嘅損失令人安慰,卻睇起來憂愁,並祈禱摩爾人平安;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過這個凱西奧,雖然說到土耳其人的損失令人安慰,卻看起來憂愁,並祈禱摩爾人平安;

passages.original: for they were parted With foul and violent tempest.
passages.vernacular: 因為佢哋喺惡劣猛烈嘅風暴中走散喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為他們在惡劣猛烈的風暴中走散了。

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: Pray heavens he be; For I have serv’d him, and the man commands Like a full soldier.
passages.vernacular: 願上天保佑佢平安;因為我曾為佢效勞,佢指揮起來像個真正嘅軍人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願上天保佑他平安;因為我曾為他效勞,他指揮起來像個真正的軍人。

passages.original: Let’s to the sea-side, ho!
passages.vernacular: 我哋去海邊,喂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們去海邊,喂!

passages.original: As well to see the vessel that’s come in As to throw out our eyes for brave Othello, Even till we make the main and the aerial blue An indistinct regard.
passages.vernacular: 既去睇進港嘅船,也要為勇敢嘅奧賽羅放眼遠望,直到海同空氣嘅藍色變成一片模糊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既去看進港的船,也要為勇敢的奧賽羅放眼遠望,直到海與空氣的藍色變成一片模糊。

passages.title: Third Gentleman 第三紳士
passages.original: Come, let’s do so; For every minute is expectancy Of more arrivance.
passages.vernacular: 來,我哋咁做;因為每一分鐘都期待更多船隻抵達。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,我們這樣做;因為每一分鐘都期待更多船隻抵達。

passages.original: Enter Cassio.
passages.vernacular: [凱西奧上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [凱西奧上。]

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Thanks you, the valiant of this warlike isle, That so approve the Moor!
passages.vernacular: 感謝你哋,呢個好戰島嶼上嘅勇士,如此推崇摩爾人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 感謝你們,這個好戰島嶼上的勇士,如此推崇摩爾人!

passages.original: O, let the heavens Give him defence against the elements, For I have lost him on a dangerous sea.
passages.vernacular: 啊,願上天保護佢抵禦自然力量,因為我喺一片危險嘅海上失去咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,願上天保護他抵禦自然力量,因為我在一片危險的海上失去了他。

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: Is he well shipp’d?
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅船好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的船好嗎?

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: His bark is stoutly timber’d, and his pilot Of very expert and approv’d allowance;
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅船木料結實,佢嘅領航員經驗豐富、得到認可;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的船木料結實,他的領航員經驗豐富、得到認可;

passages.original: Therefore my hopes, not surfeited to death, Stand in bold cure.
passages.vernacular: 所以我嘅希望冇被過度滿足而死,仍有大膽嘅康復把握。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我的希望沒被過度滿足而死,仍有大膽的康復把握。

passages.original: [Within.] A sail, a sail, a sail!
passages.vernacular: [內。]一張帆,一張帆,一張帆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: [內。]一張帆,一張帆,一張帆!

passages.original: Enter a Messenger.
passages.vernacular: [一位信使上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [一位信使上。]

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: What noise?
passages.vernacular: 咩聲音?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼聲音?

passages.title: Messenger 信使
passages.original: The town is empty; on the brow o’ the sea Stand ranks of people, and they cry “A sail!”
passages.vernacular: 城裡空咗;海邊高處站滿一排排人,佢哋喊「有帆!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 城裡空了;海邊高處站滿一排排人,他們喊「有帆!」

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: My hopes do shape him for the governor.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅希望認定佢係總督。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的希望認定他是總督。

passages.original: [A shot.]
passages.vernacular: [一聲炮響。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [一聲炮響。]

passages.title: Second Gentleman 第二紳士
passages.original: They do discharge their shot of courtesy.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋鳴放禮炮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們鳴放禮炮。

passages.original: Our friends at least.
passages.vernacular: 至少係我哋嘅朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至少是我們的朋友。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: I pray you, sir, go forth, And give us truth who ’tis that is arriv’d.
passages.vernacular: 請你,先生,出去睇睇,告訴我哋到底係誰到咗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你,先生,出去看看,告訴我們到底是誰到了。

passages.title: Second Gentleman 第二紳士
passages.original: I shall.
passages.vernacular: 我去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我去。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: But, good lieutenant, is your general wiv’d?
passages.vernacular: 不過,好副官,你嘅將軍結咗婚嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,好副官,你的將軍結婚了嗎?

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Most fortunately: he hath achiev’d a maid That paragons description and wild fame, One that excels the quirks of blazoning pens, And in the essential vesture of creation Does tire the ingener.
passages.vernacular: 非常幸運:佢贏得咗一位少女,佢超越任何描述同狂熱嘅名聲,勝過歌頌者筆下嘅巧思,在造物嘅本質衣裳之中,連創作者都疲於形容。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 非常幸運:他贏得了一位少女,她超越任何描述與狂熱的名聲,勝過歌頌者筆下的巧思,在造物的本質衣裳之中,連創作者都疲於形容。

passages.original: Enter second Gentleman.
passages.vernacular: [第二位紳士上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [第二位紳士上。]

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: How now?
passages.vernacular: 點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎樣?

passages.original: Who has put in?
passages.vernacular: 誰進港喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰進港了?

passages.title: Second Gentleman 第二紳士
passages.original: ’Tis one Iago, ancient to the general.
passages.vernacular: 係一位伊阿古,將軍嘅旗官。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是一位伊阿古,將軍的旗官。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: He has had most favourable and happy speed: Tempests themselves, high seas, and howling winds, The gutter’d rocks, and congregated sands, Traitors ensteep’d to clog the guiltless keel, As having sense of beauty, do omit Their mortal natures, letting go safely by The divine Desdemona.
passages.vernacular: 佢一路最順利愉快:風暴本身、大浪、呼嘯嘅風、鋸齒狀岩石、聚集嘅沙灘,呢啲浸在水下、阻礙無辜船龍骨嘅叛徒,彷彿懂得美,放棄咗佢哋致命嘅本性,讓神聖嘅戴絲德夢娜安全通過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他一路最順利愉快:風暴本身、大浪、呼嘯的風、鋸齒狀岩石、聚集的沙灘,這些浸在水下、阻礙無辜船龍骨的叛徒,彷彿懂得美,放棄了它們致命的本性,讓神聖的戴絲德夢娜安全通過。

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: What is she?
passages.vernacular: 佢係誰?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是誰?

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: She that I spake of, our great captain’s captain, Left in the conduct of the bold Iago;
passages.vernacular: 我講嘅嗰位,我哋偉大統帥嘅統帥,由勇敢嘅伊阿古護送;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說的那位,我們偉大統帥的統帥,由勇敢的伊阿古護送;

passages.original: Whose footing here anticipates our thoughts A se’nnight’s speed.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋登陸比我哋預想提前咗一個星期。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們登陸比我們預想提前了一周。

passages.original: Great Jove, Othello guard, And swell his sail with thine own powerful breath, That he may bless this bay with his tall ship, Make love’s quick pants in Desdemona’s arms, Give renew’d fire to our extincted spirits, And bring all Cyprus comfort!
passages.vernacular: 偉大嘅朱庇特,保佑奧賽羅,用你強大嘅氣息鼓滿佢嘅帆,令佢嘅高大船隻賜福呢片海灣,在戴絲德夢娜嘅懷抱中做愛嘅急促喘息,畀我哋熄滅嘅精神添上新火,畀整個塞浦路斯帶來安慰!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 偉大的朱庇特,保佑奧賽羅,用你強大的氣息鼓滿他的帆,使他的高大船隻賜福這片海灣,在戴絲德夢娜的懷抱中做愛的急促喘息,給我們熄滅的精神添上新火,給整個塞浦路斯帶來安慰!

passages.original: Enter Desdemona, Iago, Roderigo, and Emilia.
passages.vernacular: [戴絲德夢娜、伊阿古、羅德利哥同愛米利亞上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [戴絲德夢娜、伊阿古、羅德利哥和愛米利亞上。]

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: O, behold, The riches of the ship is come on shore!
passages.vernacular: 啊,睇,船上嘅珍寶登岸喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,看,船上的珍寶登岸了!

passages.original: Ye men of Cyprus, let her have your knees.
passages.vernacular: 塞浦路斯嘅男人哋,向佢跪拜吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 塞浦路斯的男人們,向她跪拜吧。

passages.original: Hail to thee, lady!
passages.vernacular: 向你致敬,小姐!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 向你致敬,小姐!

passages.original: and the grace of heaven, Before, behind thee, and on every hand, Enwheel thee round!
passages.vernacular: 願天恩在你前、後同四周環繞你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願天恩在你前、後和四周環繞你!

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: I thank you, valiant Cassio.
passages.vernacular: 謝謝你,勇敢嘅凱西奧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 謝謝你,勇敢的凱西奧。

passages.original: What tidings can you tell me of my lord?
passages.vernacular: 你能告訴我我丈夫嘅咩消息?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能告訴我我丈夫的什麼消息?

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: He is not yet arrived, nor know I aught But that he’s well, and will be shortly here.
passages.vernacular: 佢仲未到,我只知道佢安好,好快會到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他還沒到,我只知道他安好,很快會到。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: O, but I fear—How lost you company?
passages.vernacular: 啊,但我擔心——你哋點失散嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,但我擔心——你們怎麼失散的?

passages.original: [Within.] A sail, a sail!
passages.vernacular: [內。]有帆,有帆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: [內。]有帆,有帆!

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: The great contention of the sea and skies Parted our fellowship. But, hark! a sail.
passages.vernacular: 海同天嘅大搏鬥令我哋失散。不過,聽!有帆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 海與天的大搏鬥使我們失散。不過,聽!有帆。

passages.original: [Guns within.]
passages.vernacular: [內有炮聲。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [內有炮聲。]

passages.title: Second Gentleman 第二紳士
passages.original: They give their greeting to the citadel.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋向城堡致敬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們向城堡致敬。

passages.original: This likewise is a friend.
passages.vernacular: 呢個也係朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這也是朋友。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: See for the news.
passages.vernacular: 去睇消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去看消息。

passages.original: [Exit Gentleman.]
passages.vernacular: [紳士下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [紳士下。]

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Good ancient, you are welcome.
passages.vernacular: 好旗官,歡迎你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好旗官,歡迎你。

passages.original: [To Emilia.]
passages.vernacular: [對愛米利亞。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對愛米利亞。]

passages.original: Welcome, mistress.
passages.vernacular: 歡迎,夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歡迎,夫人。

passages.original: Let it not gall your patience, good Iago, That I extend my manners;
passages.vernacular: 好伊阿古,請唔好因我過分周到而惹你惱怒;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好伊阿古,請不要因我過分周到而惹你惱怒;

passages.original: ’tis my breeding That gives me this bold show of courtesy.
passages.vernacular: 係我嘅教養令我如此大膽地表示禮貌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是我的教養使我如此大膽地表示禮貌。

passages.original: [Kissing her.]
passages.vernacular: [吻佢。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [吻她。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Sir, would she give you so much of her lips As of her tongue she oft bestows on me, You would have enough.
passages.vernacular: 先生,如果佢肯畀你好似畀我嗰啲咁多舌頭一樣多嘅嘴唇,你就受夠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,如果她肯給你像給我那麼多舌頭一樣多的嘴唇,你就受夠了。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Alas, she has no speech.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,佢冇話講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,她沒話說。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: In faith, too much.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,太多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,太多了。

passages.original: I find it still when I have list to sleep.
passages.vernacular: 當我想瞓覺時,總係發現呢點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我想睡覺時,總是發現這點。

passages.original: Marry, before your ladyship, I grant, She puts her tongue a little in her heart, And chides with thinking.
passages.vernacular: 當然,喺小姐你面前,我承認,佢會把舌頭稍微收進心裡,只用思想責備。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,在小姐你面前,我承認,她會把舌頭稍微收進心裡,只用思想責備。

passages.title: Emilia 愛米利亞
passages.original: You have little cause to say so.
passages.vernacular: 你冇咩理由咁講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你沒什麼理由這樣說。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Come on, come on; you are pictures out of doors, Bells in your parlours, wild-cats in your kitchens, Saints in your injuries, devils being offended, Players in your housewifery, and housewives in your beds.
passages.vernacular: 得啦,得啦;你哋出門像畫像,喺客廳像鈴鐺,喺廚房像野貓,受傷害時像聖人,被冒犯時像魔鬼,做家務像演戲,在床上先像主婦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 得了,得了;你們出門像畫像,在客廳像鈴鐺,在廚房像野貓,受傷害時像聖人,被冒犯時像魔鬼,做家務像演戲,在床上才像主婦。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: O, fie upon thee, slanderer!
passages.vernacular: 啊,呸,你呢個誹謗者!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,呸,你這個誹謗者!

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Nay, it is true, or else I am a Turk.
passages.vernacular: 唔,呢個係真嘅,否則我就係土耳其人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,這是真的,否則我就是土耳其人。

passages.original: You rise to play, and go to bed to work.
passages.vernacular: 你哋起床玩,上床工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們起床玩,上床工作。

passages.title: Emilia 愛米利亞
passages.original: You shall not write my praise.
passages.vernacular: 你唔准寫我嘅讚美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不許寫我的讚美。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: No, let me not.
passages.vernacular: 唔,唔畀我寫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,不讓我寫。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: What wouldst thou write of me, if thou shouldst praise me?
passages.vernacular: 如果你要讚美我,你會寫我咩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你要讚美我,你會寫我什麼?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: O gentle lady, do not put me to’t, For I am nothing if not critical.
passages.vernacular: 啊溫柔嘅小姐,唔好逼我,因為我唔挑剔就咩都唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊溫柔的小姐,不要逼我,因為我不挑剔就什麼都不是。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Come on, assay.—There’s one gone to the harbour?
passages.vernacular: 來,試試。——有人去咗港口嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,試試。——有人去港口了嗎?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Ay, madam.
passages.vernacular: 去咗,夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去了,夫人。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: I am not merry, but I do beguile The thing I am, by seeming otherwise.— Come, how wouldst thou praise me?
passages.vernacular: 我唔開心,但我用表面嘅假象欺騙我嘅真實處境。——來,你點讚美我?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不開心,但我用表面的假象欺騙我的真實處境。——來,你怎麼讚美我?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: I am about it, but indeed, my invention Comes from my pate as birdlime does from frieze, It plucks out brains and all:
passages.vernacular: 我正在諗,不過其實,我嘅靈感從腦袋出嚟,就像粘鳥膠從粗呢上拉出,連腦子一齊扯出嚟:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我正在想,不過其實,我的靈感從腦袋出來,就像粘鳥膠從粗呢上拉出,連腦子一起扯出來:

passages.original: but my Muse labours, And thus she is deliver’d.
passages.vernacular: 但我嘅繆斯在分娩,而家生下嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我的繆斯在分娩,現在生下來了。

passages.original: If she be fair and wise, fairness and wit, The one’s for use, the other useth it.
passages.vernacular: 佢若既美且慧,美貌同智慧,一個供使用,一個善用佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她若既美且慧,美貌與智慧,一個供使用,一個善用它。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Well prais’d!
passages.vernacular: 讚得好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讚得好!

passages.original: How if she be black and witty?
passages.vernacular: 如果佢黑而聰明呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她黑而聰明呢?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: If she be black, and thereto have a wit, She’ll find a white that shall her blackness fit.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢黑,又有智慧,佢會搵到一個白人,配得上佢嘅黑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她黑,又有智慧,她會找到一個白人,配得上她的黑。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Worse and worse.
passages.vernacular: 越來越差。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 越來越糟。

passages.title: Emilia 愛米利亞
passages.original: How if fair and foolish?
passages.vernacular: 如果美而愚蠢呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果美而愚蠢呢?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: She never yet was foolish that was fair, For even her folly help’d her to an heir.
passages.vernacular: 美麗嘅女人從未愚蠢過,因為連佢嘅愚蠢也幫佢生咗繼承人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美麗的女人從未愚蠢過,因為連她的愚蠢也幫她生了繼承人。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: These are old fond paradoxes to make fools laugh i’ the alehouse.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲係古老愚蠢嘅悖論,用嚟喺酒館逗傻瓜笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些是古老愚蠢的悖論,用來在酒館逗傻瓜笑。

passages.original: What miserable praise hast thou for her that’s foul and foolish?
passages.vernacular: 對又醜又蠢嘅女人,你有咩可憐嘅讚美?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對又醜又蠢的女人,你有什麼可憐的讚美?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: There’s none so foul and foolish thereunto, But does foul pranks which fair and wise ones do.
passages.vernacular: 冇又醜又蠢嘅女人,不做美麗聰明女人做嘅嗰啲壞事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有又醜又蠢的女人,不做美麗聰明女人做的那些壞事。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: O heavy ignorance!
passages.vernacular: 啊,沉重嘅無知!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,沉重的無知!

passages.original: Thou praisest the worst best.
passages.vernacular: 你把最壞嘅讚得最好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你把最壞的讚得最好。

passages.original: But what praise couldst thou bestow on a deserving woman indeed, one that in the authority of her merit did justly put on the vouch of very malice itself?
passages.vernacular: 但你對一位真正值得讚美嘅女人,能畀咩讚美?佢憑自己功德嘅權威,就連最惡意嘅人也不得不為佢作證。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你對一位真正值得讚美的女人,能給什麼讚美?她憑自己功德的權威,就連最惡意的人也不得不為她作證。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: She that was ever fair and never proud, Had tongue at will and yet was never loud, Never lack’d gold and yet went never gay, Fled from her wish, and yet said, “Now I may”;
passages.vernacular: 佢永遠美麗卻從不驕傲,言辭自如卻從不吵嚷,從不缺金卻從不炫耀,逃避自己嘅願望,卻講「而家我可以喇」;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她永遠美麗卻從不驕傲,言辭自如卻從不吵嚷,從不缺金卻從不炫耀,逃避自己的願望,卻說「現在我可以了」;

passages.original: She that, being anger’d, her revenge being nigh, Bade her wrong stay and her displeasure fly;
passages.vernacular: 佢被激怒時,報復近在咫尺,卻吩咐自己嘅委屈留下、不悅飛走;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她被激怒時,報復近在咫尺,卻吩咐自己的委屈留下、不悅飛走;

passages.original: She that in wisdom never was so frail To change the cod’s head for the salmon’s tail;
passages.vernacular: 佢智慧上從不軟弱到要用鱈魚頭換鮭魚尾;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她智慧上從不軟弱到要用鱈魚頭換鮭魚尾;

passages.original: She that could think and ne’er disclose her mind, See suitors following and not look behind;
passages.vernacular: 佢能思考卻從不透露心意,見追求者跟隨也不回頭;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她能思考卻從不透露心意,見追求者跟隨也不回頭;

passages.original: She was a wight, if ever such wight were—
passages.vernacular: 佢係個人物,如果真有咁樣嘅人物——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是個人物,如果真有這樣的人物——

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: To do what?
passages.vernacular: 去做咩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去做什麼?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: To suckle fools and chronicle small beer.
passages.vernacular: 去餵養傻瓜同記錄小事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去餵養傻瓜和記錄小事。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: O most lame and impotent conclusion!—Do not learn of him, Emilia, though he be thy husband.—How say you, Cassio?
passages.vernacular: 啊,最跛足無力嘅結論!——唔好向佢學,愛米利亞,雖然佢係你丈夫。——你點講,凱西奧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,最跛足無力的結論!——不要向他學,愛米利亞,雖然他是你丈夫。——你怎麼說,凱西奧?

passages.original: is he not a most profane and liberal counsellor?
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係一位最粗俗、最放肆嘅顧問嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不是一位最粗俗、最放肆的顧問嗎?

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: He speaks home, madam.
passages.vernacular: 佢講話直中要害,夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說話直中要害,夫人。

passages.original: You may relish him more in the soldier than in the scholar.
passages.vernacular: 你更能欣賞佢作為軍人,而唔係作為學者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你更能欣賞他作為軍人,而不是作為學者。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]

passages.original: He takes her by the palm.
passages.vernacular: 佢握住佢嘅手掌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他握住她的手掌。

passages.original: Ay, well said, whisper.
passages.vernacular: 好,講得好,低聲細語吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,說得好,低聲細語吧。

passages.original: With as little a web as this will I ensnare as great a fly as Cassio.
passages.vernacular: 我用咁小嘅一張網,就能網住凱西奧咁大嘅蒼蠅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我用這麼小的一張網,就能網住凱西奧這樣的大蒼蠅。

passages.original: Ay, smile upon her, do.
passages.vernacular: 對,對佢微笑,笑吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,對她微笑,笑吧。

passages.original: I will gyve thee in thine own courtship.
passages.vernacular: 我要用你自己嘅殷勤把你鎖住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要用你自己的殷勤把你鎖住。

passages.original: You say true, ’tis so, indeed.
passages.vernacular: 你講得對,確實如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說得對,確實如此。

passages.original: If such tricks as these strip you out of your lieutenantry, it had been better you had not kissed your three fingers so oft, which now again you are most apt to play the sir in.
passages.vernacular: 如果呢類把戲令你丟掉副官職位,你最好冇常常親吻你嘅三個手指——而家你又好樂意擺出大人姿態喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果這類把戲使你丟掉副官職位,你最好沒常常親吻你的三個手指——現在你又很樂意擺出大人姿態了。

passages.original: Very good; well kissed, an excellent courtesy!
passages.vernacular: 好好;吻得好,極好嘅禮節!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很好;吻得好,極好的禮節!

passages.original: ’Tis so, indeed.
passages.vernacular: 確實如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實如此。

passages.original: Yet again your fingers to your lips?
passages.vernacular: 又把手指放到嘴唇上?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又把手指放到嘴唇上?

passages.original: Would they were clyster-pipes for your sake!
passages.vernacular: 但願佢哋係灌腸管,為咗你好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但願它們是灌腸管,為了你好!

passages.original: [Trumpets within.]
passages.vernacular: [內有號角聲。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [內有號角聲。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: The Moor!
passages.vernacular: 摩爾人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 摩爾人!

passages.original: I know his trumpet.
passages.vernacular: 我認得佢嘅號角。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我認得他的號角。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: ’Tis truly so.
passages.vernacular: 確實如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實如此。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Let’s meet him, and receive him.
passages.vernacular: 我哋去迎接佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們去迎接他。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Lo, where he comes!
passages.vernacular: 睇,佢來喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看,他來了!

passages.original: Enter Othello and Attendants.
passages.vernacular: [奧賽羅同侍從哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧賽羅和侍從們上。]

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: O my fair warrior!
passages.vernacular: 啊我嘅美麗戰士!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊我的美麗戰士!

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: My dear Othello!
passages.vernacular: 我親愛嘅奧賽羅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我親愛的奧賽羅!

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: It gives me wonder great as my content To see you here before me.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢度先見到你,令我驚奇嘅程度,同我嘅滿足一樣大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這裡先見到你,使我驚奇的程度,和我的滿足一樣大。

passages.original: O my soul’s joy!
passages.vernacular: 啊我靈魂嘅喜悅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊我靈魂的喜悅!

passages.original: If after every tempest come such calms, May the winds blow till they have waken’d death!
passages.vernacular: 如果每場風暴之後都有咁樣嘅平靜,願風吹到驚醒死神為止!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果每場風暴之後都有這樣的平靜,願風吹到驚醒死神為止!

passages.original: And let the labouring bark climb hills of seas Olympus-high, and duck again as low As hell’s from heaven!
passages.vernacular: 讓辛苦嘅船爬上奧林匹斯嗰樣高嘅浪山,再俯衝落去,低如地獄離天堂嗰麼低!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓辛苦的船爬上奧林匹斯那樣高的浪山,再俯衝下去,低如地獄離天堂那麼低!

passages.original: If it were now to die, ’Twere now to be most happy, for I fear My soul hath her content so absolute That not another comfort like to this Succeeds in unknown fate.
passages.vernacular: 如果而家就死,嗰就係而家最幸福,因為我擔心我嘅靈魂已獲得如此絕對嘅滿足,喺未知嘅命運中,唔會再有同樣嘅安慰接續而來。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果現在就死,那就是現在最幸福,因為我擔心我的靈魂已獲得如此絕對的滿足,在未知的命運中,不會再有同樣的安慰接續而來。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: The heavens forbid But that our loves and comforts should increase Even as our days do grow!
passages.vernacular: 願上天禁止我哋嘅愛同安慰不隨日子一同增長!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願上天禁止我們的愛和安慰不隨日子一同增長!

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Amen to that, sweet powers!
passages.vernacular: 阿們,甜美嘅諸神!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿們,甜美的諸神!

passages.original: I cannot speak enough of this content.
passages.vernacular: 我講唔盡呢份滿足。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說不盡這份滿足。

passages.original: It stops me here; it is too much of joy: And this, and this, the greatest discords be [They kiss.]
passages.vernacular: 佢堵住我嘅喉嚨;歡喜太多喇:呢個,呢個,係我哋嘅心將要產生嘅最大不和諧 [二人接吻。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它堵住我的喉嚨;歡喜太多了:這個,這個,是我們的心將要產生的最大不和諧 [二人接吻。]

passages.original: That e’er our hearts shall make!
passages.vernacular: 係我哋嘅心曾經製造嘅最大不和諧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是我們的心曾經製造的最大不和諧!

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]

passages.original: O, you are well tun’d now, But I’ll set down the pegs that make this music, As honest as I am.
passages.vernacular: 啊,你哋而家音調和諧,但我要鬆下發出呢段音樂嘅琴栓,雖然我係咁誠實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,你們現在音調和諧,但我要鬆下發出這段音樂的琴栓,雖然我是這麼誠實。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Come, let us to the castle.— News, friends, our wars are done, the Turks are drown’d.
passages.vernacular: 來,我哋去城堡。——朋友哋,好消息,我哋嘅戰爭結束喇,土耳其人淹死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,我們去城堡。——朋友們,好消息,我們的戰爭結束了,土耳其人淹死了。

passages.original: How does my old acquaintance of this isle?
passages.vernacular: 呢個島上我嘅老相識哋好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個島上我的老相識們好嗎?

passages.original: Honey, you shall be well desir’d in Cyprus; I have found great love amongst them.
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅,你在塞浦路斯會受到歡迎;我在佢哋當中得到好多愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的,你在塞浦路斯會受到歡迎;我在他們當中得到很多愛。

passages.original: O my sweet, I prattle out of fashion, and I dote In mine own comforts.—I prithee, good Iago, Go to the bay and disembark my coffers.
passages.vernacular: 啊我嘅甜心,我講話不合常規,沉醉在自己嘅幸福裡。——請你,好伊阿古,去海灣把我嘅箱子卸落嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊我的甜心,我說話不合常規,沉醉在自己的幸福裡。——請你,好伊阿古,去海灣把我的箱子卸下來。

passages.original: Bring thou the master to the citadel; He is a good one, and his worthiness Does challenge much respect.—Come, Desdemona, Once more well met at Cyprus.
passages.vernacular: 把船長帶到城堡;佢係個好人,佢嘅品格值得好多尊重。——來,戴絲德夢娜,再次喺塞浦路斯相聚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把船長帶到城堡;他是個好人,他的品格值得很多尊重。——來,戴絲德夢娜,再次在塞浦路斯相聚。

passages.original: [Exeunt Othello, Desdemona and Attendants.]
passages.vernacular: [奧賽羅、戴絲德夢娜同侍從哋下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧賽羅、戴絲德夢娜和侍從們下。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Do thou meet me presently at the harbour.
passages.vernacular: 你立刻到港口與我會面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你立刻到港口與我會面。

passages.original: Come hither.
passages.vernacular: 過嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過來。

passages.original: If thou be’st valiant—as, they say, base men being in love have then a nobility in their natures more than is native to them—list me.
passages.vernacular: 如果你勇敢——據講卑賤嘅人戀愛時,天性中會有超過本性嘅高貴——聽我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你勇敢——據說卑賤的人戀愛時,天性中會有超過本性的高貴——聽我說。

passages.original: The lieutenant tonight watches on the court of guard:
passages.vernacular: 副官今晚喺警衛室值夜:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 副官今晚在警衛室值夜:

passages.original: first, I must tell thee this: Desdemona is directly in love with him.
passages.vernacular: 首先,我必須告訴你呢點:戴絲德夢娜直接愛上了佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首先,我必須告訴你這點:戴絲德夢娜直接愛上了他。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: With him?
passages.vernacular: 愛佢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛他?

passages.original: Why, ’tis not possible.
passages.vernacular: 咦,不可能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,不可能。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Lay thy finger thus, and let thy soul be instructed.
passages.vernacular: 把手指咁樣放著,讓你嘅靈魂受教。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把手指這樣放著,讓你的靈魂受教。

passages.original: Mark me with what violence she first loved the Moor, but for bragging, and telling her fantastical lies.
passages.vernacular: 留意佢起初係幾猛烈咁愛上摩爾人,只因佢吹噓,對佢講啲離奇嘅謊話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 留意她起初是多麼猛烈地愛上摩爾人,只因他吹噓,對她說些離奇的謊話。

passages.original: And will she love him still for prating?
passages.vernacular: 佢會繼續因為佢嘅胡講而愛佢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她會繼續因為他的胡說而愛他嗎?

passages.original: Let not thy discreet heart think it.
passages.vernacular: 唔好讓你審慎嘅心咁諗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要讓你審慎的心這樣想。

passages.original: Her eye must be fed.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛必須得到滋養。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的眼睛必須得到滋養。

passages.original: And what delight shall she have to look on the devil?
passages.vernacular: 睇住魔鬼,佢有咩樂趣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看著魔鬼,她有什麼樂趣?

passages.original: When the blood is made dull with the act of sport, there should be, again to inflame it and to give satiety a fresh appetite, loveliness in favour, sympathy in years, manners, and beauties;
passages.vernacular: 當血氣因歡愛而變得遲鈍時,為咗重新點燃佢,畀饜足一個新嘅胃口,必須有外貌嘅可愛、年齡、舉止同美貌嘅相配;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當血氣因歡愛而變得遲鈍時,為了重新點燃它,給饜足一個新的胃口,必須有外貌的可愛、年齡、舉止和美貌的相配;

passages.original: all which the Moor is defective in: now, for want of these required conveniences, her delicate tenderness will find itself abused, begin to heave the gorge, disrelish and abhor the Moor, very nature will instruct her in it, and compel her to some second choice.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲摩爾人都有缺陷:而家,由於缺乏呢啲必要嘅便利,佢細膩溫柔嘅心會發現自己受咗騙,開始作嘔,厭惡並憎恨摩爾人,天性本身會教佢,並迫使佢做第二次選擇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些摩爾人都有缺陷:現在,由於缺乏這些必要的便利,她細膩溫柔的心會發現自己受了騙,開始作嘔,厭惡並憎恨摩爾人,天性本身會教她,並迫使她做第二次選擇。

passages.original: Now sir, this granted (as it is a most pregnant and unforced position) who stands so eminently in the degree of this fortune as Cassio does?
passages.vernacular: 而家,先生,既然承認呢點(呢個係個極有講服力、毫不牽強嘅論點),誰比凱西奧更突出地處於呢個機遇嘅位置?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,先生,既然承認這點(這是個極有說服力、毫不牽強的論點),誰比凱西奧更突出地處於這個機遇的位置?

passages.original: a knave very voluble; no further conscionable than in putting on the mere form of civil and humane seeming, for the better compassing of his salt and most hidden loose affection?
passages.vernacular: 一個口才極好嘅惡棍;佢嘅良心僅限於扮出文明人道嘅外表,以便更好地達到佢好色而隱秘嘅放蕩情慾?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個口才極好的惡棍;他的良心僅限於扮出文明人道的外表,以便更好地達到他好色而隱祕的放蕩情慾?

passages.original: Why, none, why, none!
passages.vernacular: 咦,冇,冇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,沒有,沒有!

passages.original: A slipper and subtle knave, a finder out of occasions;
passages.vernacular: 一個油滑狡猾嘅惡棍,尋找機會嘅人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個油滑狡猾的惡棍,尋找機會的人;

passages.original: that has an eye can stamp and counterfeit advantages, though true advantage never present itself: a devilish knave!
passages.vernacular: 佢有雙眼睛,即使真正嘅好處從未出現,也能偽造製造好處:真係個魔鬼般嘅惡棍!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有雙眼睛,即使真正的好處從未出現,也能偽造製造好處:真是個魔鬼般的惡棍!

passages.original: Besides, the knave is handsome, young, and hath all those requisites in him that folly and green minds look after.
passages.vernacular: 此外,呢個惡棍英俊、年輕,具備愚蠢同不成熟之心所尋求嘅一切條件。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此外,這個惡棍英俊、年輕,具備愚蠢和不成熟之心所尋求的一切條件。

passages.original: A pestilent complete knave, and the woman hath found him already.
passages.vernacular: 一個瘟疫般徹頭徹尾嘅惡棍,而嗰女人已經發現咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個瘟疫般徹頭徹尾的惡棍,而那女人已經發現了他。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: I cannot believe that in her, she is full of most blessed condition.
passages.vernacular: 我唔能相信佢會咁樣,佢具備最有福嘅品性。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能相信她會這樣,她具備最有福的品性。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Blest fig’s end!
passages.vernacular: 有福個屁!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有福個屁!

passages.original: the wine she drinks is made of grapes: if she had been blessed, she would never have loved the Moor.
passages.vernacular: 佢飲嘅酒也係葡萄做嘅:如果佢有福,就絕唔會愛上摩爾人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她喝的酒也是葡萄做的:如果她有福,就絕不會愛上摩爾人。

passages.original: Blessed pudding!
passages.vernacular: 有福嘅布丁!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有福的布丁!

passages.original: Didst thou not see her paddle with the palm of his hand?
passages.vernacular: 你冇睇到佢用手指撥弄佢嘅手掌嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你沒看到她用手指撥弄他的手掌嗎?

passages.original: Didst not mark that?
passages.vernacular: 你冇留意到嗰個嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你沒留意到那個嗎?

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Yes, that I did.
passages.vernacular: 有,我睇到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有,我看到。

passages.original: But that was but courtesy.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰只係禮貌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那只是禮貌。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Lechery, by this hand.
passages.vernacular: 淫蕩,憑呢隻手發誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 淫蕩,憑這隻手發誓。

passages.original: An index and obscure prologue to the history of lust and foul thoughts.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係情慾同骯髒思想歷史嘅索引同隱晦序幕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是情慾與骯髒思想歷史的索引和隱晦序幕。

passages.original: They met so near with their lips that their breaths embrac’d together.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋嘴唇靠得咁近,連氣息都擁抱在一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們嘴唇靠得這麼近,連氣息都擁抱在一起。

passages.original: Villainous thoughts, Roderigo!
passages.vernacular: 卑鄙嘅想法,羅德利哥!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 卑鄙的想法,羅德利哥!

passages.original: When these mutualities so marshal the way, hard at hand comes the master and main exercise, the incorporate conclusion. Pish!
passages.vernacular: 當呢啲互相親密嘅舉動咁樣開路,緊隨而來嘅就係主要嘅正劇,肉體結合嘅結局。呸!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當這些互相親密的舉動這樣開路,緊隨而來的就是主要的正劇,肉體結合的結局。呸!

passages.original: But, sir, be you ruled by me.
passages.vernacular: 不過,先生,你聽我安排。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,先生,你聽我安排。

passages.original: I have brought you from Venice.
passages.vernacular: 我把你從威尼斯帶來。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把你從威尼斯帶來。

passages.original: Watch you tonight.
passages.vernacular: 你今晚守夜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你今晚守夜。

passages.original: For the command, I’ll lay’t upon you.
passages.vernacular: 指揮權,我交畀你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 指揮權,我交給你。

passages.original: Cassio knows you not.
passages.vernacular: 凱西奧唔認識你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凱西奧不認識你。

passages.original: I’ll not be far from you.
passages.vernacular: 我唔會離你太遠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不會離你太遠。

passages.original: Do you find some occasion to anger Cassio, either by speaking too loud, or tainting his discipline, or from what other course you please, which the time shall more favourably minister.
passages.vernacular: 你搵個機會激怒凱西奧,大聲講話,或詆毀佢嘅紀律,或用你認為更合適嘅任何方式,時機會更有利地提供。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你找個機會激怒凱西奧,大聲說話,或詆毀他的紀律,或用你認為更合適的任何方式,時機會更有利地提供。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Well.
passages.vernacular: 好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Sir, he is rash, and very sudden in choler, and haply with his truncheon may strike at you:
passages.vernacular: 先生,佢魯莽,發怒好突然,也許會用警棍打你:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,他魯莽,發怒很突然,也許會用警棍打你:

passages.original: provoke him that he may, for even out of that will I cause these of Cyprus to mutiny, whose qualification shall come into no true taste again but by the displanting of Cassio.
passages.vernacular: 激佢咁做,因為憑此我可以令塞浦路斯人發動叛亂,佢哋嘅平息,除非罷免凱西奧,否則唔會恢復真正嘅平靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 激他這樣做,因為憑此我可以讓塞浦路斯人發動叛亂,他們的平息,除非罷免凱西奧,否則不會恢復真正的平靜。

passages.original: So shall you have a shorter journey to your desires by the means I shall then have to prefer them, and the impediment most profitably removed, without the which there were no expectation of our prosperity.
passages.vernacular: 咁你通往願望嘅路程會更短,因為我屆時有辦法推進佢哋,而最大嘅障礙也會最有利地被清除,冇呢個障礙,我哋就冇成功嘅希望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣你通往願望的路程會更短,因為我屆時有辦法推進它們,而最大的障礙也會最有利地被清除,沒有這個障礙,我們就沒有成功的希望。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: I will do this, if I can bring it to any opportunity.
passages.vernacular: 我會咁做,如果我能搵到機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會這樣做,如果我能找到機會。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: I warrant thee.
passages.vernacular: 我向你保證。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我向你保證。

passages.original: Meet me by and by at the citadel: I must fetch his necessaries ashore. Farewell.
passages.vernacular: 待會兒喺城堡與我會面:我必須把佢嘅必需品拎上岸。再見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 待會兒在城堡與我會面:我必須把他的必需品拿上岸。再見。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Adieu.
passages.vernacular: 再見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: That Cassio loves her, I do well believe it; That she loves him, ’tis apt, and of great credit:
passages.vernacular: 凱西奧愛佢,我完全相信;佢愛凱西奧,也好合理,非常可信:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凱西奧愛她,我完全相信;她愛凱西奧,也很合理,非常可信:

passages.original: The Moor, howbeit that I endure him not, Is of a constant, loving, noble nature;
passages.vernacular: 摩爾人,雖然我忍受唔到佢,卻具有堅定、深情、高貴嘅天性;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 摩爾人,雖然我忍受不了他,卻具有堅定、深情、高貴的天性;

passages.original: And, I dare think, he’ll prove to Desdemona A most dear husband.
passages.vernacular: 我敢諗,佢會成為戴絲德夢娜最親愛嘅丈夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我敢想,他會成為戴絲德夢娜最親愛的丈夫。

passages.original: Now, I do love her too, Not out of absolute lust (though peradventure I stand accountant for as great a sin) But partly led to diet my revenge, For that I do suspect the lusty Moor Hath leap’d into my seat.
passages.vernacular: 而家,我也愛佢,唔係完全出於情慾(雖然也許我也要為同樣大嘅罪負責),而一部分係為咗滋養我嘅復仇,因為我懷疑嗰好色嘅摩爾人曾跳上我嘅位置。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,我也愛她,不是完全出於情慾(雖然也許我也要為同樣大的罪負責),而一部分是為了滋養我的復仇,因為我懷疑那好色的摩爾人曾跳上我的位置。

passages.original: The thought whereof Doth, like a poisonous mineral, gnaw my inwards, And nothing can or shall content my soul Till I am even’d with him, wife for wife, Or, failing so, yet that I put the Moor At least into a jealousy so strong That judgement cannot cure.
passages.vernacular: 呢個想法好似有毒嘅礦物一樣啃噬我嘅內臟,冇嘢能夠、也唔會滿足我嘅靈魂,直到我同佢扯平,以妻還妻,或者如果做唔到,至少令摩爾人陷入一種強烈到理智無法治癒嘅嫉妒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這想法像有毒的礦物一樣啃噬我的內臟,什麼都不能、也不會滿足我的靈魂,直到我與他扯平,以妻還妻,或者如果做不到,至少讓摩爾人陷入一種強烈到理智無法治癒的嫉妒。

passages.original: Which thing to do, If this poor trash of Venice, whom I trash For his quick hunting, stand the putting on, I’ll have our Michael Cassio on the hip, Abuse him to the Moor in the rank garb (For I fear Cassio with my night-cap too) Make the Moor thank me, love me, and reward me For making him egregiously an ass And practicing upon his peace and quiet Even to madness.
passages.vernacular: 為達此目的,如果呢個威尼斯嘅可憐渣滓(我因佢獵取得太急而勒住佢)經得起推動,我就要抓住我哋嘅邁克爾·凱西奧嘅把柄,喺摩爾人面前用最惡劣嘅方式中傷佢(因為我也擔心凱西奧與我嘅睡帽有染),令摩爾人感謝我、愛我、獎賞我,因為我令佢成為一頭極端愚蠢嘅驢,並圖謀佢嘅安寧,直到發瘋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為達此目的,如果這個威尼斯的可憐渣滓(我因他獵取得太急而勒住他)經得起推動,我就要抓住我們的邁克爾·凱西奧的把柄,在摩爾人面前用最惡劣的方式中傷他(因為我也擔心凱西奧與我的睡帽有染),讓摩爾人感謝我、愛我、獎賞我,因為我使他成為一頭極端愚蠢的驢,並圖謀他的安寧,直到發瘋。

passages.original: ’Tis here, but yet confus’d.
passages.vernacular: 計謀喺度,但仲混亂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 計謀在這裡,但還混亂。

passages.original: Knavery’s plain face is never seen till us’d.
passages.vernacular: 奸詐嘅真面目,要等到使用時先睇到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奸詐的真面目,要等到使用時才看見。

passages.original: [Exit.]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene II — A Street 第二幕第二場:街道

passages.original: Enter Othello’s Herald with a proclamation.
passages.vernacular: [奧賽羅嘅傳令官持公告上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧賽羅的傳令官持公告上。]

passages.title: Herald 傳令官
passages.original: It is Othello’s pleasure, our noble and valiant general, that upon certain tidings now arrived, importing the mere perdition of the Turkish fleet, every man put himself into triumph:
passages.vernacular: 奧賽羅將軍(我哋高貴勇敢嘅統帥)有令,鑑於剛收到消息,土耳其艦隊已全軍覆沒,每個人都應慶祝勝利:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奧賽羅將軍(我們高貴勇敢的統帥)有令,鑑於剛收到消息,土耳其艦隊已全軍覆沒,每個人都應慶祝勝利:

passages.original: some to dance, some to make bonfires, each man to what sport and revels his addition leads him.
passages.vernacular: 有嘅跳舞,有嘅點篝火,每人各按自己嘅喜好去消遣狂歡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有的跳舞,有的點篝火,每人各按自己的喜好去消遣狂歡。

passages.original: For besides these beneficial news, it is the celebration of his nuptial.
passages.vernacular: 因為除咗呢啲喜訊之外,仲係佢婚禮嘅慶典。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為除了這些喜訊之外,還是他婚禮的慶典。

passages.original: So much was his pleasure should be proclaimed.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅意願就係咁多,要我宣告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的意願就是這麼多,要我宣告。

passages.original: All offices are open, and there is full liberty of feasting from this present hour of five till the bell have told eleven.
passages.vernacular: 所有廚房酒窖大開,從而家五點起,到鐘敲十一點為止,人人可自由宴飲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有廚房酒窖大開,從現在五點起,到鐘敲十一點為止,人人可自由宴飲。

passages.original: Heaven bless the isle of Cyprus and our noble general Othello!
passages.vernacular: 願上天保佑塞浦路斯島同我哋高貴嘅統帥奧賽羅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願上天保佑塞浦路斯島和我們高貴的統帥奧賽羅!

passages.original: [Exit.]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene III — A Hall in the Castle 第二幕第三場:城堡大廳

passages.original: Enter Othello, Desdemona, Cassio and Attendants.
passages.vernacular: [奧賽羅、戴絲德夢娜、凱西奧同侍從哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧賽羅、戴絲德夢娜、凱西奧和侍從們上。]

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Good Michael, look you to the guard tonight.
passages.vernacular: 好邁克爾,今晚你負責睇守警衛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好邁克爾,今晚你負責看守警衛。

passages.original: Let’s teach ourselves that honourable stop, Not to outsport discretion.
passages.vernacular: 讓我哋自己學會嗰種體面嘅節制,唔好玩樂到失去分寸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我們自己學會那種體面的節制,不要玩樂到失去分寸。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Iago hath direction what to do.
passages.vernacular: 伊阿古已有指示該點做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 伊阿古已有指示該怎麼做。

passages.original: But notwithstanding with my personal eye Will I look to’t.
passages.vernacular: 不過儘管如此,我仍然會親自去察睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過儘管如此,我還是會親自去察看。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Iago is most honest.
passages.vernacular: 伊阿古最誠實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 伊阿古最誠實。

passages.original: Michael, good night.
passages.vernacular: 邁克爾,晚安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 邁克爾,晚安。

passages.original: Tomorrow with your earliest Let me have speech with you.
passages.vernacular: 明日請你儘早來,讓我同你傾傾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明天請你儘早來,讓我與你談談。

passages.original: [To Desdemona.]
passages.vernacular: [對戴絲德夢娜。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對戴絲德夢娜。]

passages.original: Come, my dear love, The purchase made, the fruits are to ensue;
passages.vernacular: 來,我親愛嘅愛人,買賣已經成交,成果就要來喇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,我親愛的愛人,買賣已經成交,成果就要來了;

passages.original: That profit’s yet to come ’tween me and you.— Good night.
passages.vernacular: 嗰利潤仲有待你我之間來臨。——晚安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那利潤還有待你我之間來臨。——晚安。

passages.original: [Exeunt Othello, Desdemona and Attendants.]
passages.vernacular: [奧賽羅、戴絲德夢娜同侍從哋下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧賽羅、戴絲德夢娜和侍從們下。]

passages.original: Enter Iago.
passages.vernacular: [伊阿古上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [伊阿古上。]

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Welcome, Iago.
passages.vernacular: 歡迎,伊阿古。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歡迎,伊阿古。

passages.original: We must to the watch.
passages.vernacular: 我哋要去守夜喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們要去守夜了。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Not this hour, lieutenant.
passages.vernacular: 仲未到,副官。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還不到,副官。

passages.original: ’Tis not yet ten o’ th’ clock.
passages.vernacular: 仲未到十點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還沒到十點。

passages.original: Our general cast us thus early for the love of his Desdemona;
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅將軍咁早打發我哋,係出於對佢嘅戴絲德夢娜嘅愛;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的將軍這麼早打發我們,是出於對他的戴絲德夢娜的愛;

passages.original: who let us not therefore blame: he hath not yet made wanton the night with her;
passages.vernacular: 所以我哋唔好怪佢:佢仲未同佢一齊令夜晚放蕩起來;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我們不要怪他:他還沒有與她一起讓夜晚放蕩起來;

passages.original: and she is sport for Jove.
passages.vernacular: 而佢係朱庇特嘅玩物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而她是朱庇特的玩物。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: She’s a most exquisite lady.
passages.vernacular: 佢係位極精緻嘅小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是位極精緻的小姐。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: And, I’ll warrant her, full of game.
passages.vernacular: 而且我敢擔保,佢充滿情趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我敢擔保,她充滿情趣。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Indeed, she is a most fresh and delicate creature.
passages.vernacular: 確實,佢係個最清新嬌嫩嘅人兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實,她是個最清新嬌嫩的人兒。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: What an eye she has!
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛幾咁美!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的眼睛多美!

passages.original: methinks it sounds a parley to provocation.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得佢發出挑逗嘅談判信號。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得它發出挑逗的談判信號。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: An inviting eye, and yet methinks right modest.
passages.vernacular: 一雙邀請嘅眼睛,但我覺得卻又相當端莊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一雙邀請的眼睛,但我覺得卻又相當端莊。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: And when she speaks, is it not an alarm to love?
passages.vernacular: 佢講嘢嘅時候,唔係向愛情發出警報嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說話的時候,不是向愛情發出警報嗎?

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: She is indeed perfection.
passages.vernacular: 佢確實完美。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她確實完美。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Well, happiness to their sheets!
passages.vernacular: 好,祝佢哋嘅床單幸福!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,祝他們的床單幸福!

passages.original: Come, lieutenant, I have a stoup of wine; and here without are a brace of Cyprus gallants that would fain have a measure to the health of black Othello.
passages.vernacular: 來,副官,我有一壺酒;門外有兩位塞浦路斯嘅勇士,好想乾一杯為黑奧賽羅祝福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,副官,我有一壺酒;門外有兩位塞浦路斯的勇士,很想乾一杯為黑奧賽羅祝福。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Not tonight, good Iago.
passages.vernacular: 今晚唔好,好伊阿古。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今晚不要,好伊阿古。

passages.original: I have very poor and unhappy brains for drinking.
passages.vernacular: 我酒量好差,腦袋好唔爭氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我酒量很差,腦袋很不爭氣。

passages.original: I could well wish courtesy would invent some other custom of entertainment.
passages.vernacular: 我真希望禮節能發明別嘅款待方式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望禮節能發明別的款待方式。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: O, they are our friends; but one cup: I’ll drink for you.
passages.vernacular: 啊,佢哋係我哋嘅朋友;就一杯:我替你飲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,他們是我們的朋友;就一杯:我替你喝。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: I have drunk but one cup tonight, and that was craftily qualified too, and behold, what innovation it makes here:
passages.vernacular: 我今晚只飲咗一杯,而且仲巧妙地兌咗水,你睇,佢喺度造成幾大變化:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我今晚只喝了一杯,而且還巧妙地兌了水,你看,它在這裡造成多大變化:

passages.original: I am unfortunate in the infirmity, and dare not task my weakness with any more.
passages.vernacular: 我不幸有呢個弱點,唔敢再勉強我嘅虛弱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不幸有這個弱點,不敢再勉強我的虛弱。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: What, man!
passages.vernacular: 咩,老兄!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,老兄!

passages.original: ’Tis a night of revels.
passages.vernacular: 今晚係狂歡之夜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今晚是狂歡之夜。

passages.original: The gallants desire it.
passages.vernacular: 勇士哋想咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勇士們想要這樣。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Where are they?
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺邊?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們在哪?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Here at the door.
passages.vernacular: 就喺門口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在門口。

passages.original: I pray you, call them in.
passages.vernacular: 請你叫佢哋入嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你叫他們進來。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: I’ll do’t; but it dislikes me.
passages.vernacular: 我去叫;不過我唔鍾意咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我去叫;不過我不喜歡這樣。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: If I can fasten but one cup upon him, With that which he hath drunk tonight already, He’ll be as full of quarrel and offence As my young mistress’ dog.
passages.vernacular: 如果我能把一杯酒硬灌畀佢,加上佢今晚已經飲嘅,佢就會像我小姐嘅小狗咁充滿爭吵同冒犯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我能把一杯酒硬灌給他,加上他今晚已經喝的,他就會像我小姐的小狗那樣充滿爭吵和冒犯。

passages.original: Now my sick fool Roderigo, Whom love hath turn’d almost the wrong side out, To Desdemona hath tonight carous’d Potations pottle-deep;
passages.vernacular: 而家我嗰害病嘅傻瓜羅德利哥,愛情幾乎把佢翻咗個底朝天,今晚為戴絲德夢娜乾杯,飲咗滿滿一大壺酒;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我那害病的傻瓜羅德利哥,愛情幾乎把他翻了個底朝天,今晚為戴絲德夢娜乾杯,喝了滿滿一大壺酒;

passages.original: and he’s to watch: Three lads of Cyprus, noble swelling spirits, That hold their honours in a wary distance, The very elements of this warlike isle, Have I tonight fluster’d with flowing cups, And they watch too.
passages.vernacular: 而佢要守夜:三位塞浦路斯青年,高貴而自負嘅人,與人保持謹慎嘅榮譽距離,係呢個好戰島嶼嘅真正元素,我今晚已用滿杯把佢哋灌得暈頭轉向,佢哋也要守夜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而他要守夜:三位塞浦路斯青年,高貴而自負的人,與人保持謹慎的榮譽距離,是這個好戰島嶼的真正元素,我今晚已用滿杯把他們灌得暈頭轉向,他們也要守夜。

passages.original: Now, ’mongst this flock of drunkards, Am I to put our Cassio in some action That may offend the isle.
passages.vernacular: 而家,喺呢群醉鬼當中,我要令我哋嘅凱西奧做出可能冒犯全島嘅行動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,在這群醉鬼當中,我要讓我們的凱西奧做出可能冒犯全島的行動。

passages.original: But here they come: If consequence do but approve my dream, My boat sails freely, both with wind and stream.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋來喇:如果後續發展證實我嘅夢想,我嘅船就會順風順水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他們來了:如果後續發展證實我的夢想,我的船就會順風順水。

passages.original: Enter Cassio, Montano and Gentlemen; followed by Servant with wine.
passages.vernacular: [凱西奧、蒙塔諾同紳士哋上;僕人持酒隨後。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [凱西奧、蒙塔諾和紳士們上;僕人持酒隨後。]

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: ’Fore God, they have given me a rouse already.
passages.vernacular: 憑上帝,佢哋已經灌咗我一大杯喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑上帝,他們已經灌了我一大杯了。

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: Good faith, a little one; not past a pint, as I am a soldier.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,只係一點點;唔超過一品脫,我以軍人身份擔保。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,只是一點點;不超過一品脫,我以軍人身份擔保。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Some wine, ho! [Sings.]
passages.vernacular: 拎酒來,喂![唱。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿酒來,喂![唱。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: And let me the cannikin clink, clink, And let me the cannikin clink, clink:
passages.vernacular: 讓我碰碰小酒杯,叮,叮,讓我碰碰小酒杯,叮,叮:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我碰碰小酒杯,叮,叮,讓我碰碰小酒杯,叮,叮:

passages.original: A soldier’s a man, O, man’s life’s but a span, Why then let a soldier drink.
passages.vernacular: 軍人也係人,啊,人生不過一掌寬,咁就讓軍人飲酒吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 軍人也是人,啊,人生不過一掌寬,那就讓軍人喝酒吧。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Some wine, boys!
passages.vernacular: 拎酒來,小子哋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿酒來,小子們!

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: ’Fore God, an excellent song.
passages.vernacular: 憑上帝,好歌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑上帝,好歌。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: I learned it in England, where indeed they are most potent in potting:
passages.vernacular: 我喺英格蘭學嘅,嗰度嘅人確實最擅長灌酒:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在英格蘭學的,那裡的人確實最擅長灌酒:

passages.original: your Dane, your German, and your swag-bellied Hollander,—drink, ho!—are nothing to your English.
passages.vernacular: 你哋嘅丹麥人、德國人,仲有大肚皮嘅荷蘭人——飲呀,喂!——都比唔上英格蘭人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們的丹麥人、德國人,還有大肚皮的荷蘭人——喝呀,喂!——都比不上英格蘭人。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Is your Englishman so expert in his drinking?
passages.vernacular: 你哋英格蘭人咁擅長飲酒嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們英格蘭人這麼擅長喝酒嗎?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Why, he drinks you, with facility, your Dane dead drunk;
passages.vernacular: 咦,佢輕易就能把你嘅丹麥人灌到爛醉;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,他輕易就能把你的丹麥人灌到爛醉;

passages.original: he sweats not to overthrow your Almain; he gives your Hollander a vomit ere the next pottle can be filled.
passages.vernacular: 佢不費力就能放倒你嘅德國人;在下一壺酒倒滿之前,佢就令荷蘭人嘔吐喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不費力就能放倒你的德國人;在下一壺酒倒滿之前,他就讓荷蘭人嘔吐了。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: To the health of our general!
passages.vernacular: 為我哋將軍嘅健康乾杯!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為我們將軍的健康乾杯!

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: I am for it, lieutenant; and I’ll do you justice.
passages.vernacular: 我贊成,副官;我奉陪到底。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我贊成,副官;我奉陪到底。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: O sweet England!
passages.vernacular: 啊,親愛嘅英格蘭!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,親愛的英格蘭!

passages.original: [Sings.]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: King Stephen was a worthy peer, His breeches cost him but a crown;
passages.vernacular: 斯蒂芬王係位可敬嘅貴族,佢嘅褲子只花咗一克朗;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯蒂芬王是位可敬的貴族,他的褲子只花了一克朗;

passages.original: He held them sixpence all too dear, With that he call’d the tailor lown.
passages.vernacular: 佢嫌嗰六便士太貴,因此罵裁縫係無賴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他嫌那六便士太貴,因此罵裁縫是無賴。

passages.original: He was a wight of high renown, And thou art but of low degree:
passages.vernacular: 佢係聲名顯赫嘅人,而你只係低微之輩:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是聲名顯赫的人,而你只是低微之輩:

passages.original: ’Tis pride that pulls the country down, Then take thine auld cloak about thee.
passages.vernacular: 係驕傲拖垮國家,所以披上你嗰件舊斗篷吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是驕傲拖垮國家,所以披上你那件舊斗篷吧。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Some wine, ho!
passages.vernacular: 拎酒來,喂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿酒來,喂!

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: ’Fore God, this is a more exquisite song than the other.
passages.vernacular: 憑上帝,呢首比剛才嗰首更精彩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑上帝,這首比剛才那首更精彩。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Will you hear ’t again?
passages.vernacular: 要再聽一遍嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要再聽一遍嗎?

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: No, for I hold him to be unworthy of his place that does those things.
passages.vernacular: 唔,因為我認為做呢啲事嘅人配唔上佢嘅職位。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,因為我認為做這些事的人配不上他的職位。

passages.original: Well, God’s above all, and there be souls must be saved, and there be souls must not be saved.
passages.vernacular: 好,上帝高於一切,有啲靈魂必須得救,有啲靈魂不得救。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,上帝高於一切,有些靈魂必須得救,有些靈魂不得救。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: It’s true, good lieutenant.
passages.vernacular: 冇錯,好副官。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒錯,好副官。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: For mine own part, no offence to the general, nor any man of quality, I hope to be saved.
passages.vernacular: 就我自己而言,對將軍或任何有身份嘅人冇冒犯,我希望得救。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就我自己而言,對將軍或任何有身份的人沒冒犯,我希望得救。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: And so do I too, lieutenant.
passages.vernacular: 我也係,副官。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也是,副官。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Ay, but, by your leave, not before me; the lieutenant is to be saved before the ancient.
passages.vernacular: 係,但恕我直講,唔能喺我之前;副官要比旗官先得救。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,但恕我直言,不能在我之前;副官要比旗官先得救。

passages.original: Let’s have no more of this; let’s to our affairs.
passages.vernacular: 唔好再講呢個;我哋去辦正事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別再說這個;我們去辦正事。

passages.original: Forgive us our sins!
passages.vernacular: 求主赦免我哋嘅罪!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 求主赦免我們的罪!

passages.original: Gentlemen, let’s look to our business.
passages.vernacular: 先生哋,我哋去辦我哋嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生們,我們去辦我們的事。

passages.original: Do not think, gentlemen, I am drunk.
passages.vernacular: 先生哋,唔好以為我醉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生們,不要以為我醉了。

passages.original: This is my ancient, this is my right hand, and this is my left.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我嘅旗官,呢個係我嘅右手,呢個係我嘅左手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我的旗官,這是我的右手,這是我的左手。

passages.original: I am not drunk now.
passages.vernacular: 我而家冇醉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在沒醉。

passages.original: I can stand well enough, and I speak well enough.
passages.vernacular: 我企得穩,也講得清。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我站得穩,也說得清。

passages.title: All 眾人
passages.original: Excellent well.
passages.vernacular: 好得很。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好得很。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Why, very well then.
passages.vernacular: 咦,咁就好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,那很好。

passages.original: You must not think, then, that I am drunk.
passages.vernacular: 咁你哋唔能以為我醉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那你們不能以為我醉了。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: To the platform, masters.
passages.vernacular: 去平台,各位。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去平台,各位。

passages.original: Come, let’s set the watch.
passages.vernacular: 來,我哋佈置崗哨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,我們佈置崗哨。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: You see this fellow that is gone before, He is a soldier fit to stand by Cæsar And give direction:
passages.vernacular: 你哋睇到剛才走咗嗰個人,佢係個配企喺凱撒身邊發號施令嘅軍人:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們看到剛才走了的那個人,他是個配站在凱撒身邊發號施令的軍人:

passages.original: and do but see his vice, ’Tis to his virtue a just equinox, The one as long as th’ other.
passages.vernacular: 再睇佢嘅惡習,與佢嘅美德剛好係晝夜等長,一樣長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再看他的惡習,與他的美德剛好是晝夜等長,一樣長。

passages.original: ’Tis pity of him.
passages.vernacular: 佢真可惜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他真可惜。

passages.original: I fear the trust Othello puts him in, On some odd time of his infirmity, Will shake this island.
passages.vernacular: 我擔心奧賽羅對佢嘅信任,在佢某個軟弱嘅時刻,會動搖呢座島。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我擔心奧賽羅對他的信任,在他某個軟弱的時刻,會動搖這座島。

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: But is he often thus?
passages.vernacular: 但佢經常咁樣嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他經常這樣嗎?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: ’Tis evermore the prologue to his sleep: He’ll watch the horologe a double set If drink rock not his cradle.
passages.vernacular: 呢個總係佢入睡嘅序幕:如果酒唔搖佢入睡,佢可以盯住時鐘走兩圈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這總是他入睡的序幕:如果酒不搖他入睡,他可以盯著時鐘走兩圈。

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: It were well The general were put in mind of it.
passages.vernacular: 最好提醒將軍呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最好提醒將軍這件事。

passages.original: Perhaps he sees it not, or his good nature Prizes the virtue that appears in Cassio, And looks not on his evils: is not this true?
passages.vernacular: 也許佢冇睇到,或者佢嘅好心性只睇重凱西奧表現出嘅美德,唔睇佢嘅惡習:唔係咁嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許他沒看到,或者他的好心性只看重凱西奧表現出的美德,不看他的惡習:不是這樣嗎?

passages.original: Enter Roderigo.
passages.vernacular: [羅德利哥上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅德利哥上。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: [Aside to him.]
passages.vernacular: [對佢旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對他旁白。]

passages.original: How now, Roderigo?
passages.vernacular: 點樣,羅德利哥?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼樣,羅德利哥?

passages.original: I pray you, after the lieutenant; go.
passages.vernacular: 請你跟住副官去;去吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你跟著副官去;去吧。

passages.original: [Exit Roderigo.]
passages.vernacular: [羅德利哥下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅德利哥下。]

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: And ’tis great pity that the noble Moor Should hazard such a place as his own second With one of an ingraft infirmity:
passages.vernacular: 高貴嘅摩爾人竟用一個天生有缺陷嘅人來擔任自己嘅副手,真係太可惜:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 高貴的摩爾人竟用一個天生有缺陷的人來擔任自己的副手,真是太可惜:

passages.original: It were an honest action to say so To the Moor.
passages.vernacular: 向摩爾人講明呢點,係正直嘅行為。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 向摩爾人說明這點,是正直的行為。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Not I, for this fair island.
passages.vernacular: 我唔會,哪怕為咗呢座美麗嘅島。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不會,哪怕為了這座美麗的島。

passages.original: I do love Cassio well and would do much To cure him of this evil. But, hark! What noise?
passages.vernacular: 我好鍾意凱西奧,願意盡力治好佢呢個毛病。不過,聽!咩聲音?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很喜歡凱西奧,願意盡力治好他這個毛病。不過,聽!什麼聲音?

passages.original: [Cry within: “Help! help!”]
passages.vernacular: [內喊:「救命!救命!」]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [內喊:「救命!救命!」]

passages.original: Enter Cassio, driving in Roderigo.
passages.vernacular: [凱西奧追打羅德利哥上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [凱西奧追打羅德利哥上。]

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Zounds, you rogue, you rascal!
passages.vernacular: 天啊,你呢個流氓,你呢個無賴!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天啊,你這個流氓,你這個無賴!

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: What’s the matter, lieutenant?
passages.vernacular: 點解,副官?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼回事,副官?

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: A knave teach me my duty!
passages.vernacular: 一個惡棍來教我職責!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個惡棍來教我職責!

passages.original: I’ll beat the knave into a twiggen bottle.
passages.vernacular: 我要把呢個惡棍打成柳條編嘅瓶子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要把這個惡棍打成柳條編的瓶子。

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: Beat me?
passages.vernacular: 打我?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 打我?

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Dost thou prate, rogue?
passages.vernacular: 你還敢多嘴,流氓?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你還敢多嘴,流氓?

passages.original: [Striking Roderigo.]
passages.vernacular: [打羅德利哥。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [打羅德利哥。]

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: Nay, good lieutenant; I pray you, sir, hold your hand.
passages.vernacular: 唔,好副官;請你,先生,住手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,好副官;請你,先生,住手。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Let me go, sir, Or I’ll knock you o’er the mazard.
passages.vernacular: 放開我,先生,否則我敲爛你嘅腦袋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 放開我,先生,否則我敲爛你的腦袋。

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: Come, come, you’re drunk.
passages.vernacular: 得啦,得啦,你醉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 得了,得了,你醉了。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Drunk?
passages.vernacular: 醉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醉?

passages.original: [They fight.]
passages.vernacular: [二人打鬥。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [二人打鬥。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: [Aside to Roderigo.]
passages.vernacular: [對羅德利哥旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對羅德利哥旁白。]

passages.original: Away, I say!
passages.vernacular: 走,我話!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走,我說!

passages.original: Go out and cry a mutiny.
passages.vernacular: 出去喊叛亂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 出去喊叛亂。

passages.original: [Exit Roderigo.]
passages.vernacular: [羅德利哥下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅德利哥下。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Nay, good lieutenant, God’s will, gentlemen.
passages.vernacular: 唔,好副官,天啊,各位先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,好副官,天啊,各位先生。

passages.original: Help, ho!—Lieutenant,—sir,—Montano,—sir:— Help, masters!
passages.vernacular: 救命,喂!——副官——先生——蒙塔諾——先生:——救命,各位!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 救命,喂!——副官——先生——蒙塔諾——先生:——救命,各位!

passages.original: Here’s a goodly watch indeed!
passages.vernacular: 好一個漂亮嘅崗哨啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好一個漂亮的崗哨啊!

passages.original: [A bell rings.]
passages.vernacular: [鐘響。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [鐘響。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Who’s that which rings the bell?—Diablo, ho!
passages.vernacular: 誰在敲鐘?——見鬼,喂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰在敲鐘?——見鬼,喂!

passages.original: The town will rise.
passages.vernacular: 全城會被驚醒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 全城會被驚醒。

passages.original: God’s will, lieutenant, hold, You will be sham’d forever.
passages.vernacular: 天啊,副官,住手,你會永遠蒙羞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天啊,副官,住手,你會永遠蒙羞。

passages.original: Enter Othello and Attendants.
passages.vernacular: [奧賽羅同侍從哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧賽羅和侍從們上。]

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: What is the matter here?
passages.vernacular: 呢度出咗咩事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡出了什麼事?

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: Zounds, I bleed still, I am hurt to the death.
passages.vernacular: 天啊,我仲喺度流血,我傷得快死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天啊,我還在流血,我傷得快死了。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Hold, for your lives!
passages.vernacular: 住手,要命嘅話!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 住手,要命的話!

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Hold, ho!
passages.vernacular: 住手,喂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 住手,喂!

passages.original: lieutenant,—sir,—Montano,—gentlemen,— Have you forgot all place of sense and duty? Hold!
passages.vernacular: 副官——先生——蒙塔諾——各位先生——你哋都忘咗理智同職責嘅本分嗎?住手!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 副官——先生——蒙塔諾——各位先生——你們都忘了理智和職責的本分嗎?住手!

passages.original: The general speaks to you; hold, hold, for shame!
passages.vernacular: 將軍在對你哋講嘢;住手,住手,不知羞恥!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 將軍在對你們說話;住手,住手,不知羞恥!

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Why, how now, ho!
passages.vernacular: 咦,點樣喇,喂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,怎麼了,喂!

passages.original: From whence ariseth this?
passages.vernacular: 呢個係從何而起?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是從何而起?

passages.original: Are we turn’d Turks, and to ourselves do that Which heaven hath forbid the Ottomites?
passages.vernacular: 我哋變成咗土耳其人,自己對自己做上天禁止奧斯曼人做嘅事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們變成了土耳其人,自己對自己做上天禁止奧斯曼人做的事?

passages.original: For Christian shame, put by this barbarous brawl:
passages.vernacular: 為咗基督徒嘅羞恥,停止呢場野蠻嘅鬥毆:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了基督徒的羞恥,停止這場野蠻的鬥毆:

passages.original: He that stirs next to carve for his own rage Holds his soul light; he dies upon his motion.
passages.vernacular: 誰接落去動手發洩怒火,就係視靈魂為輕;一動就死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰接下來動手發洩怒火,就是視靈魂為輕;一動就死。

passages.original: Silence that dreadful bell, it frights the isle From her propriety.
passages.vernacular: 讓嗰可怕嘅鐘聲靜落來,佢嚇得全島失去常態。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓那可怕的鐘聲靜下來,它嚇得全島失去常態。

passages.original: What is the matter, masters?
passages.vernacular: 點解,各位?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼回事,各位?

passages.original: Honest Iago, that looks dead with grieving, Speak, who began this?
passages.vernacular: 誠實嘅伊阿古,你悲痛得面如死灰,講,誰開始嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誠實的伊阿古,你悲痛得面如死灰,說,誰開始的?

passages.original: On thy love, I charge thee.
passages.vernacular: 憑你對我嘅愛,我命令你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑你對我的愛,我命令你。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: I do not know.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道。

passages.original: Friends all but now, even now, In quarter, and in terms like bride and groom Devesting them for bed;
passages.vernacular: 剛才還都係朋友,就在剛才,喺營房裡,像新娘新郎寬衣上床嗰樣友好;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 剛才還都是朋友,就在剛才,在營房裡,像新娘新郎寬衣上床那樣友好;

passages.original: and then, but now, As if some planet had unwitted men, Swords out, and tilting one at other’s breast, In opposition bloody.
passages.vernacular: 然後,就在剛才,彷彿某個行星令人失去理智,拔出劍,互相對住胸膛刺,流血對抗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,就在剛才,彷彿某個行星使人失去理智,拔出劍,互相對著胸膛刺,流血對抗。

passages.original: I cannot speak Any beginning to this peevish odds;
passages.vernacular: 我講唔出呢場愚蠢爭執嘅任何開端;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說不出這場愚蠢爭執的任何開端;

passages.original: And would in action glorious I had lost Those legs that brought me to a part of it!
passages.vernacular: 我寧願喺光榮嘅行動中失去嗰雙把我帶嚟參與其中嘅腿!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧願在光榮的行動中失去那雙把我帶來參與其中的腿!

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: How comes it, Michael, you are thus forgot?
passages.vernacular: 邁克爾,你點會咁失態?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 邁克爾,你怎麼會這樣失態?

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: I pray you, pardon me; I cannot speak.
passages.vernacular: 請原諒我;我講唔出口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請原諒我;我說不出口。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Worthy Montano, you were wont be civil.
passages.vernacular: 尊貴嘅蒙塔諾,你向來彬彬有禮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尊貴的蒙塔諾,你向來彬彬有禮。

passages.original: The gravity and stillness of your youth The world hath noted, and your name is great In mouths of wisest censure:
passages.vernacular: 你年輕時嘅莊重同沉靜,世人都有目共睹,你嘅名聲喺最明智嘅評論者口中好響亮:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你年輕時的莊重與沉靜,世人都有目共睹,你的名聲在最明智的評論者口中很響亮:

passages.original: what’s the matter, That you unlace your reputation thus, And spend your rich opinion for the name Of a night-brawler?
passages.vernacular: 呢個係點解,你竟咁解開你嘅名譽,把你豐厚嘅聲譽換成夜間鬥毆者嘅名聲?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是怎麼回事,你竟這樣解開你的名譽,把你豐厚的聲譽換成夜間鬥毆者的名聲?

passages.original: Give me answer to it.
passages.vernacular: 畀我答覆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我答覆。

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: Worthy Othello, I am hurt to danger.
passages.vernacular: 尊貴嘅奧賽羅,我傷得好危險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尊貴的奧賽羅,我傷得很危險。

passages.original: Your officer, Iago, can inform you, While I spare speech, which something now offends me, Of all that I do know;
passages.vernacular: 你嘅軍官伊阿古可以告訴你我所知道嘅一切,我省啲講嘢,而家講嘢有啲傷我;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的軍官伊阿古可以告訴你我所知道的一切,我省些說話,現在說話有點傷我;

passages.original: nor know I aught By me that’s said or done amiss this night, Unless self-charity be sometimes a vice, And to defend ourselves it be a sin When violence assails us.
passages.vernacular: 我也唔知道今晚我講過或做過咩不當嘅事,除非自我保護有時係惡行,當暴力襲來時自衛也係罪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也不知道今晚我說過或做過什麼不當的事,除非自我保護有時是惡行,當暴力襲來時自衛也是罪。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Now, by heaven, My blood begins my safer guides to rule, And passion, having my best judgement collied, Assays to lead the way.
passages.vernacular: 而家,憑天發誓,我嘅血氣開始支配我更穩妥嘅向導,激情已令我最好嘅判斷變得黯淡,試圖帶路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,憑天發誓,我的血氣開始支配我更穩妥的向導,激情已使我最好的判斷變得黯淡,試圖帶路。

passages.original: Zounds, if I stir, Or do but lift this arm, the best of you Shall sink in my rebuke.
passages.vernacular: 天啊,只要我一動,或只係舉起呢隻手臂,你哋當中最強嘅也會在我嘅斥責中沉淪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天啊,只要我一動,或只是舉起這隻手臂,你們當中最強的也會在我的斥責中沉淪。

passages.original: Give me to know How this foul rout began, who set it on, And he that is approv’d in this offence, Though he had twinn’d with me, both at a birth, Shall lose me. What!
passages.vernacular: 讓我知道呢場卑劣嘅混亂係點樣開始嘅,係誰挑起嘅,誰被證明在呢個冒犯中有份,即使佢與我係同胎雙生,也會失去我。咩!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我知道這場卑劣的混亂是怎樣開始的,是誰挑起的,誰被證明在這冒犯中有份,即使他與我是同胎雙生,也會失去我。什麼!

passages.original: in a town of war, Yet wild, the people’s hearts brimful of fear, To manage private and domestic quarrel, In night, and on the court and guard of safety?
passages.vernacular: 在一座戰爭中嘅城市,仍然動盪,人民心中充滿恐懼,卻在夜裡,在警衛崗位上,鬧私人同家庭嘅爭吵?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在一座戰爭中的城市,仍然動盪,人民心中充滿恐懼,卻在夜裡,在警衛崗位上,鬧私人和家庭的爭吵?

passages.original: ’Tis monstrous.
passages.vernacular: 太荒唐喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太荒唐了。

passages.original: Iago, who began’t?
passages.vernacular: 伊阿古,誰開嘅頭?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 伊阿古,誰開的頭?

passages.title: Montano 蒙塔諾
passages.original: If partially affin’d, or leagu’d in office, Thou dost deliver more or less than truth, Thou art no soldier.
passages.vernacular: 如果你因偏袒或同僚情誼而多講或少講咗真相,你就唔係軍人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你因偏袒或同僚情誼而多說或少說了真相,你就不是軍人。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Touch me not so near.
passages.vernacular: 唔好咁樣刺痛我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別這樣刺痛我。

passages.original: I had rather have this tongue cut from my mouth Than it should do offence to Michael Cassio.
passages.vernacular: 我寧願割掉呢條舌頭,也唔願佢冒犯邁克爾·凱西奧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧願割掉這條舌頭,也不願它冒犯邁克爾·凱西奧。

passages.original: Yet I persuade myself, to speak the truth Shall nothing wrong him.
passages.vernacular: 然而我講服自己,講出真相唔會冤枉佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而我說服自己,說出真相不會冤枉他。

passages.original: Thus it is, general: Montano and myself being in speech, There comes a fellow crying out for help, And Cassio following him with determin’d sword, To execute upon him.
passages.vernacular: 事情係咁嘅,將軍:蒙塔諾同我正在交談,來咗一個喊救命嘅人,凱西奧拎住出鞘嘅劍追住佢,要處置佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事情是這樣的,將軍:蒙塔諾和我正在交談,來了一個喊救命的人,凱西奧拿著出鞘的劍追著他,要處置他。

passages.original: Sir, this gentleman Steps in to Cassio and entreats his pause.
passages.vernacular: 先生,呢位紳士上前勸凱西奧停手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,這位紳士上前勸凱西奧停手。

passages.original: Myself the crying fellow did pursue, Lest by his clamour (as it so fell out) The town might fall in fright:
passages.vernacular: 我自己去追嗰個喊叫嘅人,怕佢嘅喊聲(結果真係如此)嚇壞全城:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我自己去追那個喊叫的人,怕他的喊聲(結果真是如此)嚇壞全城:

passages.original: he, swift of foot, Outran my purpose: and I return’d the rather For that I heard the clink and fall of swords, And Cassio high in oath, which till tonight I ne’er might say before.
passages.vernacular: 佢腿快,跑過咗我嘅意圖:我就折回,尤其因為我聽到劍嘅碰撞同倒地聲,仲有凱西奧高聲發誓,呢個係我今晚之前從未聽過嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他腿快,跑過了我的意圖:我就折回,尤其因為我聽到劍的碰撞和倒地聲,還有凱西奧高聲發誓,這是我今晚之前從未聽過的。

passages.original: When I came back, (For this was brief) I found them close together, At blow and thrust, even as again they were When you yourself did part them.
passages.vernacular: 我回來時(因為呢個好短暫),發現佢哋緊貼在一起,又在刺又在砍,就像你本人把佢哋分開時嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我回來時(因為這很短暫),發現他們緊貼在一起,又在刺又在砍,就像你本人把他們分開時那樣。

passages.original: More of this matter cannot I report.
passages.vernacular: 呢件事我再多講唔到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這件事我再多說不了。

passages.original: But men are men; the best sometimes forget; Though Cassio did some little wrong to him, As men in rage strike those that wish them best, Yet surely Cassio, I believe, receiv’d From him that fled some strange indignity, Which patience could not pass.
passages.vernacular: 但人終究係人;最好嘅人有時也會忘形;雖然凱西奧對佢有啲小冒犯,就像人在怒火中會打嗰啲最希望佢哋好嘅人,但我相信凱西奧確實受咗嗰個逃走者嘅某種奇怪侮辱,係耐心也無法忍受嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但人終究是人;最好的人有時也會忘形;雖然凱西奧對他有些小冒犯,就像人在怒火中會打那些最希望他們好的人,但我相信凱西奧確實受了那個逃走者的某種奇怪侮辱,是耐心也無法忍受的。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: I know, Iago, Thy honesty and love doth mince this matter, Making it light to Cassio.
passages.vernacular: 我知道,伊阿古,你嘅誠實同愛護把呢件事淡化喇,對凱西奧從輕處理。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道,伊阿古,你的誠實和愛護把這件事淡化了,對凱西奧從輕處理。

passages.original: Cassio, I love thee, But never more be officer of mine.
passages.vernacular: 凱西奧,我愛你,但你再也唔係我嘅軍官喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凱西奧,我愛你,但你再也不是我的軍官了。

passages.original: Enter Desdemona, attended.
passages.vernacular: [戴絲德夢娜在侍從陪同下上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [戴絲德夢娜在侍從陪同下上。]

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
