passages.original: Look, if my gentle love be not rais’d up!
passages.vernacular: 睇,我溫柔嘅愛人是否也被吵醒喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看,我溫柔的愛人是否也被吵醒了!

passages.original: I’ll make thee an example.
passages.vernacular: 我要拎你做榜樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要拿你做榜樣。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: What’s the matter?
passages.vernacular: 點解?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了?

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: All’s well now, sweeting; come away to bed.
passages.vernacular: 而家一切都好,親愛嘅;返去瞓吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在一切都好,親愛的;回去睡吧。

passages.original: Sir, for your hurts, myself will be your surgeon.
passages.vernacular: 先生,你嘅傷,我自己做你嘅外科醫生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,你的傷,我自己做你的外科醫生。

passages.original: Lead him off.
passages.vernacular: 帶佢落去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 帶他下去。

passages.original: [Montano is led off.]
passages.vernacular: [蒙塔諾被帶下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [蒙塔諾被帶下。]

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Iago, look with care about the town, And silence those whom this vile brawl distracted.
passages.vernacular: 伊阿古,小心巡視城鎮,安撫嗰啲被呢場卑劣鬥毆驚擾嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 伊阿古,小心巡視城鎮,安撫那些被這場卑劣鬥毆驚擾的人。

passages.original: Come, Desdemona: ’tis the soldiers’ life To have their balmy slumbers wak’d with strife.
passages.vernacular: 來,戴絲德夢娜:軍人嘅生活就係香甜嘅睡眠被爭鬥驚醒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,戴絲德夢娜:軍人的生活就是香甜的睡眠被爭鬥驚醒。

passages.original: [Exeunt all but Iago and Cassio.]
passages.vernacular: [除伊阿古同凱西奧外,眾人下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [除伊阿古和凱西奧外,眾人下。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: What, are you hurt, lieutenant?
passages.vernacular: 咩,你受傷了嗎,副官?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼,你受傷了嗎,副官?

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Ay, past all surgery.
passages.vernacular: 係,傷得無法醫治。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,傷得無法醫治。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Marry, Heaven forbid!
passages.vernacular: 天啊,但願唔係!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天啊,但願不是!

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Reputation, reputation, reputation!
passages.vernacular: 名譽,名譽,名譽!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 名譽,名譽,名譽!

passages.original: O, I have lost my reputation!
passages.vernacular: 啊,我失去咗我嘅名譽!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,我失去了我的名譽!

passages.original: I have lost the immortal part of myself, and what remains is bestial.
passages.vernacular: 我失去咗自己不朽嘅部分,剩低嘅只係獸性。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我失去了自己不朽的部分,剩下的只是獸性。

passages.original: My reputation, Iago, my reputation!
passages.vernacular: 我嘅名譽,伊阿古,我嘅名譽!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的名譽,伊阿古,我的名譽!

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: As I am an honest man, I thought you had received some bodily wound;
passages.vernacular: 我以誠實人嘅身份講,我以為你受咗身體嘅傷;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以誠實人的身份說,我以為你受了身體的傷;

passages.original: there is more sense in that than in reputation.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個比名譽更有意義。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那比名譽更有意義。

passages.original: Reputation is an idle and most false imposition, oft got without merit and lost without deserving.
passages.vernacular: 名譽係一種無聊而極虛假嘅強加之物,往往無功而得,無過而失。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 名譽是一種無聊而極虛假的強加之物,往往無功而得,無過而失。

passages.original: You have lost no reputation at all, unless you repute yourself such a loser.
passages.vernacular: 你根本冇失去名譽,除非你自己認為你失去咗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你根本沒失去名譽,除非你自己認為你失去了。

passages.original: What, man, there are ways to recover the general again:
passages.vernacular: 老兄,總有辦法重新贏返將軍:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老兄,總有辦法重新贏回將軍:

passages.original: you are but now cast in his mood, a punishment more in policy than in malice, even so as one would beat his offenceless dog to affright an imperious lion:
passages.vernacular: 你不過係而家處於佢嘅怒氣中,呢個係出於政策而非惡意嘅懲罰,就像人為咗嚇唬威嚴嘅獅子而打無辜嘅狗:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不過是現在處於他的怒氣中,這是出於政策而非惡意的懲罰,就像人為了嚇唬威嚴的獅子而打無辜的狗:

passages.original: sue to him again, and he’s yours.
passages.vernacular: 再去求佢,佢就係你嘅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再去求他,他就是你的了。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: I will rather sue to be despised than to deceive so good a commander with so slight, so drunken, and so indiscreet an officer. Drunk?
passages.vernacular: 我寧願求人鄙視我,也唔願用咁輕浮、醉酒、不慎重嘅軍官去欺騙咁好嘅指揮官。醉?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧願求人鄙視我,也不願用這麼輕浮、醉酒、不慎重的軍官去欺騙這麼好的指揮官。醉?

passages.original: and speak parrot?
passages.vernacular: 仲要像鸚鵡般胡言亂語?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還像鸚鵡般胡言亂語?

passages.original: and squabble? swagger? swear?
passages.vernacular: 仲要吵架?吹牛?咒罵?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還吵架?吹牛?咒罵?

passages.original: and discourse fustian with one’s own shadow?
passages.vernacular: 仲要對住自己嘅影子講大話?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還對著自己的影子說大話?

passages.original: O thou invisible spirit of wine, if thou hast no name to be known by, let us call thee devil!
passages.vernacular: 啊,你呢個睇唔到嘅酒精,如果你冇可稱呼嘅名字,就讓我哋叫你魔鬼!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,你這個看不到的酒精,如果你沒有可稱呼的名字,就讓我們叫你魔鬼!

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: What was he that you followed with your sword?
passages.vernacular: 你用劍追嗰個人係誰?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你用劍追的那人是誰?

passages.original: What had he done to you?
passages.vernacular: 佢對你做咗啲咩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他對你做了什麼?

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: I know not.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Is’t possible?
passages.vernacular: 有可能嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有可能嗎?

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: I remember a mass of things, but nothing distinctly;
passages.vernacular: 我記得好多事,但都唔清楚;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我記得很多事,但都不清楚;

passages.original: a quarrel, but nothing wherefore.
passages.vernacular: 一場爭吵,但唔知為咗咩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一場爭吵,但不知為了什麼。

passages.original: O God, that men should put an enemy in their mouths to steal away their brains!
passages.vernacular: 啊上帝,人竟然把仇敵放進嘴裡來偷走自己嘅腦子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊上帝,人竟然把仇敵放進嘴裡來偷走自己的腦子!

passages.original: That we should with joy, pleasance, revel, and applause, transform ourselves into beasts!
passages.vernacular: 我哋竟然帶住喜悅、歡樂、狂歡同喝彩,把自己變成野獸!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們竟然帶著喜悅、歡樂、狂歡和喝彩,把自己變成野獸!

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Why, but you are now well enough: how came you thus recovered?
passages.vernacular: 咦,但你而家好好嘅:你點恢復得咁快?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,但你現在好好的:你怎麼恢復得這麼快?

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: It hath pleased the devil drunkenness to give place to the devil wrath.
passages.vernacular: 酒鬼魔鬼讓位畀憤怒魔鬼喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 酒鬼魔鬼讓位給憤怒魔鬼了。

passages.original: One unperfectness shows me another, to make me frankly despise myself.
passages.vernacular: 一個缺陷向我顯示另一個,令我坦率地鄙視自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個缺陷向我顯示另一個,使我坦率地鄙視自己。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Come, you are too severe a moraler.
passages.vernacular: 得啦,你太嚴苛嘅道德家喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 得了,你太嚴苛的道德家了。

passages.original: As the time, the place, and the condition of this country stands, I could heartily wish this had not befallen;
passages.vernacular: 按此時此地同呢個國家嘅情況,我真心希望呢件事冇發生;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 按此時此地和這個國家的情況,我真心希望這事沒有發生;

passages.original: but since it is as it is, mend it for your own good.
passages.vernacular: 但既然已經咁樣,就為你自己嘅好處去補救吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但既然已經這樣,就為你自己的好處去補救吧。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: I will ask him for my place again; he shall tell me I am a drunkard!
passages.vernacular: 我要再向佢討返我嘅職位;佢會話我係個酒鬼!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要再向他討回我的職位;他會說我是個酒鬼!

passages.original: Had I as many mouths as Hydra, such an answer would stop them all.
passages.vernacular: 即使我有九頭蛇咁多張嘴,咁樣一個答案也會堵住佢哋全部。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使我有九頭蛇那麼多張嘴,這樣一個答案也會堵住它們全部。

passages.original: To be now a sensible man, by and by a fool, and presently a beast! O strange!
passages.vernacular: 而家係明理嘅人,一會兒係傻瓜,轉眼係野獸!啊,奇怪!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在是明理的人,一會兒是傻瓜,轉眼是野獸!啊,奇怪!

passages.original: Every inordinate cup is unbless’d, and the ingredient is a devil.
passages.vernacular: 每一杯過量嘅酒都係不蒙祝福嘅,裡面嘅成分係魔鬼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每一杯過量的酒都是不蒙祝福的,裡面的成分是魔鬼。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Come, come, good wine is a good familiar creature, if it be well used.
passages.vernacular: 得啦,得啦,好酒係好伙伴,只要適當使用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 得了,得了,好酒是好伙伴,只要適當使用。

passages.original: Exclaim no more against it.
passages.vernacular: 唔好再咒罵佢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要再咒罵它了。

passages.original: And, good lieutenant, I think you think I love you.
passages.vernacular: 好副官,我想你知道我愛你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好副官,我想你知道我愛你。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: I have well approved it, sir.—I drunk!
passages.vernacular: 我已充分驗證,先生。——我醉!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已充分驗證,先生。——我醉!

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: You, or any man living, may be drunk at a time, man.
passages.vernacular: 你,或任何活著嘅人,都可能一時醉倒,老兄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你,或任何活著的人,都可能一時醉倒,老兄。

passages.original: I’ll tell you what you shall do.
passages.vernacular: 我告訴你該點做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴你該怎麼做。

passages.original: Our general’s wife is now the general; I may say so in this respect, for that he hath devoted and given up himself to the contemplation, mark, and denotement of her parts and graces.
passages.vernacular: 我哋將軍嘅妻子而家就係將軍;我可以咁講,因為佢已把自己奉獻畀對佢嘅品質同優雅嘅凝視、留意同記錄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們將軍的妻子現在就是將軍;我可以這麼說,因為他已把自己奉獻給對她的品質與優雅的凝視、留意和記錄。

passages.original: Confess yourself freely to her.
passages.vernacular: 向佢坦白認錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 向她坦白認錯。

passages.original: Importune her help to put you in your place again.
passages.vernacular: 懇求佢幫忙令你恢復職位。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 懇求她幫忙讓你恢復職位。

passages.original: She is of so free, so kind, so apt, so blessed a disposition, she holds it a vice in her goodness not to do more than she is requested.
passages.vernacular: 佢性情如此慷慨、善良、敏捷、有福,佢認為如果唔做得比請求嘅更多,就係佢善良中嘅缺點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她性情如此慷慨、善良、敏捷、有福,她認為如果不做得比請求的更多,就是她善良中的缺點。

passages.original: This broken joint between you and her husband entreat her to splinter, and, my fortunes against any lay worth naming, this crack of your love shall grow stronger than it was before.
passages.vernacular: 請佢為你同佢丈夫之間呢個斷裂嘅關節上夾板,我拎我嘅運氣打賭任何值得一提嘅賭注,你哋愛情嘅呢道裂縫會比以前更堅固。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請她為你和她丈夫之間這個斷裂的關節上夾板,我拿我的運氣打賭任何值得一提的賭注,你們愛情的這道裂縫會比以前更堅固。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: You advise me well.
passages.vernacular: 你勸得好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你勸得好。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: I protest, in the sincerity of love and honest kindness.
passages.vernacular: 我發誓,係出於真誠嘅愛同誠實嘅善意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我發誓,是出於真誠的愛和誠實的善意。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: I think it freely; and betimes in the morning I will beseech the virtuous Desdemona to undertake for me;
passages.vernacular: 我坦然相信;明朝一早我就懇求賢德嘅戴絲德夢娜替我出面;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我坦然相信;明早一早我就懇求賢德的戴絲德夢娜替我出面;

passages.original: I am desperate of my fortunes if they check me here.
passages.vernacular: 如果我嘅命運喺呢度受阻,我就絕望喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我的命運在這裡受阻,我就絕望了。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: You are in the right.
passages.vernacular: 你做得對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你做得對。

passages.original: Good night, lieutenant, I must to the watch.
passages.vernacular: 晚安,副官,我必須去巡邏喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚安,副官,我必須去巡邏了。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Good night, honest Iago.
passages.vernacular: 晚安,誠實嘅伊阿古。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚安,誠實的伊阿古。

passages.original: [Exit.]
passages.vernacular: [凱西奧下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [凱西奧下。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: And what’s he then, that says I play the villain?
passages.vernacular: 咁係誰話我扮演惡棍?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼,是誰說我扮演惡棍?

passages.original: When this advice is free I give and honest, Probal to thinking, and indeed the course To win the Moor again?
passages.vernacular: 當我呢個建議係自由、誠實、合乎思考,確實係贏返摩爾人嘅正途時?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我這個建議是自由、誠實、合乎思考,確實是贏回摩爾人的正途時?

passages.original: For ’tis most easy The inclining Desdemona to subdue In any honest suit.
passages.vernacular: 因為最容易嘅係講服樂於助人嘅戴絲德夢娜,在任何正當請求上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為最容易的是說服樂於助人的戴絲德夢娜,在任何正當請求上。

passages.original: She’s fram’d as fruitful As the free elements.
passages.vernacular: 佢天性豐饒,如同自由嘅元素。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她天性豐饒,如同自由的元素。

passages.original: And then for her To win the Moor, were’t to renounce his baptism, All seals and symbols of redeemed sin, His soul is so enfetter’d to her love That she may make, unmake, do what she list, Even as her appetite shall play the god With his weak function.
passages.vernacular: 而講到佢要贏得摩爾人,即使要佢放棄洗禮、放棄一切救贖罪孽嘅印記同象徵,佢嘅靈魂也如此被佢嘅愛鎖住,佢可以隨意造就、毀掉,隨心所欲,彷彿佢嘅慾望可以在佢軟弱嘅功能上扮演神。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而說到她要贏得摩爾人,即使要他放棄洗禮、放棄一切救贖罪孽的印記與象徵,他的靈魂也如此被她的愛鎖住,她可以隨意造就、毀掉,隨心所欲,彷彿她的慾望可以在他軟弱的功能上扮演神。

passages.original: How am I then, a villain To counsel Cassio to this parallel course, Directly to his good?
passages.vernacular: 咁我點算惡棍,勸凱西奧走呢條平行嘅路,直接為佢好?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那我怎麼算惡棍,勸凱西奧走這條平行的路,直接為他好?

passages.original: Divinity of hell!
passages.vernacular: 地獄嘅神學!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 地獄的神學!

passages.original: When devils will the blackest sins put on, They do suggest at first with heavenly shows, As I do now:
passages.vernacular: 當魔鬼要引人犯最黑嘅罪,起初總係以天堂嘅樣子暗示,就像我而家:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當魔鬼要引人犯最黑的罪,起初總是以天堂的樣子暗示,就像我現在:

passages.original: for whiles this honest fool Plies Desdemona to repair his fortune, And she for him pleads strongly to the Moor, I’ll pour this pestilence into his ear, That she repeals him for her body’s lust;
passages.vernacular: 當呢個誠實嘅傻瓜纏住戴絲德夢娜去修復佢嘅命運,而佢又強烈地向摩爾人為佢求情時,我要把呢個瘟疫倒進佢耳中:佢為滿足自己身體嘅情慾而要佢復職;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當這個誠實的傻瓜纏著戴絲德夢娜去修復他的命運,而她又強烈地向摩爾人為他求情時,我要把這個瘟疫倒進他耳中:她為滿足自己身體的情慾而要他復職;

passages.original: And by how much she strives to do him good, She shall undo her credit with the Moor.
passages.vernacular: 佢愈努力幫佢,就愈在摩爾人嗰度毀掉自己嘅信譽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她愈努力幫他,就愈在摩爾人那裡毀掉自己的信譽。

passages.original: So will I turn her virtue into pitch, And out of her own goodness make the net That shall enmesh them all.
passages.vernacular: 我就咁樣把佢嘅美德變成瀝青,用佢自己嘅善良織成網,網住佢哋所有人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就這樣把她的美德變成瀝青,用她自己的善良織成網,網住他們所有人。

passages.original: Enter Roderigo.
passages.vernacular: [羅德利哥上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅德利哥上。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: How now, Roderigo?
passages.vernacular: 點樣,羅德利哥?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼樣,羅德利哥?

passages.title: Roderigo 羅德利哥
passages.original: I do follow here in the chase, not like a hound that hunts, but one that fills up the cry.
passages.vernacular: 我喺度參與追獵,唔似一條真正獵捕嘅獵犬,只係湊數吠叫嘅嗰種。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在這裡參與追獵,不像一條真正獵捕的獵犬,只是湊數吠叫的那種。

passages.original: My money is almost spent, I have been tonight exceedingly well cudgelled;
passages.vernacular: 我嘅錢差唔多花光喇,今晚仲被痛打咗一頓;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的錢差不多花光了,今晚還被痛打了一頓;

passages.original: and I think the issue will be, I shall have so much experience for my pains, and so, with no money at all and a little more wit, return again to Venice.
passages.vernacular: 我諗結果係,我為我嘅辛苦得到咁多經驗,然後身無分文,稍增智慧,返威尼斯去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想結果是,我為我的辛苦得到這麼多經驗,然後身無分文,稍增智慧,回威尼斯去。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: How poor are they that have not patience!
passages.vernacular: 冇耐心嘅人幾咁可憐!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒耐心的人多麼可憐!

passages.original: What wound did ever heal but by degrees?
passages.vernacular: 咩傷口唔係逐漸癒合嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼傷口不是逐漸癒合的?

passages.original: Thou know’st we work by wit, and not by witchcraft, And wit depends on dilatory time.
passages.vernacular: 你知道我哋靠智慧而非巫術行事,而智慧要依賴拖延嘅時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道我們靠智慧而非巫術行事,而智慧要依賴拖延的時間。

passages.original: Does’t not go well?
passages.vernacular: 事情唔係進展順利嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事情不是進展順利嗎?

passages.original: Cassio hath beaten thee, And thou, by that small hurt, hast cashier’d Cassio;
passages.vernacular: 凱西奧打咗你,而你憑嗰點小傷,已經把凱西奧革職喇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凱西奧打了你,而你憑那點小傷,已經把凱西奧革職了;

passages.original: Though other things grow fair against the sun, Yet fruits that blossom first will first be ripe.
passages.vernacular: 雖然別嘅嘢迎住太陽長得好,但最先開花嘅果實最先成熟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然別的東西迎著太陽長得好,但最先開花的果實最先成熟。

passages.original: Content thyself awhile.
passages.vernacular: 先耐心等一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先耐心等一會兒。

passages.original: By the mass, ’tis morning; Pleasure and action make the hours seem short.
passages.vernacular: 憑彌撒,已係早晨;快樂同行動令時辰顯得短。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑彌撒,已是早晨;快樂和行動令時辰顯得短。

passages.original: Retire thee; go where thou art billeted.
passages.vernacular: 返去吧;去你嘅住處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回去吧;去你的住處。

passages.original: Away, I say, thou shalt know more hereafter.
passages.vernacular: 走,我話,你以後會知道更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走,我說,你以後會知道更多。

passages.original: Nay, get thee gone.
passages.vernacular: 快走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 快走。

passages.original: [Exit Roderigo.]
passages.vernacular: [羅德利哥下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅德利哥下。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Two things are to be done, My wife must move for Cassio to her mistress.
passages.vernacular: 有兩件事要做,我妻子必須向佢嘅女主人為凱西奧講情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有兩件事要做,我妻子必須向她的女主人為凱西奧說情。

passages.original: I’ll set her on; Myself the while to draw the Moor apart, And bring him jump when he may Cassio find Soliciting his wife.
passages.vernacular: 我會慫恿佢;同時我自己要把摩爾人拉到一旁,在佢恰好睇到凱西奧向佢妻子懇求嘅時候帶佢過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會慫恿她;同時我自己要把摩爾人拉到一旁,在他恰好看見凱西奧向他妻子懇求的時候帶他過去。

passages.original: Ay, that’s the way.
passages.vernacular: 對,就係呢條路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,就是這條路。

passages.original: Dull not device by coldness and delay.
passages.vernacular: 唔好因冷淡同拖延令計謀變鈍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要因冷淡與拖延使計謀變鈍。

passages.original: [Exit.]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene I — Cyprus. Before the Castle 第三幕第一場:塞浦路斯城堡前

passages.original: Enter Cassio and some Musicians.
passages.vernacular: [凱西奧同幾位樂師上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [凱西奧和幾位樂師上。]

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Masters, play here, I will content your pains, Something that’s brief;
passages.vernacular: 各位師傅,就喺度演奏,我會酬謝你哋嘅辛勞,演奏啲簡短嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 各位師傅,就在這裡演奏,我會酬謝你們的辛勞,演奏點簡短的;

passages.original: and bid “Good morrow, general.”
passages.vernacular: 並且向將軍道「早安」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並且向將軍道「早安」。

passages.original: [Music.]
passages.vernacular: [奏樂。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奏樂。]

passages.original: Enter Clown.
passages.vernacular: [小丑上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [小丑上。]

passages.title: Clown 小丑
passages.original: Why, masters, have your instruments been in Naples, that they speak i’ the nose thus?
passages.vernacular: 咦,各位師傅,你哋嘅樂器去過嗰不勒斯嗎,點解講起話來帶鼻音?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,各位師傅,你們的樂器去過那不勒斯嗎,怎麼說起話來帶鼻音?

passages.title: First Musician 第一樂師
passages.original: How, sir, how?
passages.vernacular: 點,先生,點?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼,先生,怎麼?

passages.title: Clown 小丑
passages.original: Are these, I pray you, wind instruments?
passages.vernacular: 請問,呢啲係管樂器嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請問,這些是管樂器嗎?

passages.title: First Musician 第一樂師
passages.original: Ay, marry, are they, sir.
passages.vernacular: 係,當然係,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,當然是,先生。

passages.title: Clown 小丑
passages.original: O, thereby hangs a tail.
passages.vernacular: 啊,嗰度面有條尾巴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,那裡面有條尾巴。

passages.title: First Musician 第一樂師
passages.original: Whereby hangs a tale, sir?
passages.vernacular: 掛住咩故事,先生?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 掛著什麼故事,先生?

passages.title: Clown 小丑
passages.original: Marry, sir, by many a wind instrument that I know.
passages.vernacular: 當然,先生,掛喺我知道嘅許多管樂器上(也指屁)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,先生,掛在我知道的許多管樂器上(也指屁)。

passages.original: But, masters, here’s money for you: and the general so likes your music, that he desires you, for love’s sake, to make no more noise with it.
passages.vernacular: 不過,各位師傅,呢度有錢畀你哋:將軍非常鍾意你哋嘅音樂,為咗愛,佢請求你哋唔好再用佢製造噪音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,各位師傅,這裡有錢給你們:將軍非常喜歡你們的音樂,為了愛,他請求你們不要再用它製造噪音。

passages.title: First Musician 第一樂師
passages.original: Well, sir, we will not.
passages.vernacular: 好,先生,我哋唔奏喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,先生,我們不奏了。

passages.title: Clown 小丑
passages.original: If you have any music that may not be heard, to’t again.
passages.vernacular: 如果你哋有聽唔到嘅音樂,就再演奏吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你們有聽不見的音樂,就再演奏吧。

passages.original: But, as they say, to hear music the general does not greatly care.
passages.vernacular: 但據講,將軍並唔太鍾意聽音樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但據說,將軍並不太喜歡聽音樂。

passages.title: First Musician 第一樂師
passages.original: We have none such, sir.
passages.vernacular: 我哋冇咁嘅音樂,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們沒有這樣的音樂,先生。

passages.title: Clown 小丑
passages.original: Then put up your pipes in your bag, for I’ll away.
passages.vernacular: 咁就把你哋嘅笛子收進袋子,因為我要走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就把你們的笛子收進袋子,因為我要走了。

passages.original: Go, vanish into air, away!
passages.vernacular: 去,消失喺空氣裡,走!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,消失在空氣裡,走!

passages.original: [Exeunt Musicians.]
passages.vernacular: [樂師哋下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [樂師們下。]

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Dost thou hear, mine honest friend?
passages.vernacular: 你聽到嗎,我誠實嘅朋友?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你聽到嗎,我誠實的朋友?

passages.title: Clown 小丑
passages.original: No, I hear not your honest friend. I hear you.
passages.vernacular: 唔,我冇聽到你誠實嘅朋友。我聽到嘅係你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,我沒聽到你誠實的朋友。我聽到的是你。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Prithee, keep up thy quillets.
passages.vernacular: 請你,收起你嘅雙關語吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你,收起你的雙關語吧。

passages.original: There’s a poor piece of gold for thee: if the gentlewoman that attends the general’s wife be stirring, tell her there’s one Cassio entreats her a little favour of speech.
passages.vernacular: 呢度有一小塊金幣畀你:如果服侍將軍夫人嗰位婦人已起身,告訴佢有位凱西奧懇求同佢講幾句話嘅恩典。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡有一小塊金幣給你:如果服侍將軍夫人的那位婦人已起身,告訴她有位凱西奧懇求與她說幾句話的恩典。

passages.original: Wilt thou do this?
passages.vernacular: 你肯做嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你肯做嗎?

passages.title: Clown 小丑
passages.original: She is stirring, sir; if she will stir hither, I shall seem to notify unto her.
passages.vernacular: 佢起咗身,先生;如果佢肯過嚟,我會似乎通知佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她起身了,先生;如果她肯過來,我會似乎通知她。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Do, good my friend.
passages.vernacular: 去吧,好朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去吧,好朋友。

passages.original: [Exit Clown.]
passages.vernacular: [小丑下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [小丑下。]

passages.original: Enter Iago.
passages.vernacular: [伊阿古上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [伊阿古上。]

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: In happy time, Iago.
passages.vernacular: 來得正好,伊阿古。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來得正好,伊阿古。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: You have not been a-bed, then?
passages.vernacular: 咁你仲未上床瞓覺?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那你還沒上床睡覺?

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Why, no.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,沒有。

passages.original: The day had broke Before we parted.
passages.vernacular: 我哋分手之前天已經亮喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們分手之前天已經亮了。

passages.original: I have made bold, Iago, To send in to your wife.
passages.vernacular: 伊阿古,我大膽派人去搵你妻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 伊阿古,我大膽派人去找你妻子。

passages.original: My suit to her Is, that she will to virtuous Desdemona Procure me some access.
passages.vernacular: 我向佢嘅請求係,請佢向賢德嘅戴絲德夢娜為我爭取啲接近嘅機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我向她的請求是,請她向賢德的戴絲德夢娜為我爭取些接近的機會。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: I’ll send her to you presently, And I’ll devise a mean to draw the Moor Out of the way, that your converse and business May be more free.
passages.vernacular: 我會即刻把佢派嚟,仲會設法把摩爾人引開,令你哋嘅交談同事務更自由。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會馬上把她派來,還會設法把摩爾人引開,讓你們的交談和事務更自由。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: I humbly thank you for’t.
passages.vernacular: 我謙卑地感謝你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我謙卑地感謝你。

passages.original: [Exit Iago.]
passages.vernacular: [伊阿古下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [伊阿古下。]

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: I never knew A Florentine more kind and honest.
passages.vernacular: 我從未見過比佢更善良誠實嘅佛羅倫斯人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從未見過比他更善良誠實的佛羅倫斯人。

passages.original: Enter Emilia.
passages.vernacular: [愛米利亞上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [愛米利亞上。]

passages.title: Emilia 愛米利亞
passages.original: Good morrow, good lieutenant; I am sorry For your displeasure, but all will sure be well.
passages.vernacular: 早安,好副官;我為你嘅失勢感到遺憾,不過一切必會好起來。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早安,好副官;我為你的失勢感到遺憾,不過一切必會好起來。

passages.original: The general and his wife are talking of it, And she speaks for you stoutly:
passages.vernacular: 將軍同夫人正在傾呢件事,佢堅決為你講嘢:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 將軍和夫人正在談這件事,她堅決為你說話:

passages.original: the Moor replies That he you hurt is of great fame in Cyprus And great affinity, and that in wholesome wisdom He might not but refuse you;
passages.vernacular: 摩爾人回答話,你傷嗰個人喺塞浦路斯名聲顯赫、關係深厚,出於穩妥嘅智慧,佢不得不拒絕你;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 摩爾人回答說,你傷的那個人在塞浦路斯名聲顯赫、關係深厚,出於穩妥的智慧,他不得不拒絕你;

passages.original: but he protests he loves you And needs no other suitor but his likings To take the safest occasion by the front To bring you in again.
passages.vernacular: 但佢聲明佢愛你,除咗佢自己嘅喜愛之外唔需要別嘅求情人,一有最穩妥嘅機會就會立即把你召回。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他聲明他愛你,除了他自己的喜愛之外不需要別的求情人,一有最穩妥的機會就會立即把你召回。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Yet, I beseech you, If you think fit, or that it may be done, Give me advantage of some brief discourse With Desdemona alone.
passages.vernacular: 然而,我懇求你,如果你認為合適,或可行,讓我有機會單獨同戴絲德夢娜簡短傾傾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,我懇求你,如果你認為合適,或可行,讓我有機會單獨與戴絲德夢娜簡短談談。

passages.title: Emilia 愛米利亞
passages.original: Pray you, come in.
passages.vernacular: 請入嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請進來。

passages.original: I will bestow you where you shall have time To speak your bosom freely.
passages.vernacular: 我會安排你到一個地方,讓你有時間自由傾訴心聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會安排你到一個地方,讓你有時間自由傾訴心聲。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: I am much bound to you.
passages.vernacular: 我非常感激你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我非常感激你。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene II — Cyprus. A Room in the Castle 第三幕第二場:塞浦路斯城堡一室

passages.original: Enter Othello, Iago and Gentlemen.
passages.vernacular: [奧賽羅、伊阿古同紳士哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧賽羅、伊阿古和紳士們上。]

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: These letters give, Iago, to the pilot, And by him do my duties to the senate.
passages.vernacular: 伊阿古,把呢啲信交畀領航員,並通過佢向元老院致意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 伊阿古,把這些信交給領航員,並通過他向元老院致意。

passages.original: That done, I will be walking on the works, Repair there to me.
passages.vernacular: 辦完後,我會喺工事上散步,你到嗰度搵我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 辦完後,我會在工事上散步,你到那裡找我。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Well, my good lord, I’ll do’t.
passages.vernacular: 好,我嘅好大人,我去辦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,我的好大人,我去辦。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: This fortification, gentlemen, shall we see’t?
passages.vernacular: 呢座防禦工事,先生哋,我哋去睇睇嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這座防禦工事,先生們,我們去看看嗎?

passages.title: Gentlemen 紳士們
passages.original: We’ll wait upon your lordship.
passages.vernacular: 我哋聽候大人差遣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們聽候大人差遣。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene III — Cyprus. The Garden of the Castle 第三幕第三場:塞浦路斯城堡花園

passages.original: Enter Desdemona, Cassio and Emilia.
passages.vernacular: [戴絲德夢娜、凱西奧同愛米利亞上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [戴絲德夢娜、凱西奧和愛米利亞上。]

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Be thou assured, good Cassio, I will do All my abilities in thy behalf.
passages.vernacular: 你放心,好凱西奧,我會為你盡我一切所能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你放心,好凱西奧,我會為你盡我一切所能。

passages.title: Emilia 愛米利亞
passages.original: Good madam, do.
passages.vernacular: 好夫人,請務必。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好夫人,請務必。

passages.original: I warrant it grieves my husband As if the cause were his.
passages.vernacular: 我保證呢件事令我丈夫難過,就好似事情係佢自己嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我保證這件事令我丈夫難過,就好像事情是他自己的。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: O, that’s an honest fellow.
passages.vernacular: 啊,佢係個誠實嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,他是個誠實的人。

passages.original: Do not doubt, Cassio, But I will have my lord and you again As friendly as you were.
passages.vernacular: 唔好懷疑,凱西奧,我會令我丈夫同你重新好似從前一樣友好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要懷疑,凱西奧,我會讓我丈夫和你重新像從前一樣友好。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Bounteous madam, Whatever shall become of Michael Cassio, He’s never anything but your true servant.
passages.vernacular: 慷慨嘅夫人,無論邁克爾·凱西奧將來如何,佢永遠只係您忠實嘅僕人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 慷慨的夫人,無論邁克爾·凱西奧將來如何,他永遠只是您忠實的僕人。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: I know’t.
passages.vernacular: 我知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道。

passages.original: I thank you.
passages.vernacular: 我多謝你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我謝謝你。

passages.original: You do love my lord.
passages.vernacular: 你確實愛我丈夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你確實愛我丈夫。

passages.original: You have known him long; and be you well assur’d He shall in strangeness stand no farther off Than in a politic distance.
passages.vernacular: 你認識佢好耐喇;你放心,佢嘅疏遠只會保持在政治上必要嘅距離,唔會更遠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你認識他很久了;你放心,他的疏遠只會保持在政治上必要的距離,不會更遠。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Ay, but, lady, That policy may either last so long, Or feed upon such nice and waterish diet, Or breed itself so out of circumstance, That, I being absent, and my place supplied, My general will forget my love and service.
passages.vernacular: 係,不過,夫人,嗰種政治考慮可能持續太耐,或者靠咁稀薄嘅飲食維持,或者因環境而咁樣滋生,以致我唔在時,我嘅位置有人頂替,我嘅將軍會忘記我嘅愛同服務。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,不過,夫人,那種政治考慮可能持續太久,或者靠這麼稀薄的飲食維持,或者因環境而這樣滋生,以致我不在時,我的位置有人頂替,我的將軍會忘記我的愛和服務。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Do not doubt that.
passages.vernacular: 唔好懷疑呢點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要懷疑這點。

passages.original: Before Emilia here I give thee warrant of thy place.
passages.vernacular: 當住愛米利亞嘅面,我向你保證你嘅職位。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當著愛米利亞的面,我向你保證你的職位。

passages.original: Assure thee, If I do vow a friendship, I’ll perform it To the last article.
passages.vernacular: 放心,如果我發誓友誼,我會履行到最後一個條款。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 放心,如果我發誓友誼,我會履行到最後一個條款。

passages.original: My lord shall never rest, I’ll watch him tame, and talk him out of patience;
passages.vernacular: 我丈夫將不得安寧,我會令佢瞓唔到直至馴服,向佢喋喋不休直到佢失去耐性;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我丈夫將不得安寧,我會讓他不得睡覺直至馴服,向他喋喋不休直到他失去耐性;

passages.original: His bed shall seem a school, his board a shrift;
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅床會像學校,佢嘅餐桌像告解室;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的床會像學校,他的餐桌像告解室;

passages.original: I’ll intermingle everything he does With Cassio’s suit.
passages.vernacular: 我會把佢做嘅每件事都夾雜住凱西奧嘅請求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會把他做的每件事都夾雜著凱西奧的請求。

passages.original: Therefore be merry, Cassio, For thy solicitor shall rather die Than give thy cause away.
passages.vernacular: 所以,凱西奧,高興起來,因為你嘅求情人寧死也唔會放棄你嘅案子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,凱西奧,高興起來,因為你的求情人寧死也不會放棄你的案子。

passages.original: Enter Othello and Iago.
passages.vernacular: [奧賽羅同伊阿古上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧賽羅和伊阿古上。]

passages.title: Emilia 愛米利亞
passages.original: Madam, here comes my lord.
passages.vernacular: 夫人,我嘅大人來喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夫人,我的大人來了。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Madam, I’ll take my leave.
passages.vernacular: 夫人,我告辭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夫人,我告辭了。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Why, stay, and hear me speak.
passages.vernacular: 咦,留低,聽我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,留下,聽我說。

passages.title: Cassio 凱西奧
passages.original: Madam, not now.
passages.vernacular: 夫人,而家唔得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夫人,現在不行。

passages.original: I am very ill at ease, Unfit for mine own purposes.
passages.vernacular: 我好唔自在,唔適合辦我自己嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很不自在,不適合辦我自己的事。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Well, do your discretion.
passages.vernacular: 好,隨你酌情處理。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,隨你酌情處理。

passages.original: [Exit Cassio.]
passages.vernacular: [凱西奧下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [凱西奧下。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Ha, I like not that.
passages.vernacular: 哈,我唔鍾意咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈,我不喜歡這樣。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: What dost thou say?
passages.vernacular: 你講咩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說什麼?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Nothing, my lord; or if—I know not what.
passages.vernacular: 冇咩,大人;或者如果——我唔知係咩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒什麼,大人;或者如果——我不知道是什麼。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Was not that Cassio parted from my wife?
passages.vernacular: 剛才從我妻子身邊離開嘅唔係凱西奧嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 剛才從我妻子身邊離開的不是凱西奧嗎?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Cassio, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 凱西奧,大人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凱西奧,大人?

passages.original: No, sure, I cannot think it, That he would steal away so guilty-like, Seeing you coming.
passages.vernacular: 唔,肯定唔係,我唔能想像佢睇到您嚟咗,就咁樣似做賊心虛咁溜走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,肯定不是,我不能想像他看到您來了,就這樣像做賊心虛地溜走。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: I do believe ’twas he.
passages.vernacular: 我確信嗰係佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確信那是他。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: How now, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 點樣喇,我嘅大人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,我的大人?

passages.original: I have been talking with a suitor here, A man that languishes in your displeasure.
passages.vernacular: 我剛才喺度同一位求情者傾偈,佢係個喺你不悅之下憔悴嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我剛才在這裡與一位求情者談話,他是個在你不悅之下憔悴的人。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Who is’t you mean?
passages.vernacular: 你指嘅係誰?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你指的是誰?

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Why, your lieutenant, Cassio.
passages.vernacular: 咦,你嘅副官,凱西奧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,你的副官,凱西奧。

passages.original: Good my lord, If I have any grace or power to move you, His present reconciliation take;
passages.vernacular: 好大人,如果我有任何魅力或力量能打動你,請接受佢而家嘅和解;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好大人,如果我有任何魅力或力量能打動你,請接受他現在的和解;

passages.original: For if he be not one that truly loves you, That errs in ignorance and not in cunning, I have no judgement in an honest face.
passages.vernacular: 因為如果佢唔係真心愛你嘅人,唔係出於無知而非狡詐而犯錯,咁我就唔識分辨誠實嘅面孔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為如果他不是真心愛你的人,不是出於無知而非狡詐而犯錯,那我就不懂分辨誠實的面孔。

passages.original: I prithee call him back.
passages.vernacular: 求你叫佢返嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 求你叫他回來。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Went he hence now?
passages.vernacular: 佢剛走嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他剛走嗎?

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Ay, sooth; so humbled That he hath left part of his grief with me To suffer with him.
passages.vernacular: 係,真嘅;佢卑微到把一部分悲痛留畀我,與佢同受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,真的;他卑微到把一部分悲痛留給我,與他同受。

passages.original: Good love, call him back.
passages.vernacular: 好愛人,叫佢返嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好愛人,叫他回來。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Not now, sweet Desdemon, some other time.
passages.vernacular: 而家唔得,親愛嘅戴絲德夢娜,改日。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在不行,親愛的戴絲德夢娜,改天。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: But shall’t be shortly?
passages.vernacular: 但會好快嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但會很快嗎?

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: The sooner, sweet, for you.
passages.vernacular: 為咗你,愈快愈好,親愛嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了你,愈快愈好,親愛的。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Shall’t be tonight at supper?
passages.vernacular: 今晚晚餐時得嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今晚晚餐時行嗎?

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: No, not tonight.
passages.vernacular: 唔得,今晚唔得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不行,今晚不行。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Tomorrow dinner then?
passages.vernacular: 咁聽日午飯呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那明天午飯呢?

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: I shall not dine at home; I meet the captains at the citadel.
passages.vernacular: 我唔喺屋企食飯;我要喺城堡同眾軍官會面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不在家吃飯;我要在城堡與眾軍官會面。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Why then tomorrow night, or Tuesday morn, On Tuesday noon, or night; on Wednesday morn.
passages.vernacular: 咁聽日夜晚,或星期二朝早,星期二中午或夜晚;星期三朝早。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼明天晚上,或星期二早上,星期二中午或晚上;星期三早上。

passages.original: I prithee name the time, but let it not Exceed three days.
passages.vernacular: 請你定個時間,但唔好超過三日。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你定個時間,但不要超過三天。

passages.original: In faith, he’s penitent; And yet his trespass, in our common reason, (Save that, they say, the wars must make examples Out of their best) is not almost a fault To incur a private check.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,佢好悔改;佢嘅過失,以我哋一般嘅理性睇(除咗據講戰爭必須拎最好嘅人做榜樣),幾乎算唔上值得受私下嘅責備。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,他很悔改;他的過失,以我們一般的理性看(除了據說戰爭必須拿最好的人做榜樣),幾乎算不上值得受私下的責備。

passages.original: When shall he come?
passages.vernacular: 佢幾時嚟?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他什麼時候來?

passages.original: Tell me, Othello: I wonder in my soul, What you would ask me, that I should deny, Or stand so mammering on. What?
passages.vernacular: 告訴我,奧賽羅:我心裡奇怪,你會要求我咩,係我要拒絕,或者咁猶豫不決嘅?咩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 告訴我,奧賽羅:我心裡奇怪,你會要求我什麼,是我要拒絕,或這樣猶豫不決的?什麼?

passages.original: Michael Cassio, That came a-wooing with you, and so many a time, When I have spoke of you dispraisingly, Hath ta’en your part, to have so much to do To bring him in!
passages.vernacular: 邁克爾·凱西奧,佢陪你嚟求婚,每當我講你壞話,佢都替你辯護,而家為咗令佢返嚟竟要費咁大勁!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 邁克爾·凱西奧,他陪你來求婚,每當我說你壞話,他都替你辯護,現在為了讓他回來竟要費這麼大勁!

passages.original: Trust me, I could do much.
passages.vernacular: 相信我,我可以做好多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 相信我,我可以做很多。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Prithee no more.
passages.vernacular: 請唔好再講喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請別再說了。

passages.original: Let him come when he will; I will deny thee nothing.
passages.vernacular: 讓佢隨時嚟;我咩都唔會拒絕你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓他隨時來;我什麼都不會拒絕你。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Why, this is not a boon; ’Tis as I should entreat you wear your gloves, Or feed on nourishing dishes, or keep you warm, Or sue to you to do a peculiar profit To your own person:
passages.vernacular: 咦,呢個唔係咩恩惠;就好似我請你戴手套,或食有營養嘅菜,或保暖,或請你做對自己有特別好處嘅事:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,這不是什麼恩惠;這就像我請你戴手套,或吃營養的菜,或保暖,或請你做對自己有特別好處的事:

passages.original: nay, when I have a suit Wherein I mean to touch your love indeed, It shall be full of poise and difficult weight, And fearful to be granted.
passages.vernacular: 唔,當我有個請求,真正想測試你嘅愛時,佢將會好沉重、好難,令人害怕難以答應。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,當我有個請求,真正想測試你的愛時,它將是很沉重、很難的,令人害怕難以答應。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: I will deny thee nothing.
passages.vernacular: 我咩都唔會拒絕你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我什麼都不會拒絕你。

passages.original: Whereon, I do beseech thee, grant me this, To leave me but a little to myself.
passages.vernacular: 因此,我懇求你,答應我呢個:讓我獨自留一陣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此,我懇求你,答應我這個:讓我獨自待一會兒。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Shall I deny you?
passages.vernacular: 我拒絕你嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我拒絕你嗎?

passages.original: No, farewell, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 唔,再見,我嘅大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,再見,我的大人。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Farewell, my Desdemona.
passages.vernacular: 再見,我嘅戴絲德夢娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見,我的戴絲德夢娜。

passages.original: I’ll come to thee straight.
passages.vernacular: 我即刻去搵你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我馬上去找你。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Emilia, come.
passages.vernacular: 愛米利亞,來。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛米利亞,來。

passages.original: Be as your fancies teach you.
passages.vernacular: 隨你嘅心意吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨你的心意吧。

passages.original: Whate’er you be, I am obedient.
passages.vernacular: 無論你點樣,我都順從。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論你怎樣,我都順從。

passages.original: [Exit with Emilia.]
passages.vernacular: [同愛米利亞下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同愛米利亞下。]

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Excellent wretch!
passages.vernacular: 絕妙嘅小可憐!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 絕妙的小可憐!

passages.original: Perdition catch my soul, But I do love thee!
passages.vernacular: 願我嘅靈魂墮入地獄,如果我唔愛你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願我的靈魂墮入地獄,如果我不愛你!

passages.original: And when I love thee not, Chaos is come again.
passages.vernacular: 當我唔再愛你時,混沌就重新降臨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我不再愛你時,混沌就重新降臨。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: My noble lord,—
passages.vernacular: 我高貴嘅大人——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我高貴的大人——

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: What dost thou say, Iago?
passages.vernacular: 你講咩,伊阿古?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說什麼,伊阿古?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Did Michael Cassio, when you woo’d my lady, Know of your love?
passages.vernacular: 當你追求我夫人時,邁克爾·凱西奧知道你嘅愛嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當你追求我夫人時,邁克爾·凱西奧知道你的愛嗎?

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: He did, from first to last.
passages.vernacular: 佢知道,從頭到尾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他知道,從頭到尾。

passages.original: Why dost thou ask?
passages.vernacular: 你點解問?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為何問?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: But for a satisfaction of my thought.
passages.vernacular: 只係為咗滿足我嘅思緒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是為了滿足我的思緒。

passages.original: No further harm.
passages.vernacular: 冇別嘅害處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒別的害處。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Why of thy thought, Iago?
passages.vernacular: 你嘅思緒係咩,伊阿古?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的思緒是什麼,伊阿古?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: I did not think he had been acquainted with her.
passages.vernacular: 我冇想到佢認識佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒想到他認識她。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: O yes, and went between us very oft.
passages.vernacular: 啊,認識,而且常常喺我哋之間傳話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,認識,而且常常在我們之間傳話。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Indeed?
passages.vernacular: 真嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真的?

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Indeed? Ay, indeed.
passages.vernacular: 真嘅?係,真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真的?是,真的。

passages.original: Discern’st thou aught in that?
passages.vernacular: 你從中睇出咩嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你從中看出什麼嗎?

passages.original: Is he not honest?
passages.vernacular: 佢唔誠實嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不誠實嗎?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Honest, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 誠實,大人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誠實,大人?

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Honest? ay, honest.
passages.vernacular: 誠實?係,誠實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誠實?是,誠實。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: My lord, for aught I know.
passages.vernacular: 大人,據我所知。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,據我所知。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: What dost thou think?
passages.vernacular: 你點諗?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你怎麼想?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Think, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 諗,大人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想,大人?

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Think, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 諗,大人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想,大人?

passages.original: By heaven, he echoes me, As if there were some monster in his thought Too hideous to be shown.
passages.vernacular: 天啊,佢重複我嘅話,好似佢心裡有個太醜陋而唔能展示嘅怪物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天啊,他在重複我的話,好像他心裡有個太醜陋而不能展示的怪物。

passages.original: Thou dost mean something.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅話有所指。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的話有所指。

passages.original: I heard thee say even now, thou lik’st not that, When Cassio left my wife.
passages.vernacular: 我剛才聽到你講,凱西奧離開我妻子時,你唔鍾意咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我剛才聽到你說,凱西奧離開我妻子時,你不喜歡那樣。

passages.original: What didst not like?
passages.vernacular: 你唔鍾意咩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不喜歡什麼?

passages.original: And when I told thee he was of my counsel In my whole course of wooing, thou criedst, “Indeed?”
passages.vernacular: 當我告訴你,在我整個求婚過程中佢係我嘅參謀時,你喊「真嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我告訴你,在我整個求婚過程中他是我的參謀時,你喊「真的?」

passages.original: And didst contract and purse thy brow together, As if thou then hadst shut up in thy brain Some horrible conceit:
passages.vernacular: 仲皺起眉頭緊縮,好似你把某個可怕嘅念頭鎖進腦裡:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還皺起眉頭緊縮,好像你把某個可怕的念頭鎖進腦裡:

passages.original: if thou dost love me, Show me thy thought.
passages.vernacular: 如果你愛我,把你嘅想法告訴我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你愛我,把你的想法告訴我。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: My lord, you know I love you.
passages.vernacular: 大人,您知道我愛您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,您知道我愛您。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: I think thou dost; And for I know thou’rt full of love and honesty And weigh’st thy words before thou giv’st them breath, Therefore these stops of thine fright me the more:
passages.vernacular: 我諗你愛;因為我知道你充滿愛與誠實,且在講話之前先權衡你嘅話,所以你呢啲停頓更令我害怕:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你愛;因為我知道你充滿愛與誠實,且在說話之前先權衡你的話,所以你這些停頓更令我害怕:

passages.original: For such things in a false disloyal knave Are tricks of custom;
passages.vernacular: 因為呢類事喺虛偽不忠嘅惡棍身上,係慣用嘅把戲;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為這類事在虛偽不忠的惡棍身上,是慣用的把戲;

passages.original: but in a man that’s just, They’re close dilations, working from the heart, That passion cannot rule.
passages.vernacular: 但喺正直嘅人身上,佢哋係隱藏嘅展開,從心裡發出,激情也無法控制。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但在正直的人身上,它們是隱藏的展開,從心裡發出,激情也無法控制。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: For Michael Cassio, I dare be sworn I think that he is honest.
passages.vernacular: 至於邁克爾·凱西奧,我敢發誓,我認為佢誠實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於邁克爾·凱西奧,我敢發誓,我認為他誠實。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: I think so too.
passages.vernacular: 我也咁認為。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也這樣認為。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Men should be what they seem; Or those that be not, would they might seem none!
passages.vernacular: 人應該表裡如一;否則,唔係咁嘅人,真希望佢哋睇起來也唔係!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人應該表裡如一;否則,不是這樣的人,真希望他們看起來也不是!

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Certain, men should be what they seem.
passages.vernacular: 確實,人應該表裡如一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實,人應該表裡如一。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Why then, I think Cassio’s an honest man.
passages.vernacular: 咁,我認為凱西奧係個誠實嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼,我認為凱西奧是個誠實的人。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Nay, yet there’s more in this: I prithee, speak to me as to thy thinkings, As thou dost ruminate, and give thy worst of thoughts The worst of words.
passages.vernacular: 唔,呢度面還有更多:請你好似對你自己嘅思想一樣對我講,好似你在反覆思量,把你最壞嘅想法用最壞嘅話講出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,這裡面還有更多:請你像對你自己的思想那樣對我說,像你在反覆思量那樣,把你最壞的想法用最壞的話說出來。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Good my lord, pardon me.
passages.vernacular: 好大人,請原諒我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好大人,請原諒我。

passages.original: Though I am bound to every act of duty, I am not bound to that all slaves are free to.
passages.vernacular: 雖然我受約束要履行一切義務,但我唔受約束去做所有奴隸都可以自由做嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然我受約束要履行一切義務,但我不受約束去做所有奴隸都可以自由做的事。

passages.original: Utter my thoughts?
passages.vernacular: 講出我嘅想法?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說出我的想法?

passages.original: Why, say they are vile and false: As where’s that palace whereinto foul things Sometimes intrude not?
passages.vernacular: 咦,就算佢哋係卑鄙虛假嘅:邊座宮殿唔會有時有骯髒嘅嘢闖入?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,就算它們是卑鄙虛假的:哪座宮殿不會有時有骯髒的東西闖入?

passages.original: Who has a breast so pure But some uncleanly apprehensions Keep leets and law-days, and in session sit With meditations lawful?
passages.vernacular: 誰嘅胸懷純潔到唔會有啲唔潔嘅猜疑舉行法庭、審判日,並與正當嘅沉思一齊開庭?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰的胸懷純潔到不會有些不潔的猜疑舉行法庭、審判日,並與正當的沉思一起開庭?

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Thou dost conspire against thy friend, Iago, If thou but think’st him wrong’d and mak’st his ear A stranger to thy thoughts.
passages.vernacular: 伊阿古,如果你認為你朋友受咗冤屈,卻令佢嘅耳朵對你嘅想法陌生,咁你就係在背叛朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 伊阿古,如果你認為你朋友受了冤屈,卻讓他的耳朵對你的想法陌生,那你就是在背叛朋友。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: I do beseech you, Though I perchance am vicious in my guess, As, I confess, it is my nature’s plague To spy into abuses, and of my jealousy Shapes faults that are not,—that your wisdom From one that so imperfectly conceits, Would take no notice;
passages.vernacular: 我懇求您,我嘅猜測也許有毛病,我承認,窺探弊端係我天性嘅瘟疫,我嘅猜疑會編造唔存在嘅過錯——請您嘅智慧唔好理會呢個推測如此不完整嘅人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我懇求您,我的猜測也許有毛病,我承認,窺探弊端是我天性的瘟疫,我的猜疑會編造不存在的過錯——請您的智慧不要理會這個推測如此不完整的人;

passages.original: nor build yourself a trouble Out of his scattering and unsure observance.
passages.vernacular: 也唔好憑佢零散而不確定嘅觀察,為自己製造麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也不要憑他零散而不確定的觀察,為自己製造麻煩。

passages.original: It were not for your quiet nor your good, Nor for my manhood, honesty, or wisdom, To let you know my thoughts.
passages.vernacular: 讓您知道我嘅想法,既不利於您嘅安寧同益處,也唔合我嘅男子氣概、誠實或智慧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓您知道我的想法,既不利於您的安寧和益處,也不合我的男子氣概、誠實或智慧。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: What dost thou mean?
passages.vernacular: 你係咩意思?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是什麼意思?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Good name in man and woman, dear my lord, Is the immediate jewel of their souls.
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅大人,男人同女人嘅好名聲,係佢哋靈魂最貼身嘅珍寶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的大人,男人和女人的好名聲,是他們靈魂最貼身的珍寶。

passages.original: Who steals my purse steals trash.
passages.vernacular: 偷我錢包嘅人偷嘅係垃圾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 偷我錢包的人偷的是垃圾。

passages.original: ’Tis something, nothing; ’Twas mine, ’tis his, and has been slave to thousands.
passages.vernacular: 嗰算係有,也算冇;佢曾係我嘅,而家係佢嘅,也曾做過成千人嘅奴隸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那算是有,也算沒有;它曾是我的,現在是他的,也曾做過成千人的奴隸。

passages.original: But he that filches from me my good name Robs me of that which not enriches him And makes me poor indeed.
passages.vernacular: 但偷走我好名聲嘅人,搶走咗我嘅嘢,卻無助於佢致富,卻實在令我貧窮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但偷走我好名聲的人,搶走了我的東西,卻無助於他致富,卻實在使我貧窮。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: By heaven, I’ll know thy thoughts.
passages.vernacular: 天啊,我要知道你嘅想法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天啊,我要知道你的想法。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: You cannot, if my heart were in your hand, Nor shall not, whilst ’tis in my custody.
passages.vernacular: 你唔能,即使我嘅心在你手裡,只要佢喺我嘅保管之中,你也唔會知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不能,即使我的心在你手裡,只要它在我的保管之中,你也不會知道。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Ha?
passages.vernacular: 哈?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: O, beware, my lord, of jealousy; It is the green-ey’d monster which doth mock The meat it feeds on.
passages.vernacular: 啊,大人,小心嫉妒;佢係綠眼睛嘅怪物,嘲弄佢所吞食嘅食物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,大人,小心嫉妒;它是綠眼睛的怪物,嘲弄它所吞食的食物。

passages.original: That cuckold lives in bliss Who, certain of his fate, loves not his wronger;
passages.vernacular: 嗰個戴綠帽卻確知命運、唔愛傷害佢嘅人嘅丈夫,活喺福中;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個戴綠帽卻確知命運、不愛傷害他的人的丈夫,活在福中;

passages.original: But O, what damned minutes tells he o’er Who dotes, yet doubts, suspects, yet strongly loves!
passages.vernacular: 但啊,嗰個癡愛卻懷疑、猜疑卻深愛嘅人,數住幾咁該死嘅分分秒秒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但啊,那個癡愛卻懷疑、猜疑卻深愛的人,數著多麼該死的分分秒秒!

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: O misery!
passages.vernacular: 啊,悲慘!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,悲慘!

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Poor and content is rich, and rich enough; But riches fineless is as poor as winter To him that ever fears he shall be poor.
passages.vernacular: 貧窮而知足就係富有,而且足夠富有;但對於總怕自己會窮嘅人,無邊嘅財富也像冬天一樣貧乏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貧窮而知足就是富有,而且足夠富有;但對於總怕自己會窮的人,無邊的財富也像冬天一樣貧乏。

passages.original: Good heaven, the souls of all my tribe defend From jealousy!
passages.vernacular: 好上天,保護我全族嘅靈魂免於嫉妒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好上天,保護我全族的靈魂免於嫉妒!

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Why, why is this?
passages.vernacular: 點解,點解咁樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼,為什麼這樣?

passages.original: Think’st thou I’d make a life of jealousy, To follow still the changes of the moon With fresh suspicions? No.
passages.vernacular: 你以為我會把生活過成嫉妒,永遠跟隨月亮嘅圓缺用新嘅猜疑?唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你以為我會把生活過成嫉妒,永遠跟隨月亮的圓缺用新的猜疑?不會。

passages.original: To be once in doubt Is once to be resolv’d: exchange me for a goat When I shall turn the business of my soul To such exsufflicate and blown surmises, Matching thy inference.
passages.vernacular: 一旦起疑,就一次解決:如果我把靈魂嘅大事轉向呢種乾癟、吹出嚟嘅臆測,匹配你嘅推論,就拎我換一隻山羊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一旦起疑,就一次解決:如果我把靈魂的大事轉向這種乾癟、吹出來的臆測,匹配你的推論,就拿我換一隻山羊。

passages.original: ’Tis not to make me jealous, To say my wife is fair, feeds well, loves company, Is free of speech, sings, plays, and dances well;
passages.vernacular: 講我妻子美麗、食得好、愛交際、言辭自由、唱歌彈琴跳舞好,呢啲並唔能令我嫉妒;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說我妻子美麗、吃得好、愛交際、言辭自由、唱歌彈琴跳舞好,這些並不能使我嫉妒;

passages.original: Where virtue is, these are more virtuous: Nor from mine own weak merits will I draw The smallest fear or doubt of her revolt, For she had eyes, and chose me.
passages.vernacular: 有美德嘅地方,呢啲更顯得美德:我也唔會從自己微薄嘅優點中抽出對佢背叛嘅最小恐懼或疑慮,因為佢有眼睛,而選咗我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有美德的地方,這些更顯得美德:我也不會從自己微薄的優點中抽出對她背叛的最小恐懼或疑慮,因為她有眼睛,而選了我。

passages.original: No, Iago, I’ll see before I doubt; when I doubt, prove;
passages.vernacular: 唔,伊阿古,我要先睇見先懷疑;懷疑時,就要證明;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,伊阿古,我要先看見才懷疑;懷疑時,就要證明;

passages.original: And on the proof, there is no more but this: Away at once with love or jealousy!
passages.vernacular: 有咗證據,就只剩呢一件事:立刻拋開愛或嫉妒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有了證據,就只剩這一件事:立刻拋開愛或嫉妒!

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: I am glad of it, for now I shall have reason To show the love and duty that I bear you With franker spirit:
passages.vernacular: 我好高興,因為而家我有理由用更坦率嘅精神向您表示我對您嘅愛同責任:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興,因為現在我有理由用更坦率的精神向您表示我對您的愛和責任:

passages.original: therefore, as I am bound, Receive it from me.
passages.vernacular: 所以,按我嘅職責,請聽我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,按我的職責,請聽我說。

passages.original: I speak not yet of proof.
passages.vernacular: 我仲未講到證據。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我還沒說到證據。

passages.original: Look to your wife; observe her well with Cassio;
passages.vernacular: 留意您嘅妻子;觀察佢同凱西奧在一起嘅樣子;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 留意您的妻子;觀察她與凱西奧在一起的樣子;

passages.original: Wear your eye thus, not jealous nor secure.
passages.vernacular: 咁樣用眼睛:既不嫉妒也不放心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣用眼睛:既不嫉妒也不放心。

passages.original: I would not have your free and noble nature, Out of self-bounty, be abus’d. Look to’t.
passages.vernacular: 我唔願您自由高貴嘅天性,因為自己嘅寬厚而受騙。請留意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不願您自由高貴的天性,因為自己的寬厚而受騙。請留意。

passages.original: I know our country disposition well; In Venice they do let heaven see the pranks They dare not show their husbands.
passages.vernacular: 我好了解我哋國家嘅習性;喺威尼斯,佢哋讓上天睇見唔敢畀丈夫睇嘅把戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很了解我們國家的習性;在威尼斯,她們讓上天看見不敢讓丈夫看的把戲。

passages.original: Their best conscience Is not to leave undone, but keep unknown.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋最好嘅良心唔係唔做,而係唔畀人知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們最好的良心不是不做,而是不讓人知道。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Dost thou say so?
passages.vernacular: 你咁講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這樣說?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: She did deceive her father, marrying you; And when she seem’d to shake and fear your looks, She loved them most.
passages.vernacular: 佢嫁畀您時欺騙咗佢父親;當佢似乎對您嘅面容發抖同害怕時,佢其實最愛佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她嫁給您時欺騙了她父親;當她似乎對您的面容發抖和害怕時,她其實最愛它。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: And so she did.
passages.vernacular: 佢確實如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她確實如此。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Why, go to then.
passages.vernacular: 咦,咁你講吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼,你說吧。

passages.original: She that so young could give out such a seeming, To seal her father’s eyes up close as oak, He thought ’twas witchcraft.
passages.vernacular: 佢咁年輕就能裝出嗰樣嘅樣子,把父親嘅眼睛封得像橡木一樣緊,佢仲以為係巫術。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她那麼年輕就能裝出那樣的樣子,把父親的眼睛封得像橡木一樣緊,他還以為是巫術。

passages.original: But I am much to blame.
passages.vernacular: 但我太唔對喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我太不對了。

passages.original: I humbly do beseech you of your pardon For too much loving you.
passages.vernacular: 我謙卑地懇求您原諒,因為我太愛您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我謙卑地懇求您原諒,因為我太愛您。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: I am bound to thee for ever.
passages.vernacular: 我永遠感激你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我永遠感激你。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: I see this hath a little dash’d your spirits.
passages.vernacular: 我睇呢個稍微打擊咗您嘅精神。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看這稍微打擊了您的精神。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Not a jot, not a jot.
passages.vernacular: 一點也唔,一點也唔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一點也不,一點也不。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Trust me, I fear it has.
passages.vernacular: 相信我,我怕確實如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 相信我,我怕確實如此。

passages.original: I hope you will consider what is spoke Comes from my love.
passages.vernacular: 我希望您考慮到我所講嘅出於我嘅愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望您考慮到我所說的出於我的愛。

passages.original: But I do see you’re mov’d.
passages.vernacular: 但我睇出您被觸動喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我看出您被觸動了。

passages.original: I am to pray you not to strain my speech To grosser issues nor to larger reach Than to suspicion.
passages.vernacular: 我請求您唔好把我嘅話引申到更粗劣嘅結論或更廣嘅範圍,超過猜疑嘅程度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我請求您不要把我的話引申到更粗劣的結論或更廣的範圍,超過猜疑的程度。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: I will not.
passages.vernacular: 我唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不會。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Should you do so, my lord, My speech should fall into such vile success Which my thoughts aim’d not.
passages.vernacular: 如果您嗰樣做,大人,我嘅話就會得到我心裡冇諗到嘅卑劣結果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您那樣做,大人,我的話就會得到我心裡沒想到的卑劣結果。

passages.original: Cassio’s my worthy friend.
passages.vernacular: 凱西奧係我嘅好朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凱西奧是我的好朋友。

passages.original: My lord, I see you’re mov’d.
passages.vernacular: 大人,我睇出您被觸動喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,我看出您被觸動了。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: No, not much mov’d.
passages.vernacular: 唔,冇點動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,沒怎麼動。

passages.original: I do not think but Desdemona’s honest.
passages.vernacular: 我認為戴絲德夢娜係貞潔嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我認為戴絲德夢娜是貞潔的。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Long live she so!
passages.vernacular: 願佢永遠咁樣!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願她永遠這樣!

passages.original: And long live you to think so!
passages.vernacular: 也願您永遠咁諗!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也願您永遠這樣想!

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: And yet, how nature erring from itself—
passages.vernacular: 然而,天性竟如何背離自身——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,天性竟如何背離自身——

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Ay, there’s the point.
passages.vernacular: 對,關鍵在呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,關鍵在這裡。

passages.original: As, to be bold with you, Not to affect many proposed matches, Of her own clime, complexion, and degree, Whereto we see in all things nature tends; Foh!
passages.vernacular: 比如,恕我大膽直講,佢唔喜歡許多提議嘅婚事,都係同佢自己氣候、膚色、身份嘅人,而我哋睇到喺一切事上天性都傾向呢個;呸!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 比如,恕我大膽直言,她不喜歡許多提議的婚事,都是同她自己氣候、膚色、身份的人,而我們看到在一切事上天性都傾向這個;呸!

passages.original: One may smell in such a will most rank, Foul disproportion, thoughts unnatural.
passages.vernacular: 喺咁樣嘅意願中可以聞到最惡臭嘅、骯髒嘅不相稱,違反自然嘅思想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這樣的意願中可以聞到最惡臭的、骯髒的不相稱,違反自然的思想。

passages.original: But pardon me: I do not in position Distinctly speak of her, though I may fear Her will, recoiling to her better judgement, May fall to match you with her country forms, And happily repent.
passages.vernacular: 但請原諒我:我並冇明確地針對佢講,雖然我可能擔心,佢嘅意願退回到更好嘅判斷時,會拎您與佢本國嘅形象比較,也許會後悔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但請原諒我:我並沒有明確地針對她說,雖然我可能擔心,她的意願退回到更好的判斷時,會拿您與她本國的形象比較,也許會後悔。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Farewell, farewell: If more thou dost perceive, let me know more;
passages.vernacular: 再見,再見:如果你察覺到更多,讓我知道;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見,再見:如果你察覺到更多,讓我知道;

passages.original: Set on thy wife to observe.
passages.vernacular: 叫你妻子去觀察。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叫你妻子去觀察。

passages.original: Leave me, Iago.
passages.vernacular: 離開我,伊阿古。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 離開我,伊阿古。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: [Going.]
My lord, I take my leave.
passages.vernacular: 大人,我告辭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,我告辭。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Why did I marry?
passages.vernacular: 我點解要結婚?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為什麼要結婚?

passages.original: This honest creature doubtless Sees and knows more, much more, than he unfolds.
passages.vernacular: 呢個誠實嘅人無疑睇到並知道得更多,多得多,比佢透露嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個誠實的人無疑看到並知道得更多,多得多,比他透露的。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: [Returning.]
passages.vernacular: [返回。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [返回。]

passages.original: My lord, I would I might entreat your honour To scan this thing no further.
passages.vernacular: 大人,我希望能懇求您唔好再深究呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,我希望能懇求您不要再深究這件事。

passages.original: Leave it to time: Though it be fit that Cassio have his place, For sure he fills it up with great ability, Yet if you please to hold him off awhile, You shall by that perceive him and his means.
passages.vernacular: 交畀時間:雖然凱西奧應該恢復職位,因為佢確實有出色能力勝任,但如果您願意讓佢暫時等一等,您就可以由此觀察佢同佢嘅手段。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 交給時間:雖然凱西奧應該恢復職位,因為他確實有出色能力勝任,但如果您願意讓他暫時等一等,您就可以由此觀察他和他的手段。

passages.original: Note if your lady strain his entertainment With any strong or vehement importunity, Much will be seen in that.
passages.vernacular: 留意您嘅夫人是否用任何強烈或猛烈嘅催促去促成佢嘅復職,從中可以睇出好多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 留意您的夫人是否用任何強烈或猛烈的催促去促成他的復職,從中可以看出很多。

passages.original: In the meantime, Let me be thought too busy in my fears (As worthy cause I have to fear I am) And hold her free, I do beseech your honour.
passages.vernacular: 與此同時,就當我嘅恐懼太多事吧(我確有正當理由擔心自己係咁),並請您認為佢係清白嘅,我懇求您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 與此同時,就當我的恐懼太多事吧(我確有正當理由擔心自己是這樣),並請您認為她是清白的,我懇求您。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Fear not my government.
passages.vernacular: 唔使擔心我嘅自制。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不用擔心我的自制。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: I once more take my leave.
passages.vernacular: 我再次告辭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我再次告辭。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: This fellow’s of exceeding honesty, And knows all qualities, with a learned spirit, Of human dealings.
passages.vernacular: 呢個傢伙極其誠實,以博學嘅心靈深知人際交往嘅一切品性。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這傢伙極其誠實,以博學的心靈深知人際交往的一切品性。

passages.original: If I do prove her haggard, Though that her jesses were my dear heartstrings, I’d whistle her off, and let her down the wind To prey at fortune.
passages.vernacular: 如果我證明佢係野性難馴嘅鷹,即使佢嘅腳帶係我心愛嘅心弦,我也要吹哨放走佢,讓佢順風去隨運氣獵食。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我證明她是野性難馴的鷹,即使她的腳帶是我心愛的心弦,我也要吹哨放走她,讓她順風去隨運氣獵食。

passages.original: Haply, for I am black, And have not those soft parts of conversation That chamberers have, or for I am declin’d Into the vale of years,—yet that’s not much— She’s gone, I am abus’d, and my relief Must be to loathe her.
passages.vernacular: 也許因為我黑,缺乏嗰啲閨房情郎所具有嘅柔和談吐,或者因為我已沉入暮年嘅山谷——不過呢個並唔算多——佢走喇,我受騙喇,我嘅解脫只能係厭惡佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許因為我黑,缺乏那些閨房情郎所具有的柔和談吐,或者因為我已沉入暮年的山谷——不過這並不算多——她走了,我受騙了,我的解脫只能是厭惡她。

passages.original: O curse of marriage, That we can call these delicate creatures ours, And not their appetites!
passages.vernacular: 啊,婚姻嘅詛咒,我哋可以稱呢啲嬌嫩嘅人為自己嘅,卻唔能稱佢哋嘅慾望為自己嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,婚姻的詛咒,我們可以稱這些嬌嫩的人為自己的,卻不能稱她們的慾望為自己的!

passages.original: I had rather be a toad, And live upon the vapour of a dungeon, Than keep a corner in the thing I love For others’ uses.
passages.vernacular: 我寧願做癩蛤蟆,靠地牢嘅蒸氣為生,也唔願在我所愛之物中留一角畀別人使用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧願做癩蛤蟆,靠地牢的蒸氣為生,也不願在我所愛之物中留一角給別人使用。

passages.original: Yet, ’tis the plague of great ones, Prerogativ’d are they less than the base, ’Tis destiny unshunnable, like death:
passages.vernacular: 然而,呢個係大人物嘅瘟疫,佢哋嘅特權還不如卑賤者,呢個係無法躲避嘅命運,如同死亡:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,這是大人物的瘟疫,他們的特權還不如卑賤者,這是無法躲避的命運,如同死亡:

passages.original: Even then this forked plague is fated to us When we do quicken.
passages.vernacular: 就在我哋出生時,呢個分叉嘅瘟疫就注定畀我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在我們出生時,這分叉的瘟疫就注定給我們。

passages.original: Desdemona comes.
passages.vernacular: 戴絲德夢娜來喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戴絲德夢娜來了。

passages.original: If she be false, O, then heaven mocks itself!
passages.vernacular: 如果佢不忠,啊,咁上天就係在嘲笑自己!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她不忠,啊,那麼上天就是在嘲笑自己!

passages.original: I’ll not believe’t.
passages.vernacular: 我唔相信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不相信。

passages.original: Enter Desdemona and Emilia.
passages.vernacular: [戴絲德夢娜同愛米利亞上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [戴絲德夢娜和愛米利亞上。]

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: How now, my dear Othello?
passages.vernacular: 點樣喇,我親愛嘅奧賽羅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,我親愛的奧賽羅?

passages.original: Your dinner, and the generous islanders By you invited, do attend your presence.
passages.vernacular: 您嘅午餐,仲有您邀請嘅高貴島民,都在等候您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您的午餐,還有您邀請的高貴島民,都在等候您。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: I am to blame.
passages.vernacular: 係我唔對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是我不對。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Why do you speak so faintly?
passages.vernacular: 你點解講嘢咁虛弱?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為何說話這麼虛弱?

passages.original: Are you not well?
passages.vernacular: 你唔舒服嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不舒服嗎?

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: I have a pain upon my forehead here.
passages.vernacular: 我呢度額頭痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我這裡額頭疼。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: Faith, that’s with watching, ’twill away again;
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,嗰係因為熬夜,會好嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,那是因為熬夜,會好的;

passages.original: Let me but bind it hard, within this hour It will be well.
passages.vernacular: 讓我用力把佢綁緊,一小時內就會好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我用力把它綁緊,一小時內就會好。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Your napkin is too little;
passages.vernacular: 你嘅手帕太細喇;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的手帕太小了;

passages.original: [He puts the handkerchief from him, and she drops it.]
passages.vernacular: [佢把手帕推開,手帕掉落。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [他把手帕推開,手帕掉落。]

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Let it alone.
passages.vernacular: 唔使理佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不用管它。

passages.original: Come, I’ll go in with you.
passages.vernacular: 來,我同你入去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,我和你進去。

passages.title: Desdemona 戴絲德夢娜
passages.original: I am very sorry that you are not well.
passages.vernacular: 你唔舒服,我好難過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不舒服,我很難過。

passages.original: [Exeunt Othello and Desdemona.]
passages.vernacular: [奧賽羅同戴絲德夢娜下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧賽羅和戴絲德夢娜下。]

passages.title: Emilia 愛米利亞
passages.original: I am glad I have found this napkin; This was her first remembrance from the Moor.
passages.vernacular: 我好高興搵到呢條手帕;呢個係摩爾人畀佢嘅第一份紀念物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興找到這條手帕;這是摩爾人給她的第一份紀念物。

passages.original: My wayward husband hath a hundred times Woo’d me to steal it.
passages.vernacular: 我嗰任性嘅丈夫已經一百次求我偷佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我那任性的丈夫已經一百次求我偷它。

passages.original: But she so loves the token, For he conjur’d her she should ever keep it, That she reserves it evermore about her To kiss and talk to.
passages.vernacular: 但佢太愛呢個信物,因為佢懇求佢永遠保留,所以佢始終帶喺身邊,親吻佢、對住佢講嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她太愛這信物,因為他懇求她永遠保留,所以她始終帶在身邊,親吻它、對著它說話。

passages.original: I’ll have the work ta’en out, And give’t Iago.
passages.vernacular: 我要把花樣描低,然後把佢畀伊阿古。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要把花樣描下來,然後把它給伊阿古。

passages.original: What he will do with it Heaven knows, not I, I nothing but to please his fantasy.
passages.vernacular: 佢拎佢做咩,只有上天知道,我唔知道,我只係順佢嘅心意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他拿它做什麼,只有上天知道,我不知道,我只是順他的心意。

passages.original: Enter Iago.
passages.vernacular: [伊阿古上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [伊阿古上。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: How now?
passages.vernacular: 點樣喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了?

passages.original: What do you here alone?
passages.vernacular: 你獨自喺度做咩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你獨自在這裡幹什麼?

passages.title: Emilia 愛米利亞
passages.original: Do not you chide.
passages.vernacular: 你別罵我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你別罵我。

passages.original: I have a thing for you.
passages.vernacular: 我有樣嘢畀你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有東西給你。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: A thing for me?
passages.vernacular: 畀我嘅嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我的東西?

passages.original: It is a common thing—
passages.vernacular: 嗰係件常見嘅嘢——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是件常見的東西——

passages.title: Emilia 愛米利亞
passages.original: Ha?
passages.vernacular: 哈?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: To have a foolish wife.
passages.vernacular: 就係有個傻老婆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是有個傻老婆。

passages.title: Emilia 愛米利亞
passages.original: O, is that all?
passages.vernacular: 啊,就係咁多嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,就這個嗎?

passages.original: What will you give me now For that same handkerchief?
passages.vernacular: 而家,你肯為嗰條手帕畀我咩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,你肯為那條手帕給我什麼?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: What handkerchief?
passages.vernacular: 咩手帕?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼手帕?

passages.title: Emilia 愛米利亞
passages.original: What handkerchief?
passages.vernacular: 咩手帕?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼手帕?

passages.original: Why, that the Moor first gave to Desdemona, That which so often you did bid me steal.
passages.vernacular: 咦,就係摩爾人最先送畀戴絲德夢娜嗰條,你常常叫我偷嗰條。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,就是摩爾人最先送給戴絲德夢娜的那條,你常常叫我偷的那條。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Hast stol’n it from her?
passages.vernacular: 你從佢嗰度偷嚟嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你從她那裡偷來的?

passages.title: Emilia 愛米利亞
passages.original: No, faith, she let it drop by negligence, And, to the advantage, I being here, took ’t up.
passages.vernacular: 唔,講真嘅,佢唔小心掉咗,我正好喺度,趁機撿起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,說真的,她不小心掉了,我正好在這裡,趁機撿起來。

passages.original: Look, here it is.
passages.vernacular: 睇,喺度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看,在這裡。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: A good wench, give it me.
passages.vernacular: 好姑娘,畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好姑娘,給我。

passages.title: Emilia 愛米利亞
passages.original: What will you do with’t, that you have been so earnest To have me filch it?
passages.vernacular: 你要拎佢做咩,竟然咁急住要我偷?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要拿它做什麼,竟然這麼急著要我偷?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: [Snatching it.]
passages.vernacular: [奪過。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奪過。]

passages.original: Why, what’s that to you?
passages.vernacular: 咦,呢個同你有咩關係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,這跟你有什麼關係?

passages.title: Emilia 愛米利亞
passages.original: If it be not for some purpose of import, Give ’t me again.
passages.vernacular: 如果唔係為咗咩重要嘅用途,把佢還畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果不是為了什麼重要的用途,把它還給我。

passages.original: Poor lady, she’ll run mad When she shall lack it.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅夫人,佢失去佢時會發瘋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的夫人,她失去它時會發瘋。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Be not acknown on’t, I have use for it.
passages.vernacular: 唔好承認知道呢件事,我有用處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要承認知道這事,我有用處。

passages.original: Go, leave me.
passages.vernacular: 去,離開我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,離開我。

passages.original: [Exit Emilia.]
passages.vernacular: [愛米利亞下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [愛米利亞下。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: I will in Cassio’s lodging lose this napkin, And let him find it.
passages.vernacular: 我要把呢條手帕丟喺凱西奧嘅住處,讓佢搵到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要把這條手帕丟在凱西奧的住處,讓他找到。

passages.original: Trifles light as air Are to the jealous confirmations strong As proofs of holy writ.
passages.vernacular: 輕如空氣嘅小事,對嫉妒嘅人來講,係同聖經嘅證據一樣有力嘅證實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 輕如空氣的小事,對嫉妒的人來說,是和聖經的證據一樣有力的證實。

passages.original: This may do something.
passages.vernacular: 呢個也許有用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這也許有用。

passages.original: The Moor already changes with my poison: Dangerous conceits are in their natures poisons, Which at the first are scarce found to distaste, But with a little act upon the blood Burn like the mines of sulphur.
passages.vernacular: 摩爾人已經喺我嘅毒藥下改變:危險嘅念頭本質就係毒藥,起初幾乎唔覺得難受,但稍微作用在血液上,就像硫磺礦一樣燃燒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 摩爾人已經在我的毒藥下改變:危險的念頭本質就是毒藥,起初幾乎不覺得難受,但稍微作用在血液上,就像硫磺礦一樣燃燒。

passages.original: I did say so.
passages.vernacular: 我早講過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我早說過。

passages.original: Enter Othello.
passages.vernacular: [奧賽羅上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奧賽羅上。]

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Look, where he comes.
passages.vernacular: 睇,佢來喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看,他來了。

passages.original: Not poppy, nor mandragora, Nor all the drowsy syrups of the world, Shall ever medicine thee to that sweet sleep Which thou ow’dst yesterday.
passages.vernacular: 無論罌粟、曼德拉草,還係世上所有催眠嘅糖漿,都唔能再令你得到你琴日仲擁有嘅嗰種甜美睡眠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論罌粟、曼德拉草,還是世上所有催眠的糖漿,都不能再使你得到你昨天還擁有的那種甜美睡眠。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Ha! ha!
passages.vernacular: 哈!哈!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈!哈!

passages.original: false to me?
passages.vernacular: 對我不忠?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對我不忠?

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Why, how now, general?
passages.vernacular: 咦,點樣喇,將軍?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 咦,怎麼了,將軍?

passages.original: No more of that.
passages.vernacular: 唔好再講嗰個喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別再說那個了。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Avaunt! be gone!
passages.vernacular: 走開!滾!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走開!滾!

passages.original: Thou hast set me on the rack.
passages.vernacular: 你把我放上咗刑架。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你把我放上了刑架。

passages.original: I swear ’tis better to be much abus’d Than but to know’t a little.
passages.vernacular: 我發誓,被騙得好厲害,也比稍微知道好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我發誓,被騙得很厲害,也比稍微知道好。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: How now, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 點樣喇,大人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,大人?

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: What sense had I of her stol’n hours of lust?
passages.vernacular: 我對佢偷來嘅情慾時光有咩感覺?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對她偷來的情慾時光有什麼感覺?

passages.original: I saw’t not, thought it not, it harm’d not me.
passages.vernacular: 我冇見,冇諗到,佢冇傷害我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒看見,沒想到,它沒傷害我。

passages.original: I slept the next night well, was free and merry;
passages.vernacular: 第二日夜裡我瞓得好好,自由快樂;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天夜裡我睡得很好,自由快樂;

passages.original: I found not Cassio’s kisses on her lips.
passages.vernacular: 我冇喺佢嘴唇上發現凱西奧嘅吻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒在她嘴唇上發現凱西奧的吻。

passages.original: He that is robb’d, not wanting what is stol’n, Let him not know’t, and he’s not robb’d at all.
passages.vernacular: 被盜嘅人,若不缺少被偷走嘅嘢,只要佢唔知道,佢就根本冇被盜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被盜的人,若不缺少被偷走的東西,只要他不知道,他就根本沒被盜。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: I am sorry to hear this.
passages.vernacular: 聽到呢個我好難過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽到這個我很難過。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: I had been happy if the general camp, Pioners and all, had tasted her sweet body, So I had nothing known.
passages.vernacular: 如果整個軍營,連工兵在內,都嘗過佢甜美嘅身體,只要我咩都唔知道,我就會幸福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果整個軍營,連工兵在內,都嘗過她甜美的身體,只要我什麼都不知道,我就會幸福。

passages.original: O, now, for ever Farewell the tranquil mind!
passages.vernacular: 啊,從而家起,永別喇,平靜嘅心!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,從現在起,永別了,平靜的心!

passages.original: Farewell content!
passages.vernacular: 永別喇,滿足!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 永別了,滿足!

passages.original: Farewell the plumed troops and the big wars That make ambition virtue!
passages.vernacular: 永別喇,插羽嘅軍隊同令野心成為美德嘅大戰!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 永別了,插羽的軍隊和使野心成為美德的大戰!

passages.original: O, farewell, Farewell the neighing steed and the shrill trump, The spirit-stirring drum, the ear-piercing fife, The royal banner, and all quality, Pride, pomp, and circumstance of glorious war!
passages.vernacular: 啊,永別喇,永別喇,嘶鳴嘅戰馬、尖銳嘅號角、激勵心靈嘅戰鼓、刺耳嘅短笛、皇家旗幟,以及輝煌戰爭嘅一切品質、驕傲、儀仗同氣派!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,永別了,永別了,嘶鳴的戰馬、尖銳的號角、激勵心靈的戰鼓、刺耳的短笛、皇家旗幟,以及輝煌戰爭的一切品質、驕傲、儀仗與氣派!

passages.original: And, O you mortal engines, whose rude throats The immortal Jove’s dread clamours counterfeit, Farewell!
passages.vernacular: 還有你哋,致命嘅大炮,你哋粗野嘅喉嚨模仿永生朱庇特可怕嘅雷鳴,永別喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有你們,致命的大炮,你們粗野的喉嚨模仿永生朱庇特可怕的雷鳴,永別了!

passages.original: Othello’s occupation’s gone!
passages.vernacular: 奧賽羅嘅職業完喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奧賽羅的職業完了!

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Is’t possible, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 有可能嗎,大人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有可能嗎,大人?

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Villain, be sure thou prove my love a whore; Be sure of it.
passages.vernacular: 惡棍,你一定要證明我愛嘅人係個娼婦;一定要確定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 惡棍,你一定要證明我愛的人是個娼婦;一定要確定。

passages.original: Give me the ocular proof, Or, by the worth of man’s eternal soul, Thou hadst been better have been born a dog Than answer my wak’d wrath.
passages.vernacular: 畀我親眼所見嘅證據,否則,憑人類永恆靈魂嘅價值,你寧願生為一條狗,也唔好面對我被喚醒嘅怒火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我親眼所見的證據,否則,憑人類永恆靈魂的價值,你寧願生為一條狗,也不要面對我被喚醒的怒火。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: Is’t come to this?
passages.vernacular: 到咁地步了嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到這地步了嗎?

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Make me to see’t, or at the least so prove it, That the probation bear no hinge nor loop To hang a doubt on, or woe upon thy life!
passages.vernacular: 令我睇見,或者至少證明得令證據冇任何鉸鏈或環扣可以掛上疑問,否則你嘅性命有禍喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我看見,或者至少證明得讓證據沒有任何鉸鏈或環扣可以掛上疑問,否則你的性命有禍了!

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: My noble lord,—
passages.vernacular: 我高貴嘅大人——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我高貴的大人——

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: If thou dost slander her and torture me, Never pray more.
passages.vernacular: 如果你誹謗佢並折磨我,就唔好再祈禱喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你誹謗她並折磨我,就別再祈禱了。

passages.original: Abandon all remorse; On horror’s head horrors accumulate;
passages.vernacular: 拋棄一切悔意;在恐怖之上堆積恐怖;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拋棄一切悔意;在恐怖之上堆積恐怖;

passages.original: Do deeds to make heaven weep, all earth amaz’d;
passages.vernacular: 做出令天堂哭泣、全地驚駭嘅事;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 做出令天堂哭泣、全地驚駭的事;

passages.original: For nothing canst thou to damnation add Greater than that.
passages.vernacular: 因為你再也冇比呢個更大嘅事可添加到你嘅詛咒之上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為你再也沒有比這更大的事可添加到你的詛咒之上。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: O grace!
passages.vernacular: 啊,恩典!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,恩典!

passages.original: O heaven defend me!
passages.vernacular: 啊,上天保佑我!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,上天保佑我!

passages.original: Are you a man?
passages.vernacular: 你係人嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是人嗎?

passages.original: Have you a soul or sense?
passages.vernacular: 你有靈魂或感覺嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你有靈魂或感覺嗎?

passages.original: God be wi’ you.
passages.vernacular: 願上帝與您同在。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願上帝與您同在。

passages.original: Take mine office.—O wretched fool, That liv’st to make thine honesty a vice!
passages.vernacular: 收回我嘅職位。——啊,可憐嘅傻瓜,你活著竟令自己嘅誠實成為罪惡!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 收回我的職位。——啊,可憐的傻瓜,你活著竟使自己的誠實成為罪惡!

passages.original: O monstrous world!
passages.vernacular: 啊,荒唐嘅世界!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,荒唐的世界!

passages.original: Take note, take note, O world, To be direct and honest is not safe.
passages.vernacular: 留意,留意,世界啊,直率誠實並唔安全。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 留意,留意,世界啊,直率誠實並不安全。

passages.original: I thank you for this profit, and from hence I’ll love no friend, sith love breeds such offence.
passages.vernacular: 我感謝您畀我呢個教訓,從此我唔再愛任何朋友,因為愛會招來咁嘅冒犯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我感謝您給我這個教訓,從此我不再愛任何朋友,因為愛會招來這種冒犯。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: Nay, stay.
passages.vernacular: 唔,留低。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,留下。

passages.original: Thou shouldst be honest.
passages.vernacular: 你應該係誠實嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你應該是誠實的。

passages.title: Iago 伊阿古
passages.original: I should be wise; for honesty’s a fool, And loses that it works for.
passages.vernacular: 我應該聰明;因為誠實係傻瓜,會失去自己努力爭取嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我應該聰明;因為誠實是傻瓜,會失去自己努力爭取的東西。

passages.title: Othello 奧賽羅
passages.original: By the world, I think my wife be honest, and think she is not.
passages.vernacular: 憑世界起誓,我認為我妻子貞潔,又認為佢唔貞潔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑世界起誓,我認為我妻子貞潔,又認為她不貞潔。

passages.original: I think that thou art just, and think thou art not.
